The nested raymarch distance is clamped via lerp keyed on _AdditionalLightsPosition[i].w, with 1.0 for point/spot lights and 0.0 for directional lights. originals.title: AudioSource Pooling and Recycling with Deferred Completion
originals.body:
To pool AudioSources, maintain separate free and busy lists; reclaim busy AudioSources by polling `isPlaying` in `Update()` or reverse-iterating the busy list upon removal, as described in `Recipes/monobehaviours/audiosource-pool-late-removal.md`. For single-clip intro+loop music, use one `AudioClip` containing both sections; disable looping (`loop = false`) and seek `audioSource.time` to the loop start time using a coroutine that checks per frame when the cursor passes the loop end time, avoiding gaps and latency compared to `Play()`, detailed in `Recipes/monobehaviours/single-clip-intro-loop-audiosource-time-seek.md`.  When deferring pool recycling until animated components complete, use `PoolableDecorator` components that self-report readiness via a `CanBeReturnedToPool()` method; the parent object aggregates these decorators and gates pool return only when all report true, as outlined in `Recipes/performance/defer-pool-recycle-until-animated-components-complete.md`. originals.title: Music Layer State Transitions, Beat Quantization, and Timestamp Throttling
originals.body:
To implement hysteresis state transitions for music layers (RCP-monobehaviours-002), enter the combat state when a count reaches or exceeds a threshold and exit when the count is zero; timestamp gating should be used to control intro layer duration. Music transitions should be beat-quantized by computing time-to-next-beat/bar using `AudioSource.time % boundary` (RCP-monobehaviours-068), yielding that duration in a coroutine before crossfading, eliminating jarring mid-beat transitions. Event playback can be staggered with timestamp throttling (RCP-dots-ecs-017) by storing a last-played timestamp on the audio singleton and gating playback based on whether the current time exceeds it; advance the threshold by `Random.Range` jitter to desynchronize bursts. Smooth volume changes should utilize `Mathf.MoveTowards` per frame. These recipes originate from lands-of-old-runtime, Synaptic AI Pro, and are located in files: `Recipes/monobehaviours/hysteresis-bgm-state-machine.md`, `Recipes/monobehaviours/beat-quantised-music-transition-bar-boundary.md`, and `Recipes/dots-ecs/timestamp-jitter-audio-throttle.md` respectively, all within the repository at `C:	ran_Unity

title: Root Cause Analysis: Cluster Creation Failures
body: Initial logs suggested VRAM issues, hallucinations, truncation errors, or escapes as potential causes for cluster creation failures (5 clusters created, 0 successful) within 80-second timing chunks; full diagnostic output including JSON.parse errors and byte-level analysis revealed the true root cause. title: Balance Flow to Demand, Not Capacity
body: Optimize dependent systems by scheduling the bottleneck resource's production rate to match market demand, reduced for a safety margin; synchronize non-bottleneck resources accordingly, contradicting capacity balancing. Reserve upstream capacity to buffer dependent operations and absorb statistical fluctuations—full utilization propagates delays. This opposes cost-minimization (maximizing utilization, load balancing) as per Jonah’s principle 'balance flow, not capacity'. The contradiction between systems-thinking and local optimization explains conventional practice's failure in dependent systems; standard manufacturing prioritizes per-unit cost minimization over system performance.

originals.title: Balance flow to demand, not capacity to demand
originals.body: Schedule the bottleneck resource to produce at the rate of market demand (slightly below to provide safety margin), then synchronize all non-bottleneck resources to feed that bottleneck at that rate. This directly contradicts traditional capacity-balancing practice but is necessary in dependent systems; attempting to keep all resources at full utilization ensures delays propagate with no buffer.

originals.title: Reserve capacity necessary to buffer dependent operations
originals.body: Because dependent events cascade delays and statistical fluctuations are inevitable, resources upstream of a bottleneck need reserve capacity to absorb variation without starving the bottleneck. The traditional practice of balancing all resources to full utilization guarantees that delays propagate downstream with no buffering mechanism.

This contradiction is not accidental but essential to the insight's power—it makes the principle memorable and explains why conventional practice fails in dependent systems. The tension between systems-thinking and local-optimization logic is core to understanding why TOC is counterintuitive.

title: Resource Throttling Strategy
body: Throttle resource-intensive operations to accommodate varied user hardware; conservative throttling (throttling too much) is preferable to optimistic throttling (not throttling enough). This approach accounts for the fact that end users generally have less powerful machines than developers. The rationale is to ensure a consistent and acceptable experience across diverse system capabilities.

title: Organizational Inertia & Strategic Goal Alignment
body: Successful strategies create inertia due to leader protection of established processes, creating vulnerability to market changes. Strategies fail with unstated evaluation criteria; reference defined strategic goals (revenue/profit) and the core strategic question. Lack of clarity leads to incremental optimization, misdiagnosed as capability deficits. Define long-term ideal states, near-term ideal states, and the core strategic question before evaluating ideas to promote agility. Leaders must distinguish productive activities from those that appear so by ensuring organizational objectives are clearly defined and aligned; manufacturing organizations exemplify this with a single articulated goal. Failing companies lack explicit goal alignment or allow local optimization without shared strategic direction, leading to fragmentation.

originals.title: Successful strategies create organizational inertia
originals.body: Once a company optimizes its entire organization around a successful strategy (like Interruption Marketing), changing that strategy becomes organizationally difficult. Second and third-generation leaders resist disrupting what already works, making companies vulnerable to market shifts but stable in execution.

originals.title: Strategic Goal Clarity & Alignment
originals.body: Strategies fail due to unstated evaluation criteria; always reference the defined strategic goal (e.g., revenue, profit) and compare ideas against the core strategic question. Rigid teleological planning hinders adaptation and reduces agility; explicitly define the long-term ideal state, near-term ideal state, and core strategic question before evaluating ideas. Leaders cannot distinguish between productive activities and those that merely appear so when organizational objectives are undefined. Technically competent managers optimizing inherited metrics can simultaneously drive organizational failure because questioning fundamental goals feels like questioning competence. Manufacturing organizations align around ONE clearly-articulated goal; failing companies lack explicit goal alignment or allow local optimization without shared strategic direction, leading to fragmentation and dysfunction.

title: Synthesis vs. Fabrication in Encyclopedia Entries
body: Acceptable synthesis applies frameworks from source material to examples, accurately sourced; fabrication introduces invented concrete details without explicit sourcing. Interpretive synthesis, reframing or derivation grounded in sources, is permissible as illustration or interpretation, not attributed directly to the source text. The distinction avoids creating unsupported specific details or numbers. Synthesis connects existing concepts; fabrication presents new claims as facts without backing. This convention applies specifically to encyclopedia entries.

title: Overhead Allocation & Misaligned Metrics
body: Department-level overhead allocation using square footage or resource metrics can misdirect management and obscure true operational performance. Standard accounting methods based on historical costs can misrepresent improvements; for example, showing rising costs despite doubled throughput. Prioritize system throughput goals over cost minimization when evaluating practices like batch size optimization and inventory valuation. Easy-to-measure metrics—code commits, hours worked, early arrival, cost per part, equipment utilization, labor ratios—often measure activity or local efficiency rather than overall company success; optimizing for low unit cost in a Purchasing department can lead to accumulated unused inventory if the objective isn't questioned. Official reporting systems tracking resource efficiency may mask financial losses and missed deadlines by obscuring system-level performance. Measurability doesn’t guarantee accuracy or meaningfulness.

title: Business Operations Encyclopedia Entry Guidelines

originals.title: Business Strategy & Operations Encyclopedia Entry Scope
originals.body: B&O scope requires domain and substance threshold filters; business context alone is insufficient. Narrative content in business organizations may belong elsewhere. title: Cosmetic Variant Design & Abstract Row Models

body: The `category_correct` field is evaluated independently of faithfulness, depth, and fabrication scores; an entry can have high quality metrics but still be incorrectly categorized due to imperfect category alignment. title: Coroutine Management Conventions and UI Population Strategy
body: When stopping a coroutine started by name, always use the string-name overload of `StopCoroutine` to avoid invisible, duplicate instances causing issues like double event firing; mixing overloads results in both old and new instances running concurrently. To prevent concurrent corruption when populating a UI list, implement a persistent `while(true)` coroutine gated by a boolean flag, where setting the flag initiates teardown and rebuild operations, and subsequent requests while building maintain the flag to avoid cancellation. This strategy originates from the FileDialogExplorerPlugin and is documented in `Recipes/ui-ux/infinite-coroutine-ui-population-state-machine.md`.

originals.title: Seamless Perimeter Wall UV Tiling and Adaptive Window Count
originals.body:
To achieve seamless perimeter wall UV tiling, the terminal U coordinate (`uEnd`) from each quad is carried forward to the next segment, ensuring a continuous texture strip when unrolled; this `u = uEnd` approach maps U to physical distance multiplied by `uvScale`, as implemented in `BuildingBuilder`.  Window count per segment is derived from global facade spacing and capped with a physical overlap floor, preventing shape-specific adjustments. This adaptive scaling maintains visual rhythm across buildings of varying L/T/H shapes; the origin for this approach is also `BuildingBuilder`. The relevant file paths are `Recipes/shaders/how-do-we-uv-map-tiled-wall-textures-along-a.md` and `Recipes/performance/how-do-we-distribute-a-consistent-number-of.md`, located within the repository at `C:	ran_Unity
ity-workflow-optimization`. The technique addresses both UV tiling seams and window distribution consistency.

originals.title: Procedural Generation and Editor Workflow Recipes
originals.body: Deterministic prefab variation selection uses `Random.CreateFromIndex((uint)segmentIndex)` seeded from the segment index to tie variations to geometry position, as documented in `Recipes/monobehaviours/segment-index-deterministic-variation-seed.md`. Procedural material coherence selects a `MaterialPalette` SO via weighted random selection and populates all slots from within it (file: `Recipes/serialization/how-do-we-ensure-procedurally-generated-buildings.md`). Random patrol reselection prevents revisiting the previous waypoint by incrementing the index with +1 % count if the same index is selected, inspired by Behavior Designer Movement and detailed in `Recipes/monobehaviours/random-patrol-reselection-guard.md`. Mesh LOD management avoids material array mismatches by iterating fixed slots and building materials in lockstep (file: `Recipes/performance/how-do-we-build-a-mesh-with-a-variable-number-of.md`), while programmatic `LODGroup` construction uses `SetLODs` and `RecalculateBounds`, destroying the group with `DestroyImmediate` in the editor to prevent warnings. Texture drawers use typed `ObjectField` checking `prop.textureDimension` (file: `Recipes/editor/texture-drawer-typed-object-field.md`), and `Texture2D` instances are cached using a dictionary with `HideFlags.DontSave` (`Recipes/editor/struct-keyed-texture-cache-hideflags-dontsave.md`). Asset duplication uses `Duplicate<T>()` for complex assets like materials, avoiding hand-authoring YAML (e.g., glow1_ADD.mat), and redundant materials are deduplicated before asset creation using a shader.name + colorKey dictionary (`Recipes/editor/how-do-we-avoid-generating-dozens-of-redundant.md`). Asset baking uses `Undo.DestroyObjectImmediate` for scene instances and `DeleteAsset` for tracked paths, deleting companion folders only if `FindAssets` returns zero (file: `Recipes/editor/how-do-we-implement-undo-last-bake-for-a-tool.md`), while safe asset overwrites check existence with `AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath` before creating new assets (`Recipes/editor/how-do-we-safely-overwrite-a-previously-baked.md`). To prevent memory leaks, ghost ScriptableObject instances have hideFlags set to `HideFlags.HideAndDontSave`, and are cleaned up using `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll` with `DestroyImmediate`. Animator state names are resolved to AnimationIndex and ExitTime during editor bake via case-insensitive matching (`Recipes/animation/editor-bake-animator-state-name-to-index.md`), local waypoints are converted to world space in Start using `TransformPoint` (`Recipes/monobehaviours/local-to-world-waypoints-start.md`), and NavMesh agent type IDs and area masks are resolved from authored strings via OrdinalIgnoreCase comparison (`Recipes/dots-ecs/navmesh-agent-type-area-mask-baker-lookup.md`).

title: Angle Containment and Clamping Conventions
body: When clamping `localEulerAngles`, use separate upper and lower band checks to avoid incorrect snapping due to the representation of -90° as 270°; for example, `Mathf.Clamp(-90, 90)` on 270° incorrectly resolves to 90°. To correctly contain angles with wraparound (0°/360°), normalize them to the range [0, 360) and invert the gap check when a > b, as naive >= and <= comparisons fail for arcs crossing 0°. This approach handles cases where the angle wraps around the 0/360 degree boundary.

title: Line of Sight, Ground Detection, Projectile Placement & Physics
body: Line of sight uses `Physics.Linecast`; missing hits may indicate a lack of colliders or CharacterController usage. Traverse transform hierarchies to handle compound GameObjects by comparing ancestors against the target's root. Prevent self-collisions during LOS raycasts by temporarily setting agent child collider GameObjects to layer 2 (Ignore Raycast) and restoring them using a cached `int[]` array (Recipes/monobehaviours/linecast-colliderless-target-los.md, Recipes/monobehaviours/contains-transform-compound-linecast-hit.md, Recipes/monobehaviours/self-collider-layer-swap-sight-raycast.md). Ground detection uses a two-pass raycast: first against all layers (~0), then re-validate the hit object's layer against a behavior-owned LayerMask (Knowledge/physics/re-validate-a-hit-objects-layer-against-a.md). Velocity-predicted ground seeking (RCP-physics-025) calculates ray origin as position + decidedDir × speed × predictionTime, offsetting Y downwards if distance to ground is less than innerRadius, using a proxy GameObject target for physics decoupling (Recipes/physics/velocity-predicted-ground-seek.md). Projectile placement validation uses a static helper with an early-return chain (afford → collision → entity overlap → module rules) and cached layer masks computed via `LayerMask.GetMask` (RCP-monobehaviours-042). Snapping state machines use a single `IsSnapped` flag for spline, node, and building targets (RCP-monobehaviours-053).

originals.title: Projectile Placement, Physics, and Pooling Patterns
originals.body: Placement validation uses a static helper with an early-return chain (afford → collision → entity overlap → module rules) and cached layer masks computed via `LayerMask.GetMask` (RCP-monobehaviours-042). Snap source/target entity IDs bypass collision rejection (RCP-physics-003). A generic snapping state machine for multi-target placement, parameterized by entity/graph type, uses a single `IsSnapped` flag representing spline, node, and building targets (RCP-monobehaviours-053), with each `Update*` method clearing irrelevant fields. The `Physics2DOverlapCompat` snippet (Snippets/monobehaviours/Physics2DOverlapCompat.cs) shims `Physics2D.OverlapCircle`. `PreallocNonAllocQueries` (Snippets/performance/PreallocNonAllocQueries.cs) preallocates a static `Collider[]` buffer to avoid heap allocation during physics queries (BP-performance-007). Unity's symmetric filter rule for broadphase pair generation and distance calculations is (a.BelongsTo & b.CollidesWith) != 0 && (b.BelongsTo & a.CollidesWith) != 0, with `CollidesWith` set to 0 disabling all distance queries. Projectile Factory projectiles require custom `ProjectileBehavior` ScriptableObjects adhering to six pool-safety rules detailed in `Recipes/monobehaviours/pf-custom-behavior-pool-safety-rules.md`. Hold-to-fire continuous patterns utilize `SpawnBehavior.repeatCount=-1`, `multiShotBehavior=StopActiveShot`, and `canStopMidSpawning=true` to prevent stacked streams, with `SpawnProjectile` called on button-down and `StopProjectile` on button-up. Repositioning pooled GameObjects containing ParticleSystems involves deactivating them with `SetActive(false)`, adjusting position/rotation, then reactivating with `SetActive(true)`.

originals.title: Line of Sight and Ground Detection Raycasting Techniques
originals.body: When using Physics.Linecast for line of sight, a missing hit may indicate the target lacks a Collider or uses a CharacterController; to handle compound GameObjects with child colliders, walk up the transform hierarchy comparing ancestors against the target's root. To prevent self-collisions from blocking sight during LOS raycasts, temporarily set agent child collider GameObjects to layer 2 (Ignore Raycast) and restore them using a cached int[] array, as detailed in Recipes/monobehaviours/linecast-colliderless-target-los.md, Recipes/monobehaviours/contains-transform-compound-linecast-hit.md, and Recipes/monobehaviours/self-collider-layer-swap-sight-raycast.md (C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization). For accurate ground detection, use a two-pass raycast: first against all layers (~0) to identify obstacles, then check if the initial hit belongs to the ground layer, re-validating the hit object's layer against a behavior-owned gameplay LayerMask (Knowledge/physics/re-validate-a-hit-objects-layer-against-a.md). Velocity-predicted ground seeking (RCP-physics-025) calculates the ray origin as position + decidedDir × speed × predictionTime, offsetting the Y coordinate downwards if the distance to the ground is less than the innerRadius; a proxy GameObject target decouples physics queries from steering (Recipes/physics/velocity-predicted-ground-seek.md, C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization).

title: Non-Destructive State Suppression and Restoration Recipe
body: Temporarily suppress resources by backing up original values into a dictionary keyed by resource ID, restoring them afterward and clearing the backup; nested suppression is guarded by restoring values before each new suppress call. Within ICommandLogic, use OnRestore, OnPreview, Execute, and OnCancel lifecycle methods to manage state changes independently, incorporating dirty checks to avoid redundant restore-suppress cycles. Restore operations must precede subsequent suppress calls to prevent nested suppression value loss. Null-guard all manager accesses. Implement terrain heightmap previews non-destructively using CommittedData, PreviewData, and an IsDirty flag per tile; OnPreview writes to PreviewData, OnRestore copies CommittedData back, Execute promotes PreviewData to CommittedData, and the dirty flag limits processing to modified tiles.

originals.title: Unity GameObject Destruction, Scene Access, and Safe Object Handling
originals.body: Unity destroys child GameObjects before parent cleanup, potentially losing pooled resources; sibling `OnDestroy()` calls are non-deterministic, requiring explicit disposal order within a parent's `Dispose()` method (e.g., Player.OnDispose() → CharacterController.Dispose() → SpeedModel.Dispose()) to avoid races and ensure deterministic dependency cleanup. Accessing scene information from GameObjects marked with `DontDestroyOnLoad` requires a temporary GameObject also marked `DontDestroyOnLoad`, wrapped in a try/finally block, only valid when `EditorApplication.isPlaying` is true; enumerating root GameObjects within `DontDestroyOnLoad` scenes involves creating a temporary `DontDestroyOnLoad` GameObject and using `GetRootGameObjects()` on the resulting Scene struct (Recipes/editor/how-do-you-enumerate-all-root-gameobjects-in.md, C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization). The `SafeDestroy` helper uses `Destroy` in play mode and `DestroyImmediate` in edit mode to handle object destruction across both contexts. When releasing procedural meshes/materials from editor preview objects, use `EditorUtility.IsPersistent` to determine if an object is saved; call `DestroyImmediate` only on shared mesh/material entries when `IsPersistent` returns false before destroying the GameObject itself (Recipes/editor/how-do-we-release-procedurally-generated-meshes.md).

originals.title: Scene Instance, Prefab Handling, State Restoration & Cleanup
originals.body: Distinguish scene instances from prefab references by checking `scene.IsValid()` and `scene.isLoaded()`, forcing cloning with `HideAndDontSave` if either fails; use `EditorUtility.IsPersistent(obj)` to differentiate assets from scene-only objects, combined with type checks for `IsSceneObject`. Restore the prefab stage context after bulk scene operations using reflection: `PrefabStageUtility.OpenPrefab(string, GameObject)`, falling back to the single-argument overload if necessary, originating from the AssetUsageDetector and initially from RuntimePreviewGenerator. Scene loading uses `LoadSceneAsync(Single)` while overlays require `Destroy()` and `UnloadUnusedAssets()`, with `ObjectPreview.Cleanup()` (Unity 2021.1+, RCP-editor, Voxel Labs Ultimate Preview) releasing preview resources; otherwise, expose and call `Dispose()` from `EditorWindow.OnDestroy()`, overriding `ObjectPreview.Cleanup()` requiring a call to `base.Cleanup()` then `Dispose()`. Mutable scene state modified during play mode is saved in `Awake` under `#if UNITY_EDITOR`, applied as a play-mode override, and restored in `OnDestroy` using double `#if` guards, originating from `lands-of-old-runtime`. Per-scene editor state is persisted within a ScriptableObject dictionary keyed by scene GUID, utilizing `LoadAssetAtPath || CreateAsset`, with time-based garbage collection for recently unopened scenes. The ScriptableObject is lazily created at a known asset path and flushed to disk on domain reload, originating from CoInspector; relevant files are `Recipes/monobehaviours/editor-play-mode-state-restoration.md` and `Recipes/editor/scriptableobject-session-state-scene-guid-key.md`, both in repository `C:an_Unityity-workflow-optimization`.

title: Design Gate Process and Exceptions
body: The Design Gate is mandatory before any implementation, requiring written design approval; exceptions exist for pure questions, read-only analysis, code review, single-file reads/greps without output, and trivial changes which require fast design. The process involves context exploration, requirement clarification, research, proposing 2-3 approaches, a written design, flag doc refresh, and handoff to write-plan; documentation updates are required post-implementation. Users can waive the gate only after being notified of its necessity and explicitly confirming the waiver. Skipping the gate is allowed for pure questions, read-only analysis, code review, single-file reads/greps without output. Config changes still require design approval.

originals.title: Design Gate — mandatory before implementation
originals.body: HARD-GATE rule: never code without explicit written design approval. Process: context exploration → clarify requirements → research → propose 2-3 approaches → written design → flag doc refresh → hand off to write-plan. Only exceptions: pure read-only requests. User may waive after explicit notification gate is required. Documentation update required as final step after implementation.

originals.body: Skip gate: pure questions, read-only analysis, code review, single-file read/grep without output. Do NOT skip: config changes (still need design), trivial changes (design fast anyway), ambiguous approval (confirm explicitly). User can waive gate only after being told it's required and explicitly confirming waiver.

title: Prerequisite Graph Storage Strategy

originals.title: Tool Landscape Survey (March 2026)
originals.body:
- **GitNexus** — Tree-sitter AST + KuzuDB graph, 12 langs, MCP tools, community/process detection. L1/L3 foundation.
- **Codebase Memory MCP** (DeusData) — Similar concept, Go binary, 64 langs, 99.2% token reduction. No LLM enrichment, no execution flows.
- **Code-Graph-RAG** (Memgraph) — Tree-sitter + Memgraph, MCP tools. Requires Memgraph infra, no incremental update.
- **Brokk** — Joern Code Property Graphs (control flow + data flow). JVM-focused, no MCP.
- **Augment Context Engine MCP** — Commercial, millisecond sync, 30-80% quality improvement. Cloud-only.
- **Cursor** — Merkle tree + embeddings in Turbopuffer. Tied to Cursor IDE. No graph analysis.
- **Continue.dev** — Embeddings + Tree-sitter + ripgrep. Retrieval accuracy issues.
- **Aider RepoMap** — Tree-sitter + PageRank. Regenerated from scratch, no persistence.
- **Memory-MCP** — Tier 1 (CLAUDE.md) + Tier 2 (.memory/state.json). Confidence decay model.
- **Letta Code** — Git-backed memory. General agent memory.
- **Drift MCP** — "Cortex" living memory for tribal knowledge. 50+ tools. Pattern/decision persistence.
1. **L2 with self-validation** — No tool generates LLM summaries with validation questions re-checkable for drift.
2. **Semantic drift detection** — File-hash staleness is the current signal. Validation questions are not re-run.
3. **Hierarchical compression with confidence** — No L1->L2->L3->L4 progressive detail with per-layer confidence.
4. **Persistent evolving code knowledge** — Existing graphs are rebuilt or session-scoped.
- "Reliable Graph-RAG for Codebases" (arXiv Jan 2026): AST-derived graphs beat LLM-extracted on reliability/speed.
- A-MEM (NeurIPS 2025): Zettelkasten for general LLM memory — validates atomic-notes-with-links concept.
- CoVe (ACL 2024): Self-validation works, verification must be independent from original generation.
- Self-correction research: Naive "review your answer" decreases accuracy. Targeted questions are correct approach.
- LogicLens (arXiv Jan 2026): Hybrid AST + LLM enrichment for code graphs (research only).

originals.title: LLM Knowledge Base Project - Consolidated Memory
originals.body: The LLM Knowledge Base project builds a persistent code knowledge system ("LLM Zettelkasten") as an overlay (Approach B) on GitNexus, which provides L1 (AST structural facts) and L3 (feature maps, call chains, communities). Our system adds L2 (LLM summaries with confidence) and L4 (method prose + self-validation questions), stored in a SQLite database with FTS5 for indexing. MCP servers run simultaneously; agents query GitNexus for structure and our system for summaries/confidence, supporting multi-branch content-addressable entries keyed by `gitnexus_id` and blob hash (from `git ls-tree`), enabling 99%+ reuse across branches. GitNexus’s `.gitnexus/kuzu` is copied per branch due to its lack of branch awareness; the test repository is `C:   estepo`. GitNexus provides L1 structural facts (node types like Class, Function, Method with properties and relationships) for 12 languages including TypeScript and Python, along with L3 feature maps using the Leiden algorithm and BM25 hybrid search. Missing from GitNexus are file-level content hashes, method signatures with types, and external system call tagging; our system fills these gaps by generating L2 class abstracts and L4 method prose with self-validation questions, employing a three-pass validation process where Pass 2 does not see the original code. Progressive disclosure serves L2 summaries (150-250 tokens) by default, escalating to L4 detail on demand (`expand=true`), and employs cache-friendly response design sorted by file path. The safe context zone is 5K-30K tokens; beyond that accuracy degrades. Validation questions are stored in FTS5 as a semantic search index, categorized by type (behavioral, dependency, edge case) with edge cases weighted higher for confidence scoring and drift detection uses file hash changes to trigger question re-checking before re-summarization.

title: Git Repository Recovery and Refetching
body: Interrupted `git fetch` operations can corrupt the local object store, rendering `git gc --aggressive` and `git prune` ineffective. `git fetch --refetch origin` resolves 'pack has N unresolved deltas' or 'invalid index-pack output' errors, bypassing corruption when thin packs cannot resolve due to missing blob objects; `git --refetch` (Git 2.42+) forces a full refetch without local delta bases. Repeated identical unresolved delta counts indicate structural issues diagnosable with `git fsck`; transient errors are cosmetic noise from flaky network conditions affecting post-fetch garbage collection. Recover corrupted repositories by cloning fresh copies and swapping `.git` directories, avoiding Syncthing syncing of `.git`. Resolve interrupted fetches or repack operations by removing temporary files (`tmp_pack_*`) and orphaned `.idx/.rev` files in the `.git` directory, then running `git fetch origin`, or recreating the `.git/shallow` marker if `git fetch --unshallow` fails. Shallow Git clones (--depth) are unsuitable for production; incrementally deepen history using `git fetch --depth=N origin`.

originals.title: git --refetch recovers from missing delta base objects
originals.body: Git 2.42+ `git --refetch` forces full refetch without relying on local objects as delta bases. Use when delta resolution fails due to missing blobs; bypasses corruption in repos where thin packs cannot resolve.

originals.title: Git Repository Recovery and Transient Errors
originals.body: Interrupted `git fetch` operations can corrupt the local object store, requiring a fresh clone from the remote repository; attempts to repair this with `git gc --aggressive` and `git prune` are ineffective.  'pack has N unresolved deltas' or 'invalid index-pack output' errors during `git fetch` are resolved by running `git fetch --refetch origin`. Transient errors causing different missing commit hashes, while presenting a healthy HEAD/working tree, are cosmetic noise from flaky network conditions affecting post-fetch garbage collection. Repeated identical unresolved delta counts indicate structural issues: missing local blob objects preventing thin pack delta resolution, diagnosable with `git fsck` showing broken links. Recover corrupted repositories by cloning fresh copies and swapping `.git` directories to avoid Unity Library/Temp/ reimports; avoid Syncthing syncing of `.git`, preferring `git push` and `git pull`. Resolve interrupted fetches or repack operations by manually removing temporary files (`tmp_pack_*`) and orphaned `.idx/.rev` files in the `.git` directory, followed by `git fetch origin`; detect these with `git fsck` and `git count-objects -v`. If `git fetch --unshallow` fails or incomplete remote-tracking refs exist, recreate the `.git/shallow` marker at the last good commit or use `git update-ref refs/remotes/origin/<branch> <commit>`, verifying with `git status`. Shallow Git clones (--depth) are unsuitable for production due to failures in `git blame`, `bisect`, `rebase`, and `merge-base`; incrementally deepen history using `git fetch --depth=N origin`. Use `git ls-remote --heads origin` to view remote branch lists without a full fetch, or `git fetch --depth 1 origin <branch>` for minimal transfer size over unreliable networks.

title: Framework Best Practices vs. Plugin-Specific Recipes
body: Patterns in plugins like vInspector and vHierarchy (reflection FieldInfo caching with null sentinel, rounded-rect IMGUI drawing using a 9-slice GUIStyle) necessitate framework-level Best Practices (BPs), not plugin-specific recipes; semantic search detected duplication. `unity-knowledge/extract-knowledge` mines reusable patterns from Unity asset folders (.cs, .shader, .hlsl, .compute, .asmdef files in batches of ≤20) using parallel agents with a quality bar and writes findings as best-practices (with citation URL), recipes flagged for compile-check, and project-notes to Documents/. Integration with `io.continis.hats` yielded 19 BPs (18 editor domain, 1 serialization), 1 Snippet (`ProjectWindowIconVsListViewDetect`), and 16 Recipes within the editor domain, expanding the knowledge base to 313 BPs across 14 domains; two snippet candidates were downgraded to recipes. Recipe extraction requires a single invocation of `add_recipes.py` to avoid classifier timeouts, as demonstrated during vInspector extraction where 7 recipes were successfully added via batch processing. Prior to writing any extracted recipe, semantic deduplication against the Recipes/ folder is essential; for example, two duplicates of vHierarchy recipes (reflection walk caching, rounded rect drawing) were skipped during vInspector extraction. All writes include Nexus pointers.

title: Locked Card Mechanics and Level-Proximity Approach
body: The locked card system uses a level-proximity approach, moving cards closer to the player based on their level via `OnLevelChanged` callbacks and proximity calculations, configurable with `approachWindowLevels` and `approachSlideDurationSeconds`. Cards are despawned while open (`despawnEligibility`) to prevent refreshes. Idle float tweens pause on tap to avoid `CardFlipPresenter` conflicts. Dismissal triggers `RefreshAsync` for empty states if no active events remain, skipping reveal for expired/unlocked cards; expired card farewells use `PlayBurnCard(InOutCubic)+EventRevealAnimator` signaled by `OpenAnimationComplete`. Closing actions include `counter-burn+slot-promotion`, `DiscardPendingUnlock()` on all opens, and `RelocalizeOpen`. The system uses `cardBackGUID: 828e20f2e2a62cd4db67c481657110e5`, displays cards using `LockedCardView` if locked, otherwise `EventCatalog.Visible`, and unlocks with an entrance tween + `NewlyUnlocked(level, level+1)` at flip-start.

title: Unity Memory: Color Serialization, Float Handling, and Null Safety
body: Color32 values are serialized as `r | (g<<8) | (b<<16) | (a<<24)` and unpacked with byte shifting; SafeBit helper functions (`Set`, `Clear`, `Toggle`, `Write`, `HasFlag`) manage typed bitfields [0, 31]. Color conversions to hex strings use `ColorUtility.TryParseHtmlString` with a `#` prefix guard. Structured console commands append `PREFIX:{JSON}` or `CPAPI:{}`. Linear projects utilize the [Gamma] attribute for gamma-to-linear color property conversion and the [IntRange] attribute for Range property inspector slider snapping to integer steps. Unity 6000.2+ code branches between `prop.propertyFlags` (ShaderPropertyFlags) and `prop.flags` (MaterialProperty.PropFlags) for handling the [HideInInspector] flag; shader features combine optional flags into a single material parameter as a Vector4. Nullable float3 fields are used in `IComponentData` singletons (`Snippets/dots-ecs/NullableFloat3Singleton.cs`) to represent optional per-frame positional events, requiring `.Value` unwrapping. Floating-point precision noise is mitigated by comparing `Mathf.Abs(delta) > epsilon`. Zero-allocation float/double to byte conversion uses the `FloatBytesUnion` struct (`Snippets/serialization/FloatBytesUnion.cs`) and `BigEndianReader` (`Snippets/serialization/BigEndianReader.cs`). C# nullable reference warnings are resolved with `System.Array.Empty<T>()`, `null!` for required references, and `T?` with null guards; explicit `!= null` checks or a Select(params T[]) helper function address incorrect handling of UnityEngine.Object subclasses by the `??` operator; serializing generic key-value pairs involving Unity Objects requires boxing value types to an object and using Unity's overloaded `==` operator.

title: Quantum Service Lifecycle Resume Race & GameplayController Crash Root Cause
body: Crash analysis indicates a median gap of ~4 seconds and a maximum of ~69 seconds between last activity and crash, consistently occurring in processState: BACKGROUND; this suggests a race condition, not user-idle behavior. The Quantum Service Lifecycle resume race involves OnApplicationPause(false) fast-forwarding the simulation, triggering multiple OnPlayerDeath events and racing with EnemyTrainCarsPool re-registration or Party Mode teardown. iOS crashes show ~100% BACKGROUND while Android shows 94% FOREGROUND; service locator exceptions primarily affect iOS (<1%). Crashes in processState:BACKGROUND (resume/backgrounding) have distinct root causes compared to processState:FOREGROUND (active-streaming races). IL2CPP symbol stripping on iOS has minimal impact (~0.1%, ~600 crashes). A PR targeting HomeController:OnPlayClicked and <StartGame>d__53:MoveNext resolves 86/495 (~17%) of BACKGROUND state crashes, demonstrating backgrounding is required; always verify crash context when auditing fix impact.

ServiceNotFound crashes occur at a 97.8% incidence rate during the BACKGROUND state (484/495) and 2.2% (11/495) in FOREGROUND, exacerbated by iOS's slower cold-start time (Metal shader compilation and lack of Mono fallback), involving async-continuation races with `UniTask.WaitUntil` chains and CachedService lookups after app backgrounding, and a quantum-event-driven foreground race tied to match timing. title: Zone Pairing and Retry Strategy Optimization
body: Long-arc retries (attempt2/attempt3) generate candidate zones spanning 130-207 points, compared to attempt1's 20-40, requiring unconditional application of the Difference trim across all attempts; `AnchorReconnectThresholdSq` in CutOtherZonesSystem was increased from 0.5 to 2.0 units to prevent anchor drift and defaults player variant selection to FIXED (variant=1) due to the high cost of joint evaluation (JOINT_BIG/JOINT_SMALL), which requires approximately 4x more union calls than independent per-side selection, with non-local players defaulting to FIXED; zone candidate pairings now use a `realGainPairing` strategy prioritizing LeftClockwise+RightCounterClockwise pairings deterministically, correcting the previous 'shorter arc' heuristic documented in ticket 5492 and employing a three-tier fallback: primary, targeted cross-retry (altLeft+chosenRight, then chosenLeft+altRight), and legacy 4-way. Lazy building of long arc candidates (`longLeft`, `longRight`) in retry attempts 2-4 avoids build cost when the first attempt succeeds, and retries are used 0–3 times per hundreds of real closures; the loop closure gain metric was changed from `Union(ZonePoints, candidate) - oldSurface` to `Difference(candidate, ZonePoints)` to resolve false negatives. Playtest data indicates approximately 3–5% (or ~3–5 of 119–120 closures) trigger retries, resulting in a maximum of 4–6 Clipper2 operations and short-arc-first + a 4-tier retry chain resolves ~97-100% of real loop closures on the first attempt with 0-5% needing retries.

originals.title: Retry Chain Optimization and Loop Closure Gain Metric
originals.body: Lazy building of long arc candidates (`longLeft`, `longRight`) in retry attempts 2-4 avoids build cost when the first attempt succeeds, enabling a low-risk fallback without performance penalty; this is crucial because retry attempts are used 0–3 times per hundreds of real closures and zero times across a 92-fixture corpus. The loop closure gain metric was changed from `Union(ZonePoints, candidate) - oldSurface` to `Difference(candidate, ZonePoints)` to resolve false negatives, allowing fixtures (`InsufficientGainAfterMerge_07`, `_12`) to pass on the first attempt; these are real production repros. Playtest data indicates approximately 3–5% (or ~3–5 of 119–120 closures) trigger retries, resulting in a maximum of 4–6 Clipper2 operations isolated to incorrect initial calculations and not impacting happy path latency.  Empirically validated playtesting shows that short-arc-first + a 4-tier retry chain resolves ~97-100% of real loop closures on the first attempt with 0-5% needing retries, all 'all-4-failed' cases confirmed as genuine non-closures via oracle validation. The strategy justifies the complexity of the 4-tier retry chain.

title: Procedural Mesh Cleanup, Blend Shape Handling, and Geometric Integrity Checks

title: HDRP Workflow Optimization & Cosmetic Fog Migration
body: For HDRP temporal effects using CustomPasses, allocate two RTHandles in `Setup()`, render to a temporary RTHandle in `Execute()`, composite with history via material, copy back into the history RTHandle using `Graphics.CopyTexture`, and release in `Cleanup()` (Recipes/vfx/hdrp-custompass-rthandle-temporal-buffering.md, C: ran_Unityity-workflow-optimization); dynamic shadow distance adjustment based on camera zoom involves caching `HDShadowSettings`, clamping zoom to [0, 1], linearly interpolating between minimum and maximum distances (Recipes/vfx/hdrp-shadow-distance-camera-zoom.md, C: ran_Unityity-workflow-optimization). To tile a LineRenderer beam texture consistently, scale `sharedMaterial.mainTextureScale.x` by distance/textureLengthScale and advance `mainTextureOffset.x` by `deltaTime*speed`, avoiding heap allocation (Recipes/vfx/linerenderer-beam-distance-tiled-uv-sharedmaterial.md). Fake shadows in editor previews utilize a float4x4 matrix named `_ShadowTextureMatrix` passed via `Material.SetMatrix` for shadow texture UVs, encoding an orthoProjection multiplied by a worldToLight transformation (Recipes/shaders/how-do-you-project-a-pre-baked-or-dynamically.md). Temporary material overrides capture `sharedMaterials` into list-of-lists in `CaptureRenderers`, replace slots with override materials in `ApplyOverride`, and restore originals via sentinel check in `RestoreOriginals` (Recipes/editor/how-do-you-temporarily-replace-all.md), always using `sharedMaterials`. The Lands of Old project (HDRP version 17.3.0, Assets/_Project/Lands of Old/Config/HDRP/HDRP.asset) will migrate its forest fog system from discrete LocalVolumetricFog volumes to a single HDRP-native window with a world-XZ density mask (R=forest persistent, G=atmospheric falloff based on camera distance, building footprints stamp 0), leveraging an existing EditTools/CommandBuffer lifecycle similar to UpdateTreeFog and using a Mirza AERO raymarched fullscreen pass driven by the mask RenderTexture calculating density as `density = R*forestParams + G*atmosphericParams*approachFalloff(camDist)`, incorporating HDRP Fog volume override for global haze; shader graph alpha output controls voxel density via connection to the Fragment Alpha block in the Master Stack, requiring a scene Volume with Fog override (enableVolumetricFog=true) and HDRP frame settings Volumetrics enabled, using `SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_LOD(...,0)` when sampling world-space noise. A Test-Driven Development plan (14 tasks, .flow/tdd/hdrp-fog-migration-20260703-2050/) is prepared but not implemented, starting with task-001 to validate moving LocalVolumetricFog with a Material maskMode and Fog Volume ShaderGraph.

title: File System and Temporary File Handling Best Practices
body: Visual Studio rename operations use temporary files with an `OldName` suffix, requiring debouncing to prevent double-processing; rapid-fire events are deduplicated by scanning for entries with the same path within a 500ms window. When `FileSystemEventArgs.FullPath` is missing, recover incorrect Unity paths using `Directory.GetFiles(Application.dataPath, fileName, AllDirectories)` due to an editor bug. Use `File.GetAttributes(path) & FileAttributes.Directory` after confirming path existence to distinguish files from directories. Wrap `Directory.GetDirectories()` in a bare `try/catch` block to handle `UnauthorizedAccessException`, `IOException`, and reparse loops. Sanitize filenames using `Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars` before file I/O to prevent directory traversal attacks and extension overwrites, validating lexical and canonical forms for symlink escapes. Set `FileInfo.IsReadOnly = true` after writing temporary editor files, resetting it to `false` before cleanup. Reading `EditorPrefs` or `SessionState` requires a `[InitializeOnLoad]` static constructor or `[InitializeOnLoadMethod]`. Diagnosing Harmony patching crashes involves persisting the fully-qualified method name to `EditorPrefs` or a temporary file pre-write and deleting post-success. Sanitize product names for filesystem invalid characters when constructing file paths.

originals.title: File and Directory Handling, Sanitization, and Temporary File Management
originals.body: To reliably distinguish files from directories, use `File.GetAttributes(path) & FileAttributes.Directory` after confirming path existence to avoid `FileNotFoundException`, as `Directory.Exists` is false for files and `File.Exists` is false for directories; during directory enumeration, wrap `Directory.GetDirectories()` in a bare `try/catch` block to silently skip inaccessible folders handling `UnauthorizedAccessException`, `IOException`, and reparse loops. Prior to file I/O operations, sanitize save filenames using `Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars` to prevent directory traversal attacks (e.g., '../../config') and accidental extension overwrites before path construction, validating both the lexical and canonical forms for symlink escapes. Set `FileInfo.IsReadOnly = true` after writing temporary editor files to prevent `UnauthorizedAccessException` during deletion, resetting it to `false` before cleanup; reading `EditorPrefs` or `SessionState` requires a `[InitializeOnLoad]` static constructor or `[InitializeOnLoadMethod]`. To diagnose Harmony patching crashes, persist the fully-qualified method name to `EditorPrefs` before applying each detour and clear it upon success, or append it to a persistent temporary file pre-write and delete post-success (file existence indicates the crashing method). Sanitize the product name for filesystem invalid characters when constructing file paths. These conventions originate from FileDialogExplorerPlugin and are documented in Recipes/monobehaviours/fileattributes-bitflag-directory-file-check.md (RCP-monobehaviours-144), Recipes/monobehaviours/try-catch-permission-gate-directory-scan.md (RCP-monobehaviours-145), Recipes/editor/how-do-we-safely-read-editorprefs-and.md, Recipes/editor/how-do-we-identify-which-method-detour-caused-an.md.

title: Shader Optimization and Rendering Techniques
body: Amortize trigonometric costs for cubemap rotation using Rodrigues formula `(yAxis + xzPlane*cos + cross(Y_UP,xzPlane)*sin)` in the vertex shader (Recipes/shaders/cubemap-rotation-rodrigues-vertex.md); avoid per-fragment calculations. Correct vertical stretch for orthographic cameras by multiplying vertex Y with `lerp(1.0, unity_OrthoParams.y/unity_OrthoParams.x, unity_OrthoParams.w)` (Recipes/shaders/cubemap-ortho-y-scale-correction.md). Geometry shader vertex alpha stores spike height; derive a robust tangent frame and cull zero-weight spikes via early exit (Recipes/shaders/geometry-shader-vertex-alpha-extrude.md). Reduce GPU register pressure by declaring non-positional CBUFFER uniforms as half precision (Recipes/shaders/half-precision-cbuffer-non-positional.md) and suppressing the _ST uniform for textures without UV tiling using [NoScaleOffset] (Recipes/shaders/no-scale-offset-suppress-st-uniform.md). Pack two normalized floats into a single float with quantization: qx=floor(x*2047), qy=floor(y*2047), packed=qx*2048+qy, and unpack using fmod/floor for approximately 0.05% precision (Recipes/shaders/float-packing-two-vector-2047-quantise.md). Map world positions to texture coordinates for per-frame GPU visibility queries using a singleton cache of bounds; compute a row-major flat index into a readback byte array within the `IsVisible` function (Recipes/gpu/world-pos-to-texture-coord-bounds-cache.md); map world positions to tiles in O(1) time by dividing by a uniform tile size, casting XZ components to an `int2`, and using it as a key for a `Dictionary<int2, Tile>` (Recipes/performance/position-to-key-tile-dictionary-lookup.md). Cache per-frame global shader constants from a managed `GameComponent` by caching property IDs as static readonly int fields via `Shader.PropertyToID`, injecting singletons, and calling `Shader.SetGlobal*` once per parameter in the `Tick()` method (Recipes/vfx/global-shader-params-gamecomponent-tick.md). Declare a `[HideInInspector] Vector _Tex_HDR` alongside each CUBE texture to correctly decode HDR cubemaps; Unity writes decoding instructions during import which should be passed to the `DecodeHDR(sample, _Tex_HDR)` function before tinting or exposure multiplication (Recipes/shaders/cubemap-tex-hdr-decode-instructions.md). Multiply the final skybox color by `unity_ColorSpaceDouble` (2.0 in Linear space) following HDR decoding, tinting, and exposure (Recipes/shaders/unity-color-space-double-output.md). Compute luminance using BT.601 weights: 0.299r + 0.587g + 0.114b for perceptually accurate color saturation; lerp each channel towards this value (Recipes/shaders/cubemap-blend-decode-before-lerp.md). Multiply UV coordinates by `_ScaledScreenParams.xy` in fullscreen dithering/blue noise shaders to prevent tiling (Recipes/shaders/my-blue-noise-interleaved-gradient-dithering.md); use `Graphics.Blit` with bilinear filtering to downscale oversized 2x/4x textures when RenderTexture MSAA is unavailable (Recipes/editor/how-do-you-generate-anti-aliased-thumbnails-via.md).

For orthographic cameras, multiply vertex Y by `lerp(1.0, unity_OrthoParams.y/unity_OrthoParams.x, unity_OrthoParams.w)` to correct vertical stretch, as detailed in Recipes/shaders/cubemap-ortho-y-scale-correction.md; this avoids branching. For per-frame GPU visibility queries, map world positions to texture coordinates using a singleton cache of bounds and compute a row-major flat index into a readback byte array (Recipes/gpu/world-pos-to-texture-coord-bounds-cache.md) within the `IsVisible` function. Map world positions to tiles in O(1) time by dividing by a uniform tile size, casting XZ components to an `int2`, and using it as a key for a `Dictionary<int2, Tile>` (Recipes/performance/position-to-key-tile-dictionary-lookup.md), utilizing the `MakeKey` helper function. Per-frame global shader constants are driven from a managed `GameComponent` by caching property IDs as static readonly int fields via `Shader.PropertyToID`, injecting singletons, and calling `Shader.SetGlobal*` once per parameter in the `Tick()` method (Recipes/vfx/global-shader-params-gamecomponent-tick.md). Declare zero-cost Float properties as `uniform half` in HLSL to suppress compiler warnings and act as anchors for custom drawer UI elements like [StyledCategory], [StyledBanner], or [StyledMessage(Info, text, condProp, expectedValue, top, bottom)], requiring the BOXOPHOBIC StyledMessage drawer. originals.title: HDR Cubemap Decoding, Color Saturation, and URP Sprite Rendering
originals.body: To correctly decode HDR cubemaps, declare a `[HideInInspector] Vector _Tex_HDR` alongside each CUBE texture in the shader; Unity writes decoding instructions during import which should be passed to the `DecodeHDR(sample, _Tex_HDR)` function before tinting or exposure multiplication. When blending HDR cubemaps, decode them separately before lerping to avoid incorrect luminance, ensuring each has its own `_HDR` decode vector. Following HDR decoding, tinting, and exposure, multiply the final skybox color by `unity_ColorSpaceDouble`, which is 2.0 in Linear space and approximately 4.59 in Gamma space for correct output regardless of project color space; this process applies to shaders defined within files such as `Recipes/shaders/cubemap-tex-hdr-decode-instructions.md`, `Recipes/shaders/cubemap-blend-decode-before-lerp.md`, and `Recipes/shaders/unity-color-space-double-output.md`. For perceptually accurate color saturation, compute luminance using BT.601 weights: 0.299r + 0.587g + 0.114b, then lerp each channel towards this value instead of (r+g+b)/3. Transparent preview thumbnails with minimal memory usage should branch on backgroundColor.a < 1f: use `ClearFlags.Depth + GL.Clear(true, true, bg)` for transparency and `ClearFlags.Color` for opacity, selecting `TextureFormat.RGBA32` versus `RGB24`, then apply changes using `Apply(false, markNonReadable=true)`. A render scale of 0.8 causes soft UI; use 1.0 unless GPU fill-bound testing indicates otherwise. Fullscreen dithering/blue noise shaders should multiply UV coordinates by `_ScaledScreenParams.xy` to prevent tiling, as demonstrated in `Recipes/shaders/my-blue-noise-interleaved-gradient-dithering.md`. MSAA anti-aliases polygon edges and alpha-to-coverage but not blended sprite interiors; configure Camera AA to None or SMAA (avoid FXAA) and enable Camera Dithering. When RenderTexture MSAA is unavailable, `Graphics.Blit` downscales oversized 2x/4x textures with bilinear filtering for additional anti-aliasing—see `RuntimePreviewGenerator` in `Recipes/editor/how-do-you-generate-anti-aliased-thumbnails-via.md`. title: Web Retrieval Search Fallback Chain Architecture
body: The `web_retrieval` system uses an API-based search fallback chain prioritizing Tavily, Exa, Google Custom Search, and Brave Search API to avoid bot-blocking; scrapers like SearXNG are avoided. The retrieval process utilizes native WebSearch/WebFetch tools with ToolSearch(query: "select:WebSearch,WebFetch") for deferred schema loading.  The `web_retrieval.retrieve` CLI tool is installed via `pip install -e` and invoked as `python -m web_retrieval.retrieve`. The CLI accepts `--url [--force-js]` or `--query [--max-results N]` arguments, outputs JSON on success (exit code 0), and enables hook fallthrough with exit code 1; pre-tool hooks avoid Crawl4AI, SearXNG, and Firecrawl ($83+/mo). The `web-retrieval` Docker Compose setup includes SearXNG (localhost:8080) and Crawl4AI (localhost:11235), with Crawl4AI requiring 2vCPU/4GB and SearXNG slated for removal (ADR-014). Credentials are managed in `search.py`, necessitating manual image enumeration via `docker-compose config --images` for drift detection.

originals.body: web_retrieval implements a fallback chain: Tavily (primary), Exa, Google CSE, Brave Search API; balancing capability with quota management. Tavily is primary but expensive to conserve. The ordered chain replaces SearXNG and prioritizes providers sequentially, handling HTTP 429/402 errors and network failures by falling through, raising a SearchError only on complete failure. Web access utilizes native WebSearch/WebFetch tools with ToolSearch(query: "select:WebSearch,WebFetch") for deferred schema loading. The `web_retrieval.retrieve` CLI tool (installed globally via `pip install -e`, accessible with `python -m web_retrieval.retrieve`) handles retrieval using `detect_vertical()`, `fetch_vertical()`, `fetch()`, and `search()`. It accepts `--url [--force-js]` or `--query [--max-results N]` arguments, exits 0 for success (JSON stdout), and 1 to enable hook fallthrough. PreToolUse hooks intercept calls, avoiding Crawl4AI, SearXNG, Firecrawl ($83+/mo). The `web-retrieval` Docker Compose setup includes SearXNG (localhost:8080) and Crawl4AI (localhost:11235), Crawl4AI requiring 2vCPU/4GB; SearXNG removal is planned (ADR-014). Tavily extract skills overlap with Crawl4AI, but consume API quota while Crawl4AI is self-hosted. `search.py` imports credentials and requires manual image enumeration with `docker-compose config --images` for drift detection.

title: URP Volume Stack Optimization and DramaEventPunch Cost
body: DramaEventPunch volume weight is 0 except during the punch event, costing only during its brief flare (intensity 55, iteration count 8). Steady-state bloom cost comprises SceneProfile and DramaAmbient; the punch is not an optimization target. URP blends active Volumes into a single interpolated stack with negligible CPU overhead for parameter blending; GPU cost equals one volume with blended final bloom values. The scene utilizes unlit SpriteRenderers, no scene lights, a panning camera, and full-res HDR bloom dominates mobile GPU cost. SceneProfile (15/3-iter), DramaAmbient (42/6-iter), and DramaEventPunch (55/8-iter re-roll every 0.7s) are managed by PostFxDramaController.cs (DramaAmbient for vignettes/bloom, EventPunchVolume for flares/dirt). Optimize bloom performance via: maxIterations ≤4 + intensities ~10–15 total + downscale:1 + disable highQualityFiltering; drop MSAA to 1; bake additive glow quads to static sprites with capped maxParticles; and disable HDR once LDR. Volume.weight animation must remain runtime-only, mutating only runtime instances like `volume.profile` (not sharedProfile) validated via `git status` on `.asset` files after instantiate/play/exit. SceneProfile is configured with Bloom enabled, Tonemapping Neutral, subtle Vignette, and no Motion Blur; add `Unity.RenderPipelines.Universal.Runtime` to the `.asmdef` for Bloom and `Unity.RenderPipelines.Core.Runtime` for Volume types.

originals.title: DramaEventPunch not steady-state cost
originals.body: DramaEventPunch volume weight is 0 except during the punch event, so its high intensity (55) and iteration count (8) only cost during the brief flare, not continuously. Steady-state bloom cost is SceneProfile (always on) + DramaAmbient (continuously breathing). The punch is not an optimization target.

originals.title: URP Volume Stack Optimization & Asset-Immutable Configuration
originals.body: URP blends active Volumes into a single interpolated stack (GPU cost equals one volume with blended final bloom values: iterations × intensity × resolution). CPU overhead for parameter blending is negligible. The scene uses unlit SpriteRenderers, no scene lights, and a panning camera; mobile GPU cost is dominated by full-res HDR bloom. SceneProfile (15/3-iter), DramaAmbient (42/6-iter), DramaEventPunch (55/8-iter re-roll every 0.7s) are managed by PostFxDramaController.cs (DramaAmbient for vignettes/bloom, EventPunchVolume for flares/dirt). Optimize bloom performance via: (1) maxIterations ≤4 + intensities ~10–15 total + downscale:1 + disable highQualityFiltering; (2) drop MSAA to 1; (3) bake additive glow quads to static sprites with capped maxParticles; (4) disable HDR once LDR. Avoid tuning intensity due to near-free composite multiply cost. EventPunchVolume weight was stranded at peak (pooled DOTween sequence); UpdateEventPunch now recomputes weight every frame via DOVirtual.EasedValue, enabling consolidation from three volumes to one/two by folding SceneProfile's base bloom into DramaAmbient (weight 1). Maintain asset immutability by mutating only runtime instances like `volume.profile` (not sharedProfile), validated via `git status` on `.asset` files after instantiate/play/exit. Volume.weight animation must remain runtime-only to prevent asset corruption. Configure SceneProfile (enable Bloom, Tonemapping Neutral, subtle Vignette, no Motion Blur) while keeping DefaultVolumeProfile at URP template defaults (19 post-processing components); use Unity Inspector exclusively for serialized assets; avoid manual YAML edits of `.unity` scene files. Add `Unity.RenderPipelines.Universal.Runtime` to `.asmdef` for Bloom and `Unity.RenderPipelines.Core.Runtime` for Volume types; variant collections must preserve URP and built-in pipeline shaders (Bloom, FXAA, SSAO, Lit, UI/Default). SceneBackground prefab (~30 SpriteRenderers + quad mesh) uses shared materials and is excluded from static batching audits; animated effects on a dedicated effects sub-Canvas (separate from main UI Canvas per DDR-001) prevent tween updates from invalidating static batches; ambient breathe effect reclaims CPU when post-FX panel hidden.

title: Newtonsoft.Json Requirement for Addressables and Voodoo Magic DTOs
body: Addressables 2.x no longer includes Newtonsoft.Json as a transitive dependency, requiring explicit addition via com.unity.nuget.newtonsoft-json to ensure AOT safety; previously, Addressables 1.x included it transitively. Newtonsoft.Json is used for Voodoo Magic Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) serialization because Unity's JsonUtility cannot serialize Dictionary<string,int> (clicks) or HashSet<string> (dismissed) fields natively, avoiding surrogate DTO layers and mapping shims as per project guidelines. Desktop targets (Windows/macOS) remove AOT/IL2CPP concerns that might otherwise favor JsonUtility; Unity's built-in JsonUtility’s limitations are fundamental.

title: Local Embeddings for Baseline Recall Validation & Routing Pre-filter
body: MXBAI embeddings (local) compute baseline-recall, validate topic reduction during grouping, acting as a gating check before Opus judge validation. Semantic embeddings cannot replace LLM-based encyclopedia routing due to category overlap (e.g., personal-development, psychology, career). An embedding-only approach would triple extraction fan-out, violating cost reduction goals. The architecture uses MXBAI embeddings to narrow 21 encyclopedias to ~10 candidates via local cosine similarity (97% recall), then a cheaper LLM router selects from those candidates. Recall@10 is 97%, but precision@5 is 0.4, demonstrating the limitation of embedding-only routing. This two-stage approach separates routing (local and near-free) from extraction.

An embedding-only approach would triple extraction fan-out, breaking cost reduction goals. The system uses a two-stage architecture: mxbai embeddings narrow 21 encyclopedias to ~10 candidates (97% recall) via local cosine similarity with zero LLM cost, then a cheaper LLM router selects from these 10, reducing input size and routing call cost without quality loss. This cleanly separates routing (local, near-free) from extraction (requires generation and model selection), enabling different optimization targets per stage.

title: Batch Processing Failure at Batch 17 & Recovery Procedures
body: Book processing batch jobs consistently fail at batch 17 due to authentication/rate-limiting issues. The `pipeline-result.json` file tracks categorization results (`ok`, `failed`, `missing`), and automatic re-runs are preferred over manual recovery, aligning with individual book processing routines. Batch parallelism allows for 23+ concurrent per-book pipelines, managed by the `fork_analyze` architecture which handles batches of 8–28, resuming from the flow cache after crashes (N+1 resumption following completion of batches 1–N) with a ~95% cache hit rate. The `--skip-existing` flag preserves successful batches and retries failed ones (`rl=0`, `0 topics`). Cached artifacts can mask orchestration failures; throttling options are 1 or 8, but may trigger loops requiring cache collapse. Manifest regeneration occurs only when necessary, and checkpointing strategies for large books include partial `analyze`, remaining-item counts, and pending `finalize` to prevent blocking smaller book rendering.

title: Rendering Configuration and Mobile Performance Constraints
body: Rendering settings are centralized in ADR-042 within architecture.md; the project uses Universal Render Pipeline with Render Graph (Compatibility Mode off), enforcing an all-unlit constraint, necessitating separate Mobile_RPAsset / PC_RPAsset assets per quality level. HDR is enabled pending bloom-threshold retune due to HDR-bloom coupling; disabling HDR clamps the color buffer to [0,1], eliminating bloom and degrading visuals. Bloom cost includes pass iterations, resolution, and filtering; HDR format (R11G11B10 float) does not significantly impact bandwidth compared to LDR RGBA8, while FP16 would double it. Mobile_RPAsset has m_SupportsHDR=1 and m_MSAA=2; HDR roughly doubles framebuffer bandwidth on tile GPUs when bloom thresholds > 1.0 (currently 1.2, 1.15), requiring optimization sequence: (1) Remove MSAA immediately, (2) Adjust bloom thresholds ≤ 1.0, (3) Disable HDR.

body: Use `ExecutionDataflowBlockOptions.CancellationToken` for coordinated dataflow mesh cancellation; use `CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource()` to manage concurrent cancellation. Parallel operations require cancellation support, and methods with `IProgress<T>` should offer best-effort cancellation via `CancellationToken`. `CancellationToken` requires explicit cooperation (checks or `cancellationToken.Register()`); prefer System.Reactive subscription/disposal at Rx boundaries. Asynchronous disposal necessitates a private `CancellationTokenSource` in `Dispose()`; always dispose of returned `CancellationTokenRegistration` using `using` or `IDisposable` to prevent leaks; registration cleanup must occur on completion and cancellation paths. Cancelable elements are async stream enumerators, requiring `WithCancellation()` for cancellation during enumeration.

originals.body: CancellationToken requires explicit cooperation via checks within methods; non-compliant code needs `cancellationToken.Register()` for APIs lacking native support. body: The `add_proposal` script's `--update` mode uses `args.<field>` for record construction, requiring wiring of new updatable fields in create and update code paths to prevent silent drops; updates should use `/update-tooling-reference`. title: Fixture Variant Edge Extraction & Zone Merge Optimization - Loop Closure
body: Raw edge data is recovered from fixture variants (CW vs CCW) using `ExtractEdge` with zero extraction failures when trailing geometry matches, computing the longest common suffix of zone-arc prefixes and appending an identical edge. Zone merging directly merges raw candidates utilizing `ZonePoints` entries as boundary points, bypassing Clipper2 seam recomputation and avoiding winding direction issues in `Clipper2.UnionNonAlloc`, requiring a fallback due to failure on fixture `AsymmetricOrientation_01`. Loop closure gain is calculated via `Difference(candidate, ZonePoints)`, using raw and trimmed buffers for merge welding, gain-gating, animation sizing (`CheckPlayersToKillInArea`), arc overlap guarantee, and prioritizing short-arc selection (17 points vs 803) in a retry chain. Option D (single-union loop closure), documented in `option-d-single-union-loop-closure-investigation.md`, was rejected due to negative pass rate results and potential failure with multi-lobe shapes; the recommended primary heuristic is LeftClockwise+RightCounterClockwise (zero comparison cost vs `SelectByShorterArc`). Option C (Union followed by Difference) exhibits cost equivalence (2 operations per attempt) and maintains a 4-tier attempt chain validated across 24 fixtures. Dropped pieces are classified as `NewCandidateArtifact`, `DistantZoneLobe`, or BoundaryStraddling, often caused by self-intersecting `mergeSourcePoints` confirmed across over 10 fixtures with `zoneSelfPieceCount=1`.

originals.title: Loop Closure Optimization and Rejection of Single-Union Approach
originals.body: The single-union loop closure approach (Option D), documented in option-d-single-union-loop-closure-investigation.md, was rejected due to negative pass rate results and a risk: multi-lobe shapes using the LargestArea clipper strategy may fail or produce incorrect results, requiring validation against all 24 test fixtures; this design remains unchanged. Empirical testing of eight test fixtures (0/8) showed same-handedness is not required for loop closure, allowing removal of those checks. Per-side heuristics (PreferBigger, PreferSmaller, PreferShorterArc) exhibit inverse failure patterns across fixture subsets AsymmetricOrientation_01 and 06–11 due to global interaction. The recommended primary heuristic is LeftClockwise+RightCounterClockwise, offering zero comparison cost versus SelectByShorterArc; existing 3-combo and legacy 4-way chain heuristics remain as fallbacks against Clipper2 winding regressions. Diagnostic types capture operands (Zone + zoneCreatedPoints), arc buffers pool-returned by detection time, closure failures requiring all four arcs, and shape count; fixture design emphasizes granular per-piece data capture with inline measured values like surface area and piece count for validation without asset opening. The 'always-bigger' rule was replaced by the 'short-arc-by-point-count' heuristic to resolve AsymmetricOrientation_01, achieving cost-neutral complement-arc selection; two of six fixtures tested were categorized as Problem B, necessitating an index resolution fix addressing self-overlap or insufficient gain after merge (Fixture_InsufficientGainAfterMerge 07/12). Option C, utilizing a Union followed by a Difference operation for Clipper merging, exhibits cost equivalence to the prior design, costing 2 operations per attempt and eliminating redundant full-zone merges on success; Union and Difference against same-sized inputs have equivalent algorithmic cost. The loop closure implementation of Option C employs a Difference-based approach instead of Union-then-subtract, maintaining the identical 4-tier attempt-chain selection (primary/cross-left/cross-right/none) as the shipped design, consistently using 2 operations per attempt compared to 2-3 variable operations in the original implementation and validated across 24 fixtures.

originals.title: Fixture Variant Edge Extraction & Zone Merge Optimization
originals.body: Raw edge data is recovered from fixture variants (CW vs CCW) by computing the longest common suffix of zone-arc prefixes and appending an identical edge, implemented via `ExtractEdge` with zero extraction failures across 24 fixtures when trailing geometry matches. Zone merging now directly merges raw candidates using `ZonePoints` entries as boundary points, bypassing Clipper2 seam recomputation and avoiding unpredictable winding direction issues in `Clipper2.UnionNonAlloc`, which silently fails on degenerate geometries; a fallback mechanism is required due to failure on fixture `AsymmetricOrientation_01`. Loop closure gain is calculated via `Difference(candidate, ZonePoints)`, utilizing raw and trimmed buffers for merge welding, gain-gating, animation sizing (CheckPlayersToKillInArea), arc overlap guarantee, and prioritizing short-arc selection (17 points vs 803) in a retry chain. Raw candidate buffers are used for Union merges while Difference-trimmed buffers restrict display, animation, and gain checks to prevent tangency drops; a known-bad fixture showed +9.196 gain with raw candidate welding versus zero shared vertices in the Difference trim. Dropped pieces are classified as `NewCandidateArtifact` (low severity self-intersection), `DistantZoneLobe` (no bbox overlap), or BoundaryStraddling, often caused by self-intersecting `mergeSourcePoints`, confirmed across over 10 fixtures with `zoneSelfPieceCount=1`. Zone merge diagnostics log piece count, `zoneSelfPieceCount`, `ZonePoints` point count, candidate surface/centroid/bbox, and per-dropped-piece surface/category/centroid/bbox; use `Union(ZonePoints, ZonePoints)` to detect pre-existing self-intersections.

title: Dynamic Formation Systems
body: Agents derive world position from `theta*formationIndex` each frame, recalculating `theta` as `2π/agents.Count` in `AddAgentToGroup` and `RemoveAgentFromGroup` (RCP-monobehaviours-116). Decentralized slot computation uses a `ComputePosition()` function; formation index determines agent position. Agents are added/removed via `AddAgentToGroup` and `RemoveAgentFromGroup`. The circle radius is calculated as `(spacing × count) / (2π)` (RCP-monobehaviours-152). Alternating-sign grid formations use formulas: `column=index%agentsPerRow`, `col0=center, col1+: sign=(col%2==0)?-1:+1 * ((col-1)/2+1)` for outward symmetry (RCP-monobehaviours-123), and sparse layer spacing is calculated as `(spacing × agentsPerRow) / (sparseCount + 1)` (RCP-monobehaviours-158). Bilateral formation slot positions are computed via `Transform.TransformPoint` in O(1) time, mapping a 1-based follower index to ±column offsets. When manually controlling NavMeshAgent rotation with `Quaternion.RotateTowards()`, disable `navMeshAgent.updateRotation` and zero `navMeshAgent.velocity` (Knowledge/monobehaviours.md#BP-monobehaviours-032). Formation slot positions are computed in the leader’s local space, converted using `Transform.TransformPoint` to prevent world-space offset rotation (Knowledge/monobehaviours.md#BP-monobehaviours-035). Formation speed is controlled with three speeds per follower (fullSpeed, mirrorLeader, slowdownSpeed) compared against zLookAhead, locking the leader’s speed until followers are inFormation. A three-zone speed magnitude approach—arrive ramp → normal → overspeed catch-up—prevents outer-ring lag and ensures smoother inner agent movement.

originals.title: Alternating-Sign Grid Formation with Sparse Layer Spacing and Bilateral Slot Indexing
originals.body: The alternating-sign grid row-column formula for symmetric formation uses `column=index%agentsPerRow` and `col0=center, col1+: sign=(col%2==0)?-1:+1 * ((col-1)/2+1)` to produce outward symmetry regardless of agent count. For incomplete rows in formations, the local spacing is calculated as `localSpacing = (spacing × agentsPerRow) / (sparseCount + 1)`, ensuring consistent width and inset positioning relative to edges. This sparse layer spacing rescaling is canonical for all row-based formations. Bilateral formation slot positions are computed via `Transform.TransformPoint` using an O(1) method, mapping a 1-based follower index to ±column offsets without sorting or total counts. originals.title: NavMesh Agent Rotation, Formation Maintenance, and Speed Control

Formation speed is controlled with three speeds per follower (fullSpeed, mirrorLeader, slowdownSpeed) by comparing remainingDistance to zLookAhead; the leader is locked to formationSpeed until all followers are inFormation. A three-zone speed magnitude approach—arrive ramp → normal → overspeed catch-up—prevents outer-ring lag on rotation and ensures smoother inner agent movement, combining techniques from Behavior Designer Formations and Polarith AI. title: Unity 6 URP DOTS Instancing Shader Migration
body: In Unity 6 Universal Render Pipeline (URP) with Batch Renderer Groups (BRG), remove legacy instancing macros (`UNITY_VERTEX_OUTPUT_INSTANCE_ID`, `UNITY_SETUP_INSTANCE_ID`, `UNITY_TRANSFER_INSTANCE_ID`) as they are not present in Unity 6 SRP Core; BRG uses per-entity cBuffers. Keep only `UNITY_VERTEX_OUTPUT_STEREO` / `UNITY_INITIALIZE_VERTEX_OUTPUT_STEREO` for VR functionality. DOTS instancing requires shaders to use `HLSLPROGRAM`/`ENDHLSL` and include `#include "Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal/ShaderLibrary/Core.hlsl"`. Define property accessors as `UNITY_DOTS_INSTANCED_PROP(type, name)` and accessor functions `UNITY_ACCESS_DOTS_INSTANCED_PROP(type, name)`, defined in `com.unity.render-pipelines.core/.../UnityDOTSInstancing.hlsl` line 145. Dual-path texture sampling is controlled by `#define UNITY_DOTS_INSTANCING_ENABLED` or `#define D2D_HLSL`, with the latter preceding `#include "Destructible2D.cginc"`. Maintain CBuffer parity across shader variants; include placeholder declarations for `_D2dScale`, `_D2dOffset`, `_D2dSharpness`, and `_D2dAlphaSlice`, shadowed by `#define` redirectors using `UNITY_ACCESS_DOTS_INSTANCED_PROP(...)` to prevent runtime reads.

originals.title: Default.shader DOTS Instancing in Unity 6 URP
originals.body: In Unity 6 Universal Render Pipeline (URP), all rendering passes through Batch Renderer Groups (BRG) using GPU Resident Drawers; therefore, `CGPROGRAM` and `UnityCG.cginc` cannot include the `UNITY_DOTS_INSTANCING_START/END` macros which reside in `com.unity.render-pipelines.core/ShaderLibrary/UnityDOTSInstancing.hlsl`, accessible via `#include "Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal/ShaderLibrary/Core.hlsl"`. To enable DOTS instancing, shaders must use `HLSLPROGRAM`/`ENDHLSL` and include the aforementioned `Core.hlsl`.  DOTS instancing macros are named `UNITY_DOTS_INSTANCED_PROP(type, name)` for property definition and `UNITY_ACCESS_DOTS_INSTANCED_PROP(type, name)` as an accessor; these are defined in `com.unity.render-pipelines.core/.../UnityDOTSInstancing.hlsl` line 145.  The shader uses a three-way branch for dual-path texture sampling via `SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D_ARRAY`, `SAMPLE_TEXTURE2D`, or `tex2D`, controlled by `#define UNITY_DOTS_INSTANCING_ENABLED` or `#define D2D_HLSL`. The `#define D2D_HLSL` must precede `#include "Destructible2D.cginc"`.  The SRP Batcher necessitates identical fields (names, types, order) within the `UnityPerMaterial` CBuffer across all variants; to achieve this in DOTS instancing paths, placeholder declarations for `_D2dScale`, `_D2dOffset`, `_D2dSharpness`, and `_D2dAlphaSlice` are included. These placeholders are shadowed by `#define` redirectors using `UNITY_ACCESS_DOTS_INSTANCED_PROP(...)` to prevent runtime reads, maintaining CBuffer size/layout parity.

title: Variant Testing & Negligible Fixture Handling
body: Implement candidate heuristics as test cases, run against a fixture suite to determine generalization; validate fixture quality using a sanity oracle test. Classify fixtures individually based on oracle threshold achievement, not blanket category assertions. Real bugs must pass fixtures; irreducible non-events are excluded or tested as regressions. Five fixtures—BothNegligible_01/02, RightDegenerate_01, RightSelfReferential_01, SelfReferentialArc_ThinBorder_01—demonstrate gains consistently below 0.1 and are considered irreducible non-events; loop closure gains less than 0.100000001f define fixture pass/fail classification.
