title: Progressive VFX, Light Fades, Particle Alpha & Themed Color Changes
body: Pair VisualEffect damage VFX with normalized thresholds using `math.remap`; activate when normalizedDamage >= threshold; smooth fades with `Mathf.MoveTowards`. Fade lights to zero by decrementing intensity: `initialIntensity * (Time.deltaTime / lifeDuration)` per frame, controlled by `lifeDuration`. Prevent GameObject destruction until timeline duration elapses AND `aliveParticleCount` <= 0 for all VisualEffect components. Fade ParticleSystem alpha using `GetParticles`, mutating `startColor.a`, then `SetParticles`; modifying `main.startColor` affects particles emitted *after* the change, not existing ones. Theme UI elements (e.g., `ButtonGlow.SetTint(Color)`) by modifying only RGB components to preserve effect. Transition lighting parameters (ambient intensity, directional intensity, shadow strength, light color) between day/night targets using `Vector4.MoveTowards` per frame, controlled by `transition_speed`; initial snap via `UpdateLights()` (speed 10f). Use a DOTween-based polling mechanism with a Func<bool> condition; kill the tween upon success and utilize DoWhenever for edge detection (false→true only). Implement light intensity fades with a coroutine sentinel pattern (`Recipes/monobehaviours/pool-safe-light-fade-sentinel.md`), storing the Coroutine handle, stopping existing routines on `OnEnable`, resetting intensity on `OnDisable`, and capturing initial intensity within the coroutine body.

originals.title: Progressive VFX Activation, Light Fade, and Particle Cleanup
originals.body: To progressively activate multiple VisualEffect damage VFX based on normalized health, pair each effect with a normalized threshold using `math.remap` and activate when normalizedDamage is greater than or equal to the threshold, smoothing the fade with `Mathf.MoveTowards`.  Fading a light to zero in N seconds regardless of initial intensity involves decrementing its intensity by `initialIntensity * (Time.deltaTime / lifeDuration)` each frame, making `lifeDuration` the sole timing control. During destruction animations, ensure the GameObject isn't destroyed while particles are active; this is achieved by returning a boolean from the update function and only destroying when both the timeline duration has elapsed AND the `aliveParticleCount` is less than or equal to zero for all VisualEffect components. title: Git Branch Tracking Quirks and Upstream Configuration
body: Creating a new Git branch using `git checkout -b newname sourcebranch` inherits the upstream tracking of `sourcebranch`; if `newname` differs from `sourcebranch`, the `.merge` in the branch configuration will incorrectly point to `sourcebranch`. This leads to `git push` targeting the wrong remote branch. To detect this, use `git config --get-regexp '^branch\.<name>\.'` and compare the `.remote` and `.merge` values; if they don't match the intended tracking branch, correct the upstream with `git branch --unset-upstream <name>` followed by `git push -u origin <name>`.  A local branch without upstream tracking prevents PR creation via the UI, which can be resolved by establishing tracking using `git push -u origin <branch>`.

title: SyntaxAnnotation & ParseExpression Usage
body: Use `CompilationUnitSyntax.WithAdditionalAnnotations(new SyntaxAnnotation(key, value))` to embed metadata like preprocessor symbols, source origin, and pass number within a syntax tree; annotations persist through `With*` mutations but are lost during re-parsing.  Metadata embedding avoids wrapper types and thread-unsafe static state. `SyntaxFactory.ParseExpression` is safe for parsing small, already-valid expression fragments such as stripping qualifiers like `OuterClass.` from a node's string representation. This method provides fast and syntactically valid parsing when the fragment’s validity is guaranteed; avoid using it with untrusted input or large source code segments.

title: Per-Frame RNG Seeding and Allocation-Free Rolling Average
body: To seed a Burst-compatible IJobEntity's per-frame random number generator, use `SystemAPI.Time.ElapsedTime` once per frame to initialize `Unity.Mathematics.Random`, passing the result as a job field for independent, frame-coherent operation; this avoids per-entity allocations and contention. A rolling average can be implemented with a fixed-size `Vector3[]`, a write-head index, and a running average field, achieving O(1) performance per tick by subtracting the old value divided by N and adding the new value divided by N, advancing the head index, and ensuring correctness from frame 0 due to zero initialization. This technique eliminates allocation overhead for both RNG seeding and rolling averages. The elapsed time seeded RNG approach originates from `lands-of-old-runtime` (file: `Recipes/performance/elapsed-time-seeded-rng-ijobentity.md`, repo: `C:\ran_Unityity-workflow-optimization`) while the allocation-free rolling average comes from `Polarith AI` (file: `Recipes/monobehaviours/rolling-average-buffer-allocation-free.md`, repo: `C:\ran_Unityity-workflow-optimization`).

title: ADR Record Management and Validation Issues
body: Fail-closed supersede logic now requires a valid ADR/DDR ID in `readDecisionIndex()` before upgrades, preventing incorrect behavior from unvalidated citations; unresolvable IDs fall through to touch-and-continue deduplication. Generated ADR documents contain form-feed byte (0x0c) corruption detectable with `grep -P '0c'`, stemming from a string/encoding bug in the doc-sync pipeline. The ID-extraction regex in `src/capture/docspine.ts` line ~21 incorrectly parses timestamp-form ADR filenames (`adr-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS-xx-slug.md`) as short-form IDs (ADR-NNN), impacting usage by claude-nexus within `_documents/decisions/`. Timestamp-based record identifiers (PROP ID scheme: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS) exhaust the collision retry budget (60 attempts) during rapid batch writes, necessitating microseconds, sequence counters, or random components for improved entropy; new IDs follow ADR-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS-XX while preserving legacy sequential IDs. Authoritative filenames use timestamp-based naming (`adr-YYYYMMDDHHMMSS-slug.md`) for lexical sorting and display numbers are computed at render time from the `created_at` sort field, with `rebuild_index.py` building indices starting at max(legacy_nums)+1 (verified by test_integration_mixed.py::TestGappedLegacySequence), seeding DDR-001 and ADR-011; reference upgrades lack validation of cited IDs, potentially leading to unwarranted supersedes with hallucinated IDs like ADR-999. During ADR migration, recover Decision/Alternatives/Reason text from monolithic files using `git log --all` and `git show <commit>:path`, targeting Documents/architecture.md in commits 909962e and d97607b for ADR-002 through ADR-010.

title: Quantum Simulation Hot Path GC & Determinism
body: Quantum simulation hot paths and bot code require a strict zero-garbage collection discipline, utilizing only stackalloc/fixed arrays to avoid heap allocations; this includes functions like SetPathTargetsToExpandTeamZone and traversal/filter loops. This constraint is essential for frame-by-frame determinism across networked clients and must be maintained in new features.  Floating-point epsilon (FP.Epsilon) checks are mandatory for division operations to prevent divide-by-zero errors, replacing direct zero comparisons; fallback constants for these checks should be centralized within SpeedUtils utility functions to avoid hardcoded drift and maintain platform determinism.

originals.title: Session ID pinning at flow activation to avoid timeline race conditions
originals.body: Flow timeline markers (phase transitions, __end__ cap) must share a single session ID to prevent races when concurrent sessions write to the global transcript. Detect the session once at flow activation and store it in FLOW_SESSION_ID env var so all subsequent marks use the same ID.

originals.title: TDD Session Identifier and Branch Naming Conventions
originals.body: Session identifiers in TDD flows must include minute precision following the pattern `<slug>-YYYYMMDD-HHMM` (e.g., `auth-20260523-1430`); each run receives a unique folder and all phase output paths are derived from session_id (e.g., `.flow/tdd/<slug>/design.md`). Session ID resolution precedence is: (1) explicit --session flag, (2) $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID environment variable if a session card exists, (3) best-effort inference; agent files read session_id from `.flow/tdd/current.json`. Code and documentation reference session_id, not slug. When TDD pipeline creates a git branch, extract the feature name from session_id by stripping the trailing `-YYYYMMDD-HHMM` pattern (regex: `-\d{8}-\d{4}$`), then prefix with `feature/` (e.g., `artifact-creators-20260525-1430` → `feature/artifact-creators`); pass this constraint explicitly to the planner.

originals.title: Flow State Management & Session Isolation
originals.body: To prevent state leakage when caching session data across different file paths, use a composite key of `session_id` plus the hash of the file path; this resolves issues where reusing `session_id` 'S1' against differing tmp_path files caused pollution. Flow state is persisted in `.flow/*/current.json`, `.ged/`, or `.flow/<flow-name>/current.json`, with agents extracting `session_id` as `<slug>`, and concurrent flows isolated within `.flow/.tdd/<session_id>/`; however, the flow-shared file `.flow/classifier-result.json` lacks per-session isolation. The script `flow-state-write.py --flow-id <flow-id> --flow-path <flow-path> --phase <phase> --clear` manages state and appends to `~/.claude/flow-phase-timeline.jsonl`, enforcing a single active `flow_id` in `.flow/flow-state.env`, where `--clear` resets the marker without deleting design or architecture markdown files. Flow definitions in `flow.yaml` (validated by `flow.schema.json`) specify name, version, phases, models (haiku|sonnet|opus|local), effort, thinking mode, tools, input/output schemas (JSON Schema), context isolation (per_phase|shared|none), hooks, and telemetry paths; multi-phase state files must be declared as inputs/outputs. Shared library agents are identified by type prefixes like `tdd-architect` or `flow-shared:flow-improver`, and marketplace agents follow the format `namespace:name-agent`; workflows provide background execution with pause/resume, while flows incorporate hooks (pre-bash-safety, schema validation), tool allowlists, output contracts, and are used for persistence and multi-phase state.

title: Hook Types and SearXNG Interception Limitations
body: Enforcement hooks validate content and log violations, while content-modifying hooks like `pre-webfetch` intentionally intercept requests to modify content (e.g., using crawl4ai results) via a `decision: block`, bypassing native fetch without audit logging; maintain this distinction during hook development. Attempts to use `decision: block` within a hook to inject SearXNG results failed because Claude Code interprets the `reason` field as a denial, preventing output. The underlying module functions correctly, but the hook protocol restricts its usage for content injection. To integrate SearXNG, either remove the hook or directly call the `web_retrieval` module.

originals.title: Distinction: enforcement hooks vs content-modifying hooks
originals.body: Enforcement hooks check violations and block/reject (now log instead). Content-modifying hooks like pre-webfetch use "decision": "block" to return modified content (crawl4ai result) instead of native fetch—these are intentional interception, not violation guards, and don't use audit logging. Keep this distinction when updating or adding hooks.

originals.title: SearXNG hook interception via `decision: block` doesn't work
originals.body: Attempted to intercept WebSearch calls with a hook to inject SearXNG results using `decision: block`, but Claude Code treats the `reason` field as a denial, not usable output. The module itself works fine; the limitation is the hook protocol. Workaround: remove the hook or call web_retrieval module directly.

title: Agent Database Integration and Windows Tool Execution
body: Agents cannot directly import and call Python functions; they invoke PowerShell commands and use Read/Write tools on files, requiring a CLI wrapper module (e.g., `queue_cli.py`) with commands: `get-status`, `set-status`, `list`, `add-encyclopedia`. This pattern applies to all future agent-database integrations. On Windows, agents must declare PowerShell in their tools list; Bash maps to WSL Ubuntu and cannot access Windows drive paths (C:\...). Execute PowerShell commands directly within the tool declaration, avoiding subprocess wrappers as they break path resolution; invoke Python scripts like `add_atom.py` using PowerShell with a `PROJECT_ROOT` context. The output contract is stdout messages (e.g., 'Atoms written: N new, M updated'). This convention applies to encyclopedia-batch agents including `intake-agent`, `preflight-agent`, `route-queue-agent`, `extract-batch-agent`, `consolidate-merge-agent`, and `finalize-agent`. The consolidate agent previously failed due to omitting PowerShell in its tools declaration.

originals.title: Agent-to-database integration via CLI wrapper
originals.body: Agents cannot directly import and call Python functions—they can only invoke PowerShell commands and use Read/Write tools on files. To integrate agents with databases, implement a CLI wrapper module (e.g., queue_cli.py with commands: get-status, set-status, list, add-encyclopedia) that agents invoke via PowerShell. This pattern applies to any future agent-database integration in this architecture.

originals.title: Windows agents: PowerShell in tools declaration and direct command execution
originals.body: On Windows, agents must declare PowerShell in their tools list; Bash maps to WSL Ubuntu and cannot access Windows drive paths (C:\...). Execute PowerShell commands directly in the tool, never wrap in subprocess syntax (e.g., `powershell -NoProfile -Command "..."`)—subprocess wrappers break path resolution and confuse tool execution. When invoking Python scripts (like add_atom.py), use PowerShell with PROJECT_ROOT context; output contract is stdout messages (e.g., 'Atoms written: N new, M updated'). All encyclopedia-batch agents (intake-agent, preflight-agent, route-queue-agent, extract-batch-agent, consolidate-merge-agent, finalize-agent) require this—consolidate agent previously failed due to omitted PowerShell in tools declaration.

originals.body: Guide encyclopedia extraction prompts with a 3-part definition template: (1) what the concept is, (2) how it works/mechanism, (3) what distinguishes it from related concepts. This structure improves definition depth and prevents vague or surface-level extractions.

originals.title: Encyclopedia Entry Extraction Protocol
originals.body: Entries must use generic, domain-agnostic definitions from the Shared Knowledge Base perspective. Categorize into exactly one of: Concepts & Definitions, Frameworks & Models, Principles & Laws, Processes & Methods. Each definition is 2–4 sentences covering: (1) core meaning, (2) mechanism or reason, (3) distinctions from adjacent concepts. Applicability and examples must be sourced and grounded in text. Include only substantive coverage (multiple sentences or dedicated section), not passing mentions. Output as JSON with key 'shared-kb' containing array of entries with fields: name, category, definition, applicability, example, source_topics (formatted as 'filename.md#Section Heading'), source_chapters (integers).

title: Faithfulness Grading & Fabricated Flag Logic
body: Faithfulness grading distinguishes faithfulness (core claim support) from fabrication flags (missing attribution). Fabrication=true triggers when details absent from the source are stated; e.g., '40-minute commute' given '~1 mile.' High faithfulness (0.95+) requires exhaustive verification of every concrete claim (dates, numbers, quotes, details) against the source, demanding explicit support and rejecting extrapolations – faithfulness signifies 'in the source.' Evaluation is chapter-specific to prevent concept drift; alignment between entry framing level (individual, team, organizational, industry) and source material’s framing level is crucial. Synthesized definitions are faithful if they accurately capture core concepts and remain consistent with the source thesis. Scores below 0.5 indicate significant fabrication; near-perfect faithfulness (e.g., 0.95) is expected for verbatim text.

originals.title: Unsourced specifics trigger fabricated flag regardless of high faithfulness
originals.body: Specific details absent from the source (e.g., '40-minute commute' when source only states '~1 mile') should mark fabricated=true even with high overall faithfulness (e.g., 0.9), because the two metrics measure different dimensions: faithfulness evaluates support for core claims, fabricated flags any particulars lacking source attribution.

originals.title: Faithfulness Grading Conventions
originals.body: Faithfulness scoring demands exhaustive verification of every concrete claim (dates, numbers, quotes, example details) against the source to achieve high faithfulness (0.95+), requiring all factual assertions to be verified; small details like 'seven articles' versus 'many,' or '2012' versus an unspecified year are critical. Grading entry faithfulness involves systematic claim-by-claim verification of definitions, factual assertions, experimental details, and example construction to identify unsupported inferences and invented claims. Entries must be evaluated strictly against the assigned chapter to prevent concept drift and maintain source attribution, flagging unsupported or fabricated concepts with fabrication flags for exceeding content. Claims require explicit support from the source chapter, rejecting plausible extrapolations; faithfulness signifies 'in the source,' not 'reasonably follows from the source.' Faithfulness scores below 0.5 indicate significant fabrication, while near-perfect faithfulness (e.g., 0.95) is expected for verbatim text and lower scores acceptable for minor extrapolations. Verify alignment between entry framing level (individual, team, organizational, industry) and the source material’s framing level to detect extrapolation. Synthesized definitions are faithful if they accurately capture core concepts and remain consistent with the source thesis, even without being verbatim.

originals.title: Simple vs complex Burst job pointer field strategy
originals.body: For Burst jobs: (1) simple jobs with minimal fields—pass ulist.Ptr directly as uint4* job field; (2) complex jobs with multiple NativeArray dependencies—use ConvertExistingDataToNativeArray wrapper at scheduling site to avoid changing job signature. Strategy balances code simplicity against per-call conversion overhead.

originals.title: Job Structs with Unsafe Pointers & NativeArrays
originals.body: Parallel job validation rejects NativeArray fields constructed from unsafe pointers, throwing an InvalidOperationException; to resolve this, use raw pointer fields (e.g., `uint4* ptr`) marked with `[NativeDisableUnsafePtrRestriction]` and pass the length separately instead of wrapping in a NativeArray, as demonstrated in DD2D_CellProcessingSystem for accessing globalAlphaMasks. When passing arrays to job structs without nesting NativeArrays, make the struct `unsafe`, replace NativeArray fields with pointer + length pairs (e.g., `uint4* MasksPtr`, `int MasksLength`), capture pointers using `GetUnsafeReadOnlyPtr()`, and use pointer indexing in the job's Execute method. For job structs wrapping UnsafeLists allocated with Allocator.Persistent, employ `GetTempJobMemoryHandle()` as a safety wrapper; conversely, when incorporating non-owned pointer memory from functions like `ConvertExistingDataToNativeArray`, utilize `GetTempUnsafePtrSliceHandle()`. If passing TempJob NativeArray allocations to jobs via pointers, maintain references to the original array in a managed C# array (e.g., `spriteRgbArrays`) because only the original NativeArray handle allows disposal using `Dispose()` after job completion, preventing memory leaks.

title: strip_prose Usage Guidelines and Behavior
body: `strip_prose`, in `nexus_search/nexus_context`, processes prose-only content lossily via paraphrasing; applying it to code or structured data risks meaning loss, unsuitable for citable research content. Compression via Kompress (~20% savings) requires subagents returning compressed prose to the main context; direct session context reduction is not achieved. Future replacements must perform structural stripping (headers, footers, boilerplate) only, allowing advisory text for low-value boilerplate but avoiding sentence rewriting in research/synthesis flows. The original proposal incorrectly described `strip_prose` as 'lossless'. Do not add `strip_prose` to JSON-writing or short-input agents; design agents summarize input instead.

originals.title: Prose compression only valuable in subagent pipelines
originals.body: The ~20% savings from Kompress only pays off when a subagent returns compressed prose back to main context. Doesn't directly reduce session context limits. Use compression in retriever or processing pipelines where compression is transparent to the interactive user.

originals.title: Design/intake agents should not use strip_prose
originals.body: Intake agents use short user responses (gate already skips <250 chars). Design agents should summarize input, which achieves better compression than telegraphic strip_prose. Don't add strip_prose to JSON-writing agents—it mangles structure—or short-input agents where it provides no benefit.

originals.title: strip_prose Compression Behavior
originals.body: strip_prose, located in nexus_search/nexus_context, processes prose-only content; applying it to code or structured data risks meaning loss due to telegraphic word selection and paraphrasing. This is a lossy process unsuitable for citable research content where exact wording is important; fidelity loss outweighs ~20% size savings. The original proposal incorrectly described strip_prose as 'lossless'. Future replacements must perform structural stripping (headers, footers, boilerplate) only, avoiding sentence rewriting. Advisory text is acceptable for low-value boilerplate but should be avoided in research/synthesis flows requiring citation.

title: AsyncGPUReadback Handling and Fallbacks
body: The AsyncGPUReadback.Request callback can execute synchronously on some GPU drivers, requiring the async-operation-started flag to be set *after* the Request call to prevent premature RT release; this is critical for thumbnail capture scenarios where the render target (RT) must remain alive until the GPU completes reading. For thumbnail generation using AsyncGPUReadback, release the RT within the callback's finally block and implement a CPU fallback via ReadPixels if hasError is detected. Transient failures should be handled with retry logic by storing the request as nullable, attempting GetData within a try/catch/finally block, ensuring it’s always null in the finally to facilitate retries; exceptions during this process should be silently suppressed. This approach is documented in Recipes/editor/how-do-you-use-asyncgpureadback-for-thumbnail.md (origin: RuntimePreviewGenerator) and Recipes/gpu/async-gpu-readback-retry-try-catch.md (origin: lands-of-old-runtime), both located within the C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization repository.

originals.body: AsyncGPUReadback.Request callback may execute immediately (synchronously) on certain GPU drivers, before Request returns. Set the async-operation-started flag AFTER the Request call, not before. This guards against callback firing before the flag is set, causing RT release before GPU finishes reading.

title: Flow Framework Interactive Agent Consolidation & Self-Loop Guard
body: Interactive gates use Pattern A (inline pure-interrogation agents), Pattern B (`AskUserQuestion+SendMessage-resume` resolved by the parent for blocking gates), or Pattern C (soft prompts, avoiding gate creation). Flow plugin intake agents default to Pattern A; heavy isolated work uses Pattern B. Interactive flows are defined in `flow.yaml` using type: interactive phases with loop: {condition, goto, iteration_limit}. The `Pre-agent-self-loop-guard.py` script incorrectly blocks initial phase agent spawns by misinterpreting orchestrator→phase-agent transitions; inline retrieval/synthesis avoids this. Setting `FLOW_AGENT=design-doc-ingester` in `flow-state-write.py --phase ingest` triggers the guard, resolvable by setting `FLOW_AGENT=orchestrator` in `.flow/flow-state.env`. This relates to background task fixes and a documented earlier workaround.

originals.title: Interactive gates in subagents: Hybrid A/B/C approach
originals.body: (A) Inline pure-interrogation agents into parent commands. (B) Blocking gates in phase agents emit needs_decision blocks resolved by parent via AskUserQuestion+SendMessage-resume. (C) Soft prompts become documented defaults, not gates. Balances isolation, latency, responsibility. Derived from execute.md out_of_scope pattern (lines 99-106) and flow-research-detective precedent (inline intake).

originals.title: Intake consolidation: inline by default except heavy work
originals.body: Flow plugin intake agents should inline into parent command handlers (Pattern A). Exception: heavy isolated intake work (e.g., multi-round doubt gates) stays subagent (Pattern B) to parallelize spawning. Reduces redundant subagent overhead while preserving parallelism.

originals.title: Flow Framework Interactive Phases & Self-Loop Guard
originals.body: Define iterative flows in `flow.yaml` using type: interactive phases with loop: {condition, goto, iteration_limit} for machine readability and auditability; this enables harness understanding of prompt-logic loops. The flow-research-detective framework's `Pre-agent-self-loop-guard.py` incorrectly blocks initial phase agent spawns by misinterpreting orchestrator→phase-agent transitions as self-recursion, preventing infinite spawning via agent-name collisions. Using inline retrieval/synthesis avoids this; setting `FLOW_AGENT=design-doc-ingester` in `flow-state-write.py --phase ingest` triggers the guard because the orchestrator appears to be that agent type. Reset `FLOW_AGENT=orchestrator` in `.flow/flow-state.env` before fanning out ingest agents to resolve this; this behavior relates to background task fixes addressing false positives and a documented earlier workaround.

title: Parallel Burst Targeting Recipe Consolidation
body: Distribute units evenly across building attack targets without synchronization by expanding each sub-target into a single entry and assigning units deterministically using `unitId % targetCount != targetIndex`, ensuring Burst safety; this originated in `lands-of-old-runtime` and is documented in `Recipes/dots-ecs/modulo-hash-unit-target-assignment.md` within the `C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization` repository. Resolve turret aiming conflicts by splitting into a gather pass (reading target LocalTransforms to a NativeArray<float3>) and an aim pass (writing turret LocalTransform based on gathered positions), as detailed in `Recipes/dots-ecs/two-pass-parallel-aim-localtransform-split.md` from `IntoTheEndlessSea`. For N-vs-M parallel Burst targeting, implement a flat-gather broadphase by gathering all target positions and metadata into a NativeArray<T> on the main thread, passing it as [ReadOnly] to a parallel IJobEntity where each seeker scans the array; deferred cleanup utilizes `Dispose(state.Dependency)`, described in `Recipes/dots-ecs/flat-gather-broadphase-n-vs-m-parallel-targeting.md` from `IntoTheEndlessSea`. This flat-gather approach avoids ComponentLookup cache misses and is part of the `C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization` repository.

title: Serialized Field Mutation and Event Handling Techniques
body: To mutate a struct field directly without silent copies, expose ref-returning accessor methods with switch-based index dispatch; callers bind via `ref var x = ref owner.GetRef(i)` (Recipes/memory/ref-returning-accessor-struct-mutation.md, C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization). For undo-safe multi-target SerializedProperty mutations, use the ModifyValues<T> extension method which records objects before mutation, iterates target values via reflection, marks dirty, and updates (Recipes/editor/modify-values-multi-target-undo.md, UltEvents/Serialization.cs). Serialized event fields can be lazily initialized on access with a private backing field initially null; the public getter lazy-creates the value only when accessed (Recipes/monobehaviours/lazy-init-serialized-event-field.md, UltEvents/UltEventHolder.cs). Invoke() should guard directly on the serialized event field to avoid allocation when no listener exists. This approach handles both single and multi-selection correctly for SerializedProperty modifications. The origin of ref-returning accessor patterns is lands-of-old-runtime.

title: SerializedProperty Clipboard with Play Mode Preservation
body: To enable generic component clipboard functionality, use `SerializedProperty.GetBoxedValue()` / `SetBoxedValue()` (Unity 2022.1+) for copying and pasting arbitrary property values as boxed objects, avoiding per-type switch statements; on Save, iterate the `SerializedObject` storing a mapping of `propertyPath` to `boxedValue` within a `ComponentData` alongside a `GlobalID` in a `ScriptableSingleton`. Upon entering Edit Mode, resolve these stored values by `instanceID`/`GlobalID` and apply them using `ApplyModifiedPropertiesWithoutUndo`; failed resolves are placed on a retry list which is drained during the next inspection cycle. This approach preserves MonoBehaviour field values across play mode transitions.

title: HorizontalLayoutGroup Card Removal & Incremental Reconciliation
body: GameObject creation with HorizontalLayoutGroup initially snaps elements to final positions; dismissing an event card triggers a full rebuild, causing neighbors to snap due to new object creation. Smooth removal animates LayoutElement.preferredWidth toward 0 and collapses layout spacing, enabling gradual sliding. IEventView (ADR-020) exposes SlotRoot (RectTransform) and SetVisible(bool), toggling CanvasGroup alpha (hidden: α=0, visible: α=1); EventController._eventView is private; store (IEventView, EventController) tuples for pending slots. CardFlipPresenter requires centre-anchored UI (anchorMin=anchorMax=0.5), fixed size, center pivot (0.5, 0.5), and separate GameObjects for Animation components (CardIdleMotion, CardFlipPresenter, Tremble). Sizing bugs arise from GetWorldCorners/RectToCanvas failures on animated/rotated transforms; CardFlipPresenter rotates to −90° and popup rotates 180° around Y-axis. Page-turn unlocks suppress page-hint FX atomically using cardTiltZDegrees (default 8°) via localEulerAngles.z; flight tween zeros Z. Locked cards slide from the book's right edge maintaining layer visibility, fixing an EdgeBottomRight.x coordinate-frame bug (bookPanel-local space) using InverseTransformPoint. In `HudController`, dismissing event cards implements incremental reconcile as documented in ADR-051 to avoid reloading unchanged Addressable skins and views; this involves adding newly-visible events, removing newly-dismissed ones, and leaving unchanged cards in place, optimizing performance and eliminating 'snap' behavior.

originals.title: CardFlipPresenter UI Animation & IEventView Architecture
originals.body: IEventView (ADR-020) exposes SlotRoot (RectTransform) and SetVisible(bool) toggling CanvasGroup alpha (hidden: α=0, visible: α=1). EventController._eventView is private; store (IEventView, EventController) tuples for pending slots. CardFlipPresenter.CaptureSource(RectTransform, Canvas, homeSlot) captures source rectangles on the view side (e.g., LockedCardView.CardTransform); MainInstaller manually wires to EventPopupView._flip and EventHudView._flip; a single scene instance orchestrates all animations. CardFlipPresenter requires centre-anchored UI (anchorMin=anchorMax=0.5), fixed size, center pivot (0.5, 0.5), world position/scale/rotation. Multiple Animation components (CardIdleMotion, CardFlipPresenter, Tremble) must occupy separate GameObjects. Sizing bugs arise from GetWorldCorners/RectToCanvas failures on animated/rotated transforms—CardFlipPresenter rotates to −90° and popup rotates 180° around Y-axis, mixing world-space and screen-space. Animation reverses timeline: panel edge-on, swap back to carrier, carrier shrinks home, HUD card alpha restores; it is robust against parent-relative changes. Card reveals/locked-card unlocks reuse CardFlipPresenter flight math (world-space coordinates, reparenting before dwell, destroy post-reveal); pre-lift target position references base peek position plus EmergeDeltaX. Page-turn unlocks suppress page-hint FX atomically and use cardTiltZDegrees (default 8°) via localEulerAngles.z; flight tween zeros Z to avoid conflicts with straightening. Locked cards slide from book's right edge maintaining layer visibility until fully emerged; EdgeBottomRight.x coordinate-frame bug (bookPanel-local space) fixed via InverseTransformPoint to convert book edge center to container space with adjusted Y in localPosition.

originals.title: Incremental Event Card Reconciliation in HudController
originals.body: When dismissing an event card in `HudController`, implement incremental reconcile to avoid wasteful reloading of unchanged cards' Addressable skins and views, as documented in ADR-051; this involves only adding newly-visible events, removing newly-dismissed ones, and leaving unchanged cards in place. This approach eliminates the 'snap' behavior caused by destroying and recreating cards during dismissal, ensuring smooth animation because unchanged cards persist with their GameObject and loaded skin. The strategy focuses on incremental UI reconciliation instead of a full rebuild to optimize performance.

originals.title: HorizontalLayoutGroup Card Removal Animation
originals.body: When GameObjects are created and laid out by HorizontalLayoutGroup, they initially snap to final positions on frame one without transitioning from old positions; dismissing an event card triggers a full rebuild of all visible cards, causing neighbors to appear to 'snap' into new positions. This behavior is due to the rebuild architecture creating brand-new objects with no transition state, not an animation problem itself. To achieve smooth card removal, animate the card’s LayoutElement.preferredWidth toward 0 and collapse the layout spacing gap, enabling neighbors to slide gradually instead of jumping. This pattern provides a reusable solution for polished dismissal animations within HorizontalLayoutGroup layouts.

title: Harvest Workflow & Critic Signal Restriction
body: The `harvest-critic` agent emits only `⚑` and `named-target` signals with binary confidence scores ('high' - `⚑`, 'low'), replacing the previous 'medium' default. Phase 2.5 utilizes `harvest-critic` between Phase 3 reporting and Phase 4A atom spawning to flag items lacking named implementation targets or relying on weak sources. Atoms include a `confidence` field ('high', 'medium', 'low') initially based on source count, potentially downgraded by the critic verdict, enforcing role separation between Researcher, Analyst, Critic, and Synthesizer roles. Harvest errors categorized as staleness relate to policy drift affecting CoD and `budget_tokens` recommendations from `tdd-complexity-classifier.md` and `flow.schema.json`; reversed decisions are not back-propagated (GitNexus adoption). Metadata tags ('Use As-Is', 'Adapt', 'Ideate') are normalized using `.strip('*').strip()` due to initial markdown bold wrapping (`**Adapt**`, `**Use As-Is**`, `**Ideate**`) and map to enum members ('Adopt') during `harvest-knowledge` Phase 4D ingest. The workflow includes phases 0 (URL pre-fetch), 1A/1B (parallel batch-analyze, 8–10 sources/batch), 2 (categorization & clustering), 3 (report writing), 3.5 (Critique), and 4A-4D (atom extraction with embeddings), skipping Phase 4B/4C to avoid race conditions on `cluster-candidates.json`. Output files are named `harvest-knowledge`-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md or `repo-analysis`-YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM.md; concurrent writes are prevented by scoping audit logs to per-run/harvest-slug folders (ADR-20260806000943-35) using atomic writes across 46 sources and 5 batches.

title: Prompt Budget Allocation and Memory Consolidation
body: Prompt token budget allocation uses `clusterSize * 3` sentences per cluster, mirroring ADR-018 at the merge level; this can exceed token limits. To mitigate pathological cases (approximately 170 merges), a proposed fix allocates prompt budget proportional to identifier count (not implemented). The memory clustering pass limits `MAX_CLUSTER = 3` and excludes handoff memories ('X-initialized') from extractable `MEMORY_TYPES` via filtering `COMPLETION_RE` patterns in `extract.ts` (`types.ts`) and using `readDecisionIndex(cwd)`. A CLI prune-narration removes handoff-only memories using title-anchored `COMPLETION_RE` patterns. Merge quality improves by dynamically setting prompt budget (`clusterSize * 3`), preserving verbatim identifiers with `SANITIZE_PROMPT`, and reducing `MAX_CLUSTER`. Production validation shows a rejection rate of 1.1% from 88 clusters, baseline identifier loss at 7.8%, and standardized preprocessing (quote stripping) is crucial for measurement. Coverage metrics detect semantic loss missed by identifier-loss checks; 54 of 204 flagged merges showed identifier-loss only, 12 showed coverage-only loss, and 1 showed both. Architectural issues affect models like Haiku (~29.0% identifier loss) and gemma3:12b (~32.7%) on distill merges.

Handoff memories ('X-initialized') are excluded from extractable `MEMORY_TYPES` in `extract.ts` (`types.ts`) by filtering `COMPLETION_RE` patterns in `refineCandidates()` and converting pure-restatement ADR/DDR citations to pointers using `readDecisionIndex(cwd)`. originals.title: Prompt Budget Allocation
originals.body: The prompt token budget is allocated based on cluster size, with each cluster consuming `clusterSize * 3` sentences regardless of identifier density; this allocation provides a fixed space per source pair. This behavior mirrors the architectural budget constraint defined in ADR-018 at the merge level. Dense clusters, such as 12/33 exceeding token limits, are directly attributable to this scaling by cluster size rather than identifier count. A proposed fix involves allocating prompt budget proportional to identifier count instead of source count to mitigate pathological cases like those observed in approximately 170 merges. This density-based adjustment is not currently implemented but would improve robustness. The current implementation does not account for identifier density, which can lead to inefficient token usage. Scaling by density or implementing a threshold for high-density merges are potential future improvements.

title: Git Worktrees: Shared History, IDE Integration Caveats
body: Git worktrees share the same ref store, directly advancing branch references during commit creation to enable isolated parallel development on shared branches; concurrent feature branch development results in interleaved commit histories. Creating a worktree from `origin/*` (e.g., `origin/feat/core`) excludes local unpushed commits, potentially leaving the worktree out-of-sync if a local branch has changes ahead of the remote, such as `feat/core` having 6 commits ahead of `origin`. Worktrees are invisible to IDE checkouts like the Unity Editor, necessitating direct development on watched branches for verification and preventing forced reimports/recompilations. The `EnterWorktree` function creates a worktree from a remote branch; six unpushed fixes rewrote Button wiring when branching from `origin/feat/core`. Fast-forwarding includes all ancestors, even unrelated work, which can impact merge strategy.

originals.title: Git Worktree Behavior & IDE Integration
originals.body: Creating a Git worktree from `origin/*` (e.g., `origin/feat/core`) excludes local, unpushed commits; if a local branch has changes ahead of the remote (e.g., `feat/core` having 6 commits ahead of `origin`), the worktree will be out-of-sync and require `git merge`. Worktrees are invisible to IDE checkouts like the Unity Editor, which monitor specific branches; avoid using worktrees for IDE verification and instead work directly on watched branches to prevent forced reimports/recompilations. The `EnterWorktree` function creates a worktree from the remote branch. Six unpushed fixes rewrote Button wiring when branching from `origin/feat/core`. Skipping worktrees ensures IDE consistency and avoids synchronization problems.

originals.title: Git Worktrees and Shared Branch History
originals.body: Git worktrees share the same ref store, meaning commits within a worktree directly advance the actual branch reference; this enables isolated parallel development that lands on the shared branch. Concurrent development on feature branches results in interleaved commit histories where commits are not sequentially stacked. Fast-forwarding includes all ancestors, even unrelated work, impacting merge strategy and sometimes favoring direct fast-forward to specific commits over full branch merges. Worktree functionality is useful for isolating parallel work.

title: Background Phase Execution Verification and Agent Spawn Depth Handling
body: Background execute agents can report startup without actually spawning due to potential race/authentication issues; verification is performed using on-disk markers like branch renames, baseline files, and the execution-state.json file before assuming a phase is running, with direct spawning from conductor if verification fails. Phase agent guards must check `SPAWN_DEPTH` instead of declarative matches for self-loop detection because orchestrator's initial spawn always targets the declared agent; `SPAWN_DEPTH=0` at the orchestrator and >0 within spawned agents, tracked via the post-agent-spawn-depth hook. Flow.yaml declares an agent per phase to enforce allowlist rules before orchestrator spawning. Concurrent execute agents can race on shared tasks.json files when they spawn independently or through planner background launch, leading to conflicting edits or duplicate work; therefore, duplicate agents must be stopped immediately to avoid these race conditions.

originals.body: When execute agents spawn concurrently (independently or via planner background launch) against the same tasks.json and worktree, they run in parallel and risk conflicting edits or duplicate work. Stop duplicate agents immediately to avoid race conditions.

originals.title: Phase-agent guards must check SPAWN_DEPTH, not declarative match alone
originals.body: Flow.yaml declares agent per phase for allowlist enforcement, set before orchestrator spawns. Comparing incoming subagent_type to this declaration causes false positives—orchestrator's first spawn always targets the declared agent by design. Fix: gate self-loop detection on SPAWN_DEPTH > 0 (indicates running subagent), not declarative match. SPAWN_DEPTH=0 at orchestrator, >0 inside spawned agents (tracked via post-agent-spawn-depth hook).

title: Memory Consolidation & Decay
body: Memory retention utilizes decay_class (stable/architecture/api_contract/implementation) for context-aware policies, and memories below the recall-threshold confidence are flagged `stale` but preserved in `memory_links` for provenance via an audit trail. A 60s decay cycle flags memories non-destructively; manual Consolidate merges near-duplicates using cosine similarity, while Distill clusters related memories and Haiku-rewrites them for legacy knowledge cleanup. Export-time pruning removes stale project buckets, ensuring continuous maintenance without permanent data loss. The system avoids deletion, employing flagging as a non-destructive mechanism.

originals.body: Decay (automatic 60s cycle) flags stale memories non-destructively; Consolidate (manual) merges near-duplicates via cosine similarity; Distill (manual, on-demand) clusters related memories and Haiku-rewrites each cluster, designed for legacy knowledge cleanup. Export-time pruning removes stale project buckets. Together enable continuous maintenance without permanent data loss.

originals.title: Memory Decay and Persistence

These stale memories are excluded from active recall and preserved in `memory_links` for provenance, accessible via an audit trail; decay is a non-destructive flagging mechanism rather than deletion.

title: AudioLodConfigBinder AudioMixerSnapshot Assignment
body: AudioLodConfigBinder contains three `AudioMixerSnapshot` fields for audio LOD state lookup, which are exempt from the [AutoCreateSO] attribute due to a constraint violation and inability to create instances. The `AudioMixerSnapshot` class does not derive from `ScriptableObject`, violating the drawer's `where T : ScriptableObject` constraint, and cannot be created via `CreateInstance()` as it is authored in AudioMixer. Only `AudioLodConfigBinder._config` (the SO field) receives [AutoCreateSO]; the three snapshots must be hand-assigned via the plain object picker to avoid runtime NullReferenceExceptions. All LOD tier snapshots must exist and be linked before runtime.

title: Sweep Remaining Behavior During Active Sessions
body: During active Claude Code sessions, `eligibleRemaining` increases as concurrent capture writes new memories, pushing the value from 4,020 to 4,103 despite processing 300 chunks; nightly steady state is approximately 192/day clearable. Single upticks in `eligibleRemaining` are normal, but three or more consecutive chunks with no headway trigger a stall guard abort. The prompt wording claiming 'strictly decreases' is misleading because concurrent capture adds to the remaining count. This indicates session capture outpaces sweep processing.  The stall guard abort condition checks for 3 consecutive chunks showing no headway.

title: Knowledge Extraction Tool Quirks and Workarounds
body: PowerShell classifier unavailability during environment variable or shell command checks can block knowledge writing; retry transiently. The permission classifier blocks relative-path glob patterns like `node scripts/*` in global `settings.json`; use absolute paths such as `PowerShell(node "C:\path\to\scripts")` or project-scoped `.claude/settings.json`. Relative glob patterns with a `path` parameter (e.g., `glob(pattern='*/agents/*.md', path='C:\...')`) are unreliable; use absolute paths in the pattern string. Combining relative patterns with intermediate wildcards and a `path` parameter consistently fails; resolve this by using an absolute pattern or Grep with a specific directory scope. If extract-knowledge Nexus pointer emissions fail due to safety classifier instability, rebuild the Knowledge index via `python scripts/rebuild_index.py`. Pattern resolution failures have been observed.

originals.title: Classifier Globbing Restrictions & Workarounds
originals.body: The permission classifier blocks relative-path glob patterns (e.g., `node scripts/*`, `npx tsx tools/*`) in global `settings.json` to prevent arbitrary code execution; this mirrors the LOCAL_MARKETPLACE rule style. Whitelist globally using absolute paths like `PowerShell(node "C:\path\to\scripts")`, or scope settings within a project's `.claude/settings.json`. Using a `path` parameter with relative glob patterns (e.g., `glob(pattern='*/agents/*.md', path='C:\...')`) is unreliable and returns no results; use absolute paths in the pattern string instead. Combining relative patterns with intermediate wildcards and a `path` parameter consistently fails; resolve this by switching to an absolute pattern or using Grep with a specific directory scope.

title: DOTS NaN Debugging: Pre/Post Physics Logging
body: To isolate NaN corruption in DOTs physics, insert an ISystem with UpdateBefore(PhysicsSystemGroup) that logs entity positions before physics runs; compare this pre-physics log to a post-physics output. If NaN is present in the pre-physics log, the source of the error lies within AgentSystemGroup or earlier systems; if it appears after PhysicsSystemGroup, the integrator is likely the origin. This pattern confirms whether NaN originates from input data or is introduced during physics processing. Throttle logging to the first N frames to reduce output noise and pair with frame-specific coroutine readback for detailed analysis.

If NaN appears pre-physics, the source is AgentSystemGroup or earlier; post-physics indicates the integrator. Throttle logging to first N frames to reduce output noise.

title: Guard Clause for Synthetic SessionEnd Events and Transcript Existence
body: Add guard clauses in callers, not functions, to prevent false positives when detecting missing state (e.g., writing stub notes for missing transcripts) in synthetic contexts like subagent events. In the `kanban SessionEnd` hook, use `_summarize._transcript_path(project, sid).exists()` before calling `summarize_session()`. This prevents garbage stub note writes when synthetic working directories (e.g., C:\Users\Fran) are generated without associated transcript files during Subagent SessionEnd events. Reuse the existing helper function `_transcript_path` to minimize footprint and preserve the original design intent of `summarize_session()` which provides stubs for delayed real transcripts.

Preserves the original design intent for legitimate cases while preventing false positives in synthetic contexts (e.g., subagent events). Reuse existing helper functions like `_transcript_path` for the guard condition.

title: PhysicsBodyBaker & Destructible Entity Collider Handling
body: PhysicsBodyBaker defers collider creation if alternative authoring, such as DD2D, is present on the same entity to avoid filter conflicts and unintended duplication; this allows the alternative system's collider to govern broadphase behavior. Destructible entities require both DestructibleAuthoring (sprite-bounds collider, destructible behavior) and PhysicsBodyAuthoring (mass/velocity), while non-destructible projectiles use only PhysicsBodyAuthoring. Composition separates shape responsibility from dynamics responsibility to avoid duplication; systems creating colliders must guard against creation for destructible types, checking for both the package's DD2D_DestructibleAuthoring and project-specific variants. This convention ensures consistent physics setup across destructible entities.

originals.title: PhysicsBodyBaker defers to alternative physics authoring
originals.body: PhysicsBodyBaker skips creating its own PhysicsCollider if alternative authoring (e.g., DD2D) is detected on the same entity. This allows the alternative system's collider to fully govern broadphase behavior. Prevents unintended collider duplication and filter conflicts between systems.

originals.title: Destructible Entity Authoring & Collider Integration
originals.body: Destructible entities require both DestructibleAuthoring (sprite-bounds collider, destructible behavior) and PhysicsBodyAuthoring (mass/velocity); non-destructible projectiles use only PhysicsBodyAuthoring. Systems creating colliders must guard against creation for destructible types, ensuring they maintain their own physics setup. title: Flat-Codebase & Prefab Patterns
body: The codebase uses a flat-component design; components like `CameraLookAround` encapsulate state, preventing sibling component access and favoring functionality folding within the owning component to minimize coupling. Prefabs are the single source of truth for component state (sprites, flags), eliminating dead code via downstream injection removal; deduplication skips nested prefab components using `PrefabUtility.GetCorrespondingObjectFromSource(component) != null`. Non-prefab scene objects report in-scene context, attributing issues to the source prefab (documented limitation). Lazy component resolution uses cached `GetComponentInChildren<T>()`; serialization is for external asset references like material paths. UI components register with Zenject via `GetComponentInChildren<T>()` lookups. Use `SerializeField` for compile-time safety and explicit inspector wiring; use `GetComponentInChildren` when component lifecycle depends on `Build()` invocations (e.g., `EventCardRevealAnimator` in `EventPopupView.Build()`); consolidate reusable UI logic like `EventCardView.Build()`.

originals.title: Flat-codebase pattern: component state remains private
originals.body: This codebase follows a flat-component design where each component (e.g., CameraLookAround) owns and encapsulates its internal state. Avoid sibling components reading public state getters; instead fold related functionality into the owning component. This keeps coupling low and state management localized.

originals.body: Prefab serves as single source of truth for component state (sprites, flags). Downstream injections duplicating prefab assignments are removed to eliminate dead code. Deduplication skips nested prefab components via `PrefabUtility.GetCorrespondingObjectFromSource(component) != null`, surfacing issues once from the originating prefab. Non-prefab scene objects report in-scene context; parent overrides or scene flag changes attribute issues to source prefab (documented limitation). Lazy component resolution uses cached `GetComponentInChildren<T>()`. Serialization is reserved for external asset references (e.g., material paths). UI components register with Zenject via `GetComponentInChildren<T>()` lookups, enabling multiple implementations (PlayButtonView, GrimoireView) in scene context. Consolidate reusable UI logic (reuse EventCardView.Build instead of duplicating in BuildCarrier); configuration adjustments are preferred over parallel implementations. Avoid duplicating entire UI designs for minor mismatches; target setup instead.

title: Encyclopedia Analysis Workflow & Soft Gaps
body: Successful encyclopedia routing with analyzer decline across all chapters (e.g., 'no relevant content') constitutes a soft gap, marking the encyclopedia pending and the book partial; no action is required unless the routing decision needs revisiting. The `route` phase of the encyclopedia pipeline always executes fully; analysis (`fork_analyze.py`) uses skip-existing logic during resume runs, blocking newly-routed encyclopedias unless `--onboard` is used.  The `pending_for()` function in `selective_run.py` identifies declined encyclopedias from `analyze-declined.json`, marking them as partial/incomplete; verification output `ok: true` confirms expected output by checking batch counts and topic totals, with `partial` indicating successful analysis where zero coverage reporting empty files as `invalid_files`. A book is complete when `verify-analyze` confirms all routed encyclopedias have at least one analysis file or are declined (0 topics) and recorded in `analyze-declined.json`, or pending with empty states; the `--only` flag selectively filters analyzed encyclopedias during topic generation. Encyclopedias producing zero topics after `fork_analyze` are 'declined' and recorded separately, representing legitimately empty-extracted encyclopedias that will be re-checked on resume using skip-declined.

originals.title: Analyzer declining all content is legitimate soft gap
originals.body: When an encyclopedia is routed but the analyzer declines extraction across all chapters (e.g., 'no relevant content'), this is a legitimate soft gap, not an error. The encyclopedia stays pending, and the book is marked partial. No action required unless the routing decision should be revisited.

originals.title: Encyclopedia Analysis Workflow
originals.body: The encyclopedia pipeline separates routing (cheap, cached, idempotent) from analysis (expensive). The `route` phase always executes fully. `fork_analyze.py` uses skip-existing logic during resume runs; it blocks newly-routed encyclopedias if their directories or anchor files exist unless `--onboard` is used. The `pending_for()` function in `selective_run.py` consults `analyze-declined.json` to identify and mark declined encyclopedias as partial/incomplete. Verification output `ok: true` confirms expected encyclopedia output by checking batch counts and topic totals; `partial` indicates successful analysis with zero coverage, reporting empty files as `invalid_files` and missing encyclopedias in `missing_expected: [enc_names]`. A book is complete when `verify-analyze` confirms all routed encyclopedias have at least one analysis file or are declined (0 topics) and recorded in `analyze-declined.json`, or pending with empty states; encyclopedias producing zero topics after `fork_analyze` are 'declined' and recorded separately. The `--only` flag selectively filters which encyclopedias are analyzed during topic generation. The `analyze` phase considers a book complete when `verify-analyze` confirms all expected encyclopedias have at least one analysis file. A 'partial' finalize status represents legitimately empty-extracted encyclopedias (declined: routed but yielded 0 topics), which will be re-checked during a future resume, with skip-declined making this check cheap; content for all extracted topics is complete and rendered.

title: Zone Creation and Logging Considerations
body: Zone logging of (zoneCreatedPointsCount, radius, duration) via ZoneCreationData precedes closure verification; however, these logs don't guarantee zone creation success due to degenerate geometry. `PopulateMeshAnimated` is deferred by the `ZoneMeshBuildScheduler` throttled to `MaxBuildsPerFrame=2`; trace delays using enqueue→scheduler→completion anchors should be used for investigation. The 'pick bigger per-side candidate' fix increases `zoneCreatedPointsCount` up to 2-3x mesh size, inflating `stopRadius` in `ZoneCreationController`. Reveal duration clamps at 1.0s due to oversized polygons and is calculated as (StopRadius − StartRadius) / _zoneCreationFromEdgeSpeed where _zoneCreationFromEdgeSpeed = 30 units/sec; the `zoneCreatedPoints` field is unioned with the real zone for rendering and input into `GenerateZoneCreationData()`. Geometry trim must execute immediately after long-arc retry (attempt2/attempt3) succeeds, before animation sizing, to prevent bloat leakage and requires dedicated test coverage beyond AnimationSizeTrim_* tests.

originals.body: Zone shadows render immediately; animated fills (`PopulateMeshAnimated`) are deferred via the ZoneMeshBuildScheduler throttled to `MaxBuildsPerFrame=2`, suggesting scheduler contention or distance-based culling. Trace delays using enqueue→scheduler→completion anchors. The 'pick bigger per-side candidate' fix increases `zoneCreatedPointsCount` (up to 2-3x mesh size), inflating `stopRadius` in `ZoneCreationController`. Reveal duration clamps at 1.0s due to oversized polygons, not the formula; smaller candidates maintain proportional points relative to capture size. The `zoneCreatedPoints` field is unioned with the real zone for rendering and input into `GenerateZoneCreationData()`, calculating reveal duration as (StopRadius − StartRadius) / _zoneCreationFromEdgeSpeed where StopRadius reflects the pre-merge polygon's farthest point; expanding a polygon increases this radius and animation duration, given _zoneCreationFromEdgeSpeed = 30 units/sec. GenericZone maintains `mergeSourcePoints` for merging and `zoneCreatedPoints` (trimmed by Difference) for game logic to prevent issues like detect-retry workarounds and ensure `CheckPlayersToKillInArea` doesn't see owned land. Geometry trim must execute immediately after long-arc retry (attempt2/attempt3) succeeds, before animation sizing; this is a hot-path with high regression risk requiring dedicated test coverage beyond AnimationSizeTrim_* tests; heuristic trimming post `GenerateZoneCreationData()` is insufficient. Early, unconditional trimming prevents bloat leakage.

title: Claude MCP Server Configuration and Persistence
body: MCP server approvals are context-dependent between the Claude CLI (`claude`) and CCD/desktop sessions; approval in one session does not persist to others or affect `~/.claude.json`.  Configuration files like `.claude.json` (CLI) and `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (Linux) / `AppData\Roaming\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows), along with `.mcp.json` at the repository root, require a full application restart to apply changes, including session reconnection for `~/.claude.json` edits and an app restart for `.mcp.json` modifications; project-specific flags are stored in the `enabledMcpjsonServers` array within `~/.claude.json`.  Personal preferences and permissions reside in the gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json` under the `mcpServers` key, while team conventions are committed to Git in `settings.json`, requiring `/reload-plugins` or a session restart for updates; direct edits to `settings.json` necessitate a complete restart or `/hooks` reload.  MCP servers are loaded at session start and new/modified servers require a fresh chat session (quit, process termination verification, relaunch) to be recognized, while existing connections automatically reconnect within the same session. Claude Code stores configuration in memory and periodically overwrites disk changes, so manual config edits persist only after a full application restart; if the session ID remains unchanged post-restart, ensure complete app binary termination before relaunching.

MCP tool schemas are deferred for context window optimization; plugin activation in `.mcp.json` must precede server list initialization. Claude Code stores configuration in memory and periodically overwrites disk changes, requiring a full application restart (quit + relaunch) for manual config edits to persist, ensuring complete config refresh and avoiding lingering session states; if the session ID remains unchanged after restarting, verify that the app binary has fully terminated before relaunching. MCP servers are loaded at session start, so new or modified servers require a fresh chat session (quit, confirm process termination, relaunch) to be recognized, although existing connections automatically reconnect upon restart within that same session. title: Event Data Architecture and Migration
body: Event IDs and theme labels in `worker/seed-events.json` are decoupled from code, enabling renaming without modification; the event shape (prefabKey, themeLabel, icon) is defined in the Worker and consumed by code. The `/events` endpoint supports legacy bare arrays and `{serverTime, events}` for migration to a single-source structure. Server-authored JSON at `Assets/StreamingAssets/events.json` defines events with properties including `id`, `themeLabel`, localized `title/description/acceptButton` (strings or `{en,fr,es}` objects), `minLevel`, and `endUtc`. Event data synchronizes via `sync-events.ps1` to Cloudflare KV, falling back to `worker/seed-events.json` with dates 2026-12-31 (stars) and 2026-09-21 (tower). LocalEventSource reads from `Application.streamingAssetsPath`; CascadeEventSource prioritizes Cloudflare KV, then `Assets/StreamingAssets/events.json`, and finally SEED_EVENTS in `worker/src/index.js`.

title: Rigidbody Alignment & Physics Stability
body: Align Rigidbody smoothly using physics torque: calculate `deltaRot = targetRot * Quaternion.Inverse(rb.rotation)`, convert to axis-angle, scale by stiffness, clamp magnitude, apply with `rb.AddTorque`. For controller input driving physics, use Roll, Pitch, and Yaw fields applying `AddRelativeTorque` or `AddForce`, scaled by body mass (Recipes/physics/quaternion-delta-torque-surface-alignment.md, Recipes/physics/controller-physics-rpy-split.md, repo: C:\ran_Unity\ity-workflow-optimization). Store Quaternion values as three Euler fields to prevent inspector drift; gimbal lock near ±90° on X (Recipes/serialization/quaternion-euler-storage-inspector-drift.md, UltEvents/PersistentArgument.cs). Initialize InertiaOrientation to `Quaternion.identity` because `default(quaternion)` normalizes to NaN. Guard inertia values before assignment and ensure InverseInertia and Angular velocity are consistent throughout the physics step. Prevent angular velocity magnitude overflow (|omega * dt / 2| >> 1) during quaternion integration, as it leads to NaN position errors.

originals.title: Unity Physics NaN propagation from uninitialized quaternions and invalid inertia
originals.body: default(quaternion) and PhysicsMass.Transform.rot initialize to (0,0,0,0), not identity; normalizing (0,0,0,0) produces NaN that infects positions via math.mul(NaN_quaternion, float3). Always explicitly set InertiaOrientation = quaternion.identity. Zero-valued InverseInertia or InertiaTensor components cause 1/0 division or infinite angular acceleration → NaN propagation; guard all inertia values before assignment. Angular velocity magnitude overflow (|omega * dt / 2| >> 1) also produces NaN in quaternion integration → NaN position. Ensure InverseInertia and Angular velocity are consistent throughout the physics step, and validate no saved inertiaTensor component is zero before use.

originals.title: Quaternion Delta Torque & Euler Storage for Physics Alignment
originals.body:
To smoothly align a Rigidbody to a target orientation each frame using physics torque, compute `deltaRot = targetRot * Quaternion.Inverse(rb.rotation)`, convert this quaternion delta to an axis-angle representation, scale the resulting vector by a stiffness value, clamp its magnitude, and apply it as `rb.AddTorque`; this approach, originating from Synaptic AI Pro (file: Recipes/physics/quaternion-delta-torque-surface-alignment.md, repo: C:	ran_Unity
ity-workflow-optimization), avoids directly setting Rigidbody.rotation for physics safety. When using controller input to drive physics, write Roll, Pitch, and Yaw float fields that a physics component reads and applies via `AddRelativeTorque` or `AddForce`, scaling torque by the body's mass (file: Recipes/physics/controller-physics-rpy-split.md, repo: C:	ran_Unity
ity-workflow-optimization) to ensure mass independence. To prevent inspector drift when editing Quaternion values, store them as three Euler float fields instead of four quaternion components, acknowledging the gimbal lock trade-off near ±90° on X (file: Recipes/serialization/quaternion-euler-storage-inspector-drift.md), a technique initially observed in UltEvents/PersistentArgument.cs.

title: ImpactCollisionSystem Debugging and Completion
body: Collision debug logs in the `ImpactCollisionSystem` must be placed in main-thread pass 2 due to Burst jobs' inability to call `Debug.Log`; this avoids restrictions within the Burst job itself.  Avoid using `Dependency.Complete()` as it stalls worker threads; instead, utilize an `EntityCommandBuffer` played back after job completion or skip scheduling when `CollisionEvents` is empty. The `ImpactCollisionSystem` previously fired `Dependency.Complete()` unconditionally every fixed step. This change prevents blocking of all worker threads during collision processing.

title: Addressables Ref-Count Races and Error Enrichment
body: Rapid fetching/releasing of `FetchConfig`/`ReleaseConfig` creates ref-count races leading to 'invalid active handle detected' errors (isHandleValid=false, Count>0, pendingLoads=0) during internal validation, often in respawn/character switching. Diagnose race conditions by enriching the 'invalid active handle' error within `AssetsProvider.cs` with the last 12 `Fetch/Release/Init` operations on the affected asset entry; this conditional enrichment avoids spam.

title: Chapter Processing Tool Efficiency & Cost Optimization
body: Tool efficiency ordering (cheapest to most expensive): tool-less single call < multi-turn sub-agent < Workflow (7× cost). Single tool-less calls avoid context re-sending overhead compared to multi-turn sub-agents ([Read,Write]). Claude Code system-prompt overhead (~24K tokens) exceeds chapter size (4–12K) and encyclopedia entries (1.5K/entry). Grouping calls delivers 6.4× input reduction (8 separate calls at 255K input → 1 grouped call at 40K input) by reducing the number of calls (8→1). Refactoring extraction workflows from multi-turn sub-agents to tool-less SDK calls reduces gross input per call by ~50% (~18K for SDK vs ~41K for sub-agent). A full workflow approach consumes ~125K tokens, which is 7× worse than a direct SDK call. Setting `tools=[]` removes approximately 27K tool catalog overhead; `allowed_tools=[]` does not affect costs. Default SDK overhead estimates (27K with full tools, 14K with empty tools) are inaccurate for production flows.

Multi-turn re-sends growing context across tool boundaries; tool-less avoids that accumulation. This matters as much as parallelism for total token consumption.

title: sqlite-vec Row ID and Schema Considerations
body: The `sqlite-vec` virtual table rowid requires BigInt parameters from Node.js queries in src/indexer.ts delete-cascade logic due to conflicts with SQLite's rowid when using `vec_id`. The architecture uses a single SQLite database with `content_type` discrimination across typed tables like `chunks` and `chunks_vec`, enforcing chunking at the lowest common denominator. `chunks_vec.vec_id` must be declared as INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT for Q6 row-ID stability, necessitating BigInt parameter binding for queries involving `vec_id`. Fixed-dimension vectors (mxbai-large, 1024-dim) are stored in `_vec` tables; the `vec_id` column was introduced to mitigate potential conflicts with SQLite's rowid. Benchmark performance on a ~50k-chunk synthetic corpus before committing to sqlite-vec+FTS5+RRF, considering fallback options like per-project vec partitioning or LanceDB, while vector schema generalization remains an open question.

body:
Iterate a circular region on a grid without `sqrt()` by iterating the bounding square and rejecting cells where squared distance to the center exceeds `rangeInCellsSq` (file: `Recipes/performance/radial-grid-iteration-squared-distance.md`, repo: `C: ran_unity
ity-workflow-optimization`). For sphere radius queries, expand the sphere to an AABB and iterate only cells within that rectangle, then perform a distance test (file: `Recipes/performance/sphere-to-cell-aabb-expansion-spatial-query.md`, repo: `C: ran_unity

ity-workflow-optimization`), or a spatial bucket hash map range query, which hashes XZ positions into NativeParallelMultiHashMap buckets and iterates through neighbor buckets, testing circle-to-circle distance per element (file: `Recipes/performance/spatial-bucket-hashmap-range-query.md`, repo: `C: ran_unity

The latter hashes XZ positions into NativeParallelMultiHashMap buckets and iterates through a square of neighbor buckets, testing circle-to-circle distance per element. title: NavMesh Agent Pathfinding and Recovery
body: A NavMeshAgent's `HasArrived()` spuriously returns true after `SetDestination()` without prior pathfinding; guard with `!agent.pathPending && agent.remainingDistance < threshold && !agent.hasPath`. The local `destinationSet` bool (BP-monobehaviours-031) tracks destinations set via `SetDestination()` or cleared via `Stop()`. Validate wander candidate positions with `NavMesh.SamplePosition(candidate, out hit, agent.height * 2, AllAreas)` before `SetDestination()` to prevent ignoring off-mesh locations (BP-monobehaviours-038). Detect NavMesh holes after `SetDestination()` by checking if `(slotPos - agent.pathEndPosition).sqrMagnitude > 0.5f` and retrying once with a reachable proxy; set the `destinationPending` flag to avoid repeated retries. Flush-wall spawns are prevented using a two-pass NavMesh clearance recipe (Recipes/monobehaviours/navmesh-two-pass-spawn-clearance.md in C:ran_Unityity-workflow-optimization), Pass 1 with an allowed area mask, Pass 2 finding the closest edge with an inverted mask. Fleeing agents are detected as stuck by polling displacement every N seconds; consider them stuck if displacement is less than `stuckThreshold` and `HasArrived()` returns false (Recipes/monobehaviours/flee-stuck-detection-zero-velocity-gate.md in C:ran_Unityity-workflow-optimization). This addresses formation desyncs caused by slots falling off the NavMesh, documented in Knowledge/monobehaviours.md#BP-monobehaviours-036 (C:ran_Unityity-workflow-optimization), and prevents immediately stuck spawns.

originals.title: NavMeshAgent Arrival and Wander Destination Validation
originals.body: NavMeshAgent's `HasArrived()` returns true spuriously on the first frame after `SetDestination()` if a destination is assigned without prior pathfinding; guard `HasArrived()` with `!agent.pathPending && agent.remainingDistance < threshold && !agent.hasPath`. The local `destinationSet` bool in BP-monobehaviours-031, set to true by `SetDestination()` and false by `Stop()`, prevents premature `HasArrived()` returns; its absence causes `HasArrived()` to return true on the first frame due to initial zero distance and `pathPending` being false. When implementing wander tasks, validate candidate positions with `NavMesh.SamplePosition(candidate, out hit, agent.height * 2, AllAreas)` before calling `SetDestination()`, as `SetDestination()` silently ignores off-mesh locations, potentially freezing the agent without error (BP-monobehaviours-038).

originals.title: NavMesh Agent Recovery and Spawn Clearance
originals.body:
To detect NavMesh holes after `SetDestination`, check if `(slotPos - agent.pathEndPosition).sqrMagnitude > 0.5f`; if true, retry once with a reachable proxy and set the `destinationPending` flag to prevent repeated retries. Flush-wall spawns are prevented using a two-pass NavMesh clearance recipe: Pass 1 samples positions with an allowed area mask; Pass 2 finds the closest edge with an inverted mask, rejecting spawns within a clearance distance. Fleeing agents can be detected as stuck by polling displacement every N seconds, considering them stuck if displacement is less than `stuckThreshold` and `HasArrived()` returns false, preventing infinite hung flee tasks due to unavailable far paths. This system addresses formation desyncs caused by slots falling off the NavMesh and prevents spawns that immediately get stuck. ity-workflow-optimization`.  The two-pass spawn clearance recipe originates from Polarith AI, detailed in `Recipes/monobehaviours/navmesh-two-pass-spawn-clearance.md`, also located in `C:	ran_Unity

title: ECS Singleton Access and Optimization
body: Access singletons with `GetSingleton<T>()` via `RequireForUpdate<T>()` in `OnCreate` to guarantee existence; alternatively, use `TryGetSingleton<T>()`. Optimize performance by caching the result of `HasSingleton/GetSingleton` before loops, accumulating changes locally, and calling `SetSingleton` once after the loop for batched updates. Cache `ComponentLookup` objects as fields in `OnCreate`, updating them with `.Update(ref state)` in `OnUpdate`. Hoist singleton references and resolve null checks before performance-sensitive loops to reduce codegen overhead, improve clarity, avoid repeated allocations, and API calls; accumulating mutations locally benefits sweeps of thousands of items.

title: Camera Movement & Lookaround Design
body: Use `Mathf.SmoothDampAngle` for camera movement smoothing during frame-by-frame target recalculation (e.g., camera drag) to avoid DOTween restarts and ensure smoother tracking; apply this to camera yaw by accumulating the target during drag frames, then easing it in `Update`. Decouple smoothing parameters: `smoothTime: 0.12` for snappy drag, `releaseSmoothTime: 0.8` for lazy spring-back, exposing both to the inspector. CameraLookAround's yaw behavior scales on screen aspect ratio (width/height) using `Mathf.Lerp`; portrait viewports require wider yaw range. Yaw sensitivity equals maxYaw; square-aspect screens land at an arithmetic midpoint between anchors. Alternatives were rejected due to complexity or inability to reliably hit authored anchors.

originals.title: CameraLookAround: Aspect-Ratio-Driven Yaw Scaling with Derived Sensitivity
originals.body: CameraLookAround's yaw behavior scales on screen aspect ratio (width/height), not resolution; identical aspect ratios produce identical feel regardless of pixel dimensions. Yaw range scales linearly via Mathf.Lerp between landscape and portrait anchors, with portrait viewports requiring wider yaw range than landscape. Yaw sensitivity (degrees per full-width swipe) is derived to equal maxYaw rather than authored separately, ensuring full-width drags always cover the complete yaw range and preventing sensitivity/max-angle drift. Linear interpolation means square-aspect screens land at an arithmetic midpoint between anchors. Alternatives including inverse-proportional formulas, FOV compensation, and AnimationCurves were rejected for complexity or inability to reliably hit authored anchors.

originals.title: Camera Movement Smoothing Strategies
originals.body: Use `Mathf.SmoothDampAngle` instead of DOTween springs when the easing target is recalculated every frame, such as during camera drag, avoiding tween restarts and enabling smoother tracking; for example, apply this to camera yaw by accumulating the target during drag frames and then easing it in `Update`. When implementing multi-phase camera follow mechanics like drag-follow and spring-back, decouple smoothing parameters—`smoothTime: 0.12` for snappy drag behavior and `releaseSmoothTime: 0.8` for a lazy spring-back effect. Expose both `smoothTime` and `releaseSmoothTime` in the inspector to allow designers to iterate on these values without code recompilation.
