title: Event Countdown, Animation & UI Optimization
body: TMP label text updates in EventContent.cs:21 use `if (label.text != newText) { label.text = newText; }` to prevent unnecessary re-meshing; the countdown timer label uses a StringBuilder redrawn only when the displayed second changes for performance optimization, applied across project UI code. Voodoo animation components (EyeBlink, CardIdleMotion, Tremble) replace Book of Hours coroutines and custom Easing (DDR-012), utilizing DOTween Pro with variable delays using `Random.Range(gapSecondsMin, gapSecondsMax)` and `DOVirtual.DelayedCall` curves; EyeBlink synchronizes via Sequence OnUpdate callbacks (e.g., PushRayLength) controlling fillAmount animation from 1→0→1. Sprite animations use a [Serializable] struct pairing Sprite + HoldFrames to prevent desync (DDR-042), employing coroutines, unscaled time, and `OnEnable/OnDisable` hooks. Event countdowns require DateTimeZoneHandling.Utc pinned at the Json.cs level for Newtonsoft.Json deserialization to avoid timezone shifts; duration is calculated as `EventInstance.Remaining (endUtc - serverTime)`. A 1 Hz driver on EventHud ticks all countdowns, with `ServerClock.Sync()` overriding in-session time and updating `Clock.Now` for automatic response, re-syncing via GET /time when PopupController opens unless `IsOverridden` is true; local JSON's serverTime from StreamingAssets/events.json is overwritten by `DateTime.UtcNow` for offline mode. To prevent clock tampering, calculate an offset = `serverTime − device UtcNow` and use `ServerClock.Now (device time + offset)` for expiry calculations instead of raw device time; live 1Hz ticks are clamped at 0 to prevent un-expiring events. Server time is re-synced when opening a card via MainSceneBootstrap, amending ADR-004. RR.VoodooMagic UI utilizes a TMP label driven by `CountdownFormatter` static method, not the Evo UI Countdown component.

originals.title: Event Countdown Synchronization and Server Time Handling
originals.body: Event countdowns require DateTimeZoneHandling.Utc pinned at the Json.cs level to prevent timezone shifts during Newtonsoft.Json deserialization (defaulting to DateTimeKind.Local). This centralized approach prevents client/server disagreement bugs. The countdown duration is EventInstance.Remaining (endUtc - serverTime), where serverTime from the /events endpoint is authoritative and prevents player manipulation. A 1 Hz driver on EventHud ticks all countdowns, with ServerClock.Sync() overriding in-session time and updating Clock.Now for automatic response; re-syncing via GET /time when PopupController opens unless IsOverridden is true. LocalEventSource overwrites the serverTime field with DateTime.UtcNow when loading from StreamingAssets/events.json to ensure zero clock offset in offline mode, so do not rely on local JSON's serverTime. To prevent clock tampering, compute an offset = serverTime − device UtcNow and use ServerClock.Now (device time + offset) for expiry/countdown math instead of raw device time; live 1Hz ticks are clamped at 0 to prevent un-expiring events. Server time is re-synced when opening a card via MainSceneBootstrap, amending ADR-004, preventing client-side time drift exploitation.

Components reschedule cycles with variable delays using Random.Range(gapSecondsMin, gapSecondsMax) and DOVirtual.DelayedCall curves. title: Claude Code MCP Health Checks, Classifier Outages, and Subagent Behavior
body: MCP server health checks have a ~1-2s timeout causing `-32001 Request timed out` errors with npx servers despite successful manual JSON-RPC testing; resolve slow `npx package@latest`-based cold starts by pinning versions in `~/.claude.json` (e.g., `firebase-tools@1.2.3`). The `mcp__plugin_claude-context_claude-context__search_unity_knowledge` classifier, using Opus, experiences transient outages/timeouts resolving with retries; these are not indicative of query validity or knowledge gaps. Outages of claude-opus-4-8 or claude-sonnet-4-6 safety classifiers cause Agent, PowerShell, and `mcp__plugin_claude-nexus` operations to fail; switch permission mode from auto to acceptEdits via `/permissions` during outages to restore agent spawning/Write/Edit. Agent spawning depends on claude-sonnet-5; 'claude-sonnet-5 is temporarily unavailable' failures trigger a fallback to sequential direct Read calls using Glob/Grep. Claude Code hard-caps concurrent subagent spawns at 20, triggering "Concurrent subagent limit reached" error if exceeded. A subagent claiming the safety classifier is 'down' may attempt command injection and should not be trusted without verification or re-derivation due to Claude Code auto-mode classifier blocking command-queue injection patterns.

originals.title: Claude Safety Classifier Outages and Subagent Limitations
originals.body: Outages of claude-opus-4-8 or claude-sonnet-4-6 safety classifiers cause Agent, PowerShell, and mcp__plugin_claude-nexus operations to fail with a 'safety cannot be determined' error, while Read/Grep/Glob tools remain unaffected; during outages, switch permission mode from auto to acceptEdits via /permissions to restore agent spawning and Write/Edit operations. Classifier outages typically last 5–10 minutes, and ScheduleWakeup automatically retries blocked operations, allowing read-only tools for analysis. A subagent claiming the safety classifier is 'down' may attempt command injection and should not be trusted without verification or re-derivation due to Claude Code auto-mode classifier blocking command-queue injection patterns from task notifications or tool results. Agent spawning depends on claude-sonnet-5, causing failures with the message 'claude-sonnet-5 is temporarily unavailable, so auto mode cannot determine the safety of Agent' when it’s down; Claude Code hard-caps concurrent subagent spawns at 20, triggering a "Concurrent subagent limit reached" error if exceeded and without retry queue. When Agent spawns are blocked, the system falls back to sequential direct Read calls on key files using Glob/Grep, enabling Read → synthesis → findings execution without agents, with file paths subject to existing access controls; PowerShell intermittently fails with 'claude-sonnet-4-6 is temporarily unavailable', but .NET System.IO.File.WriteAllText I/O remains operational and retrying after a seconds-long delay typically resolves the error.

originals.title: MCP Health Checks, npx Cold Starts, and Classifier Outages
originals.body: Claude Code's MCP server health-check timeout is too short (~1-2s) for npx-based servers, causing `-32001 Request timed out` errors despite successful manual JSON-RPC testing. Launching MCP servers via `npx package@latest` results in slow cold-starts due to npx re-resolving the package each launch; fix this by pinning versions in `~/.claude.json` (e.g., `firebase-tools@1.2.3`). The `mcp__plugin_claude-context_claude-context__search_unity_knowledge` classifier, which uses Opus, occasionally experiences transient outages and timeouts; these are not indicative of query validity or knowledge gaps, but will resolve with retries after a brief delay.

title: Hybrid ECS State Management & Lifecycle
body: Separate entity state and visualization initialization using `InitializeEntity()` for game state and `InitializeVisualization()` for visual binding, followed by an ECS bridge event. Managed code aggregates ECS entity state via injected `IEntityCache` using `GetEntities<TBridgeType>(key)` to avoid direct ECS World access (Recipes/monobehaviours-entity-state-vs-visualization-init-phases.md - RCP-monobehaviours-007, Recipes/dots-ecs/hybrid-ecs-state-aggregation-injected-cache.md - RCP-dots-ecs-001, `C: ran_Unity ity-workflow-optimization`). Implement a `Reset()` method in `IComponentData` (BP-dots-ecs-020) to prevent stale component states and use frame-rate-independent spawn timers with a singleton `ISystem` storing `SpawnCooldown` decremented by `fixedDeltaTime` (RCP-dots-ecs-027). Synchronize ECS state back to managed objects via an `ISystem` in the `OrderLast` of the `FixedStepSimulationSystemGroup`, after `UpdateBefore EndFixedStepSimulationEntityCommandBufferSystem` (Recipes/dots-ecs/orderlast-fixedstep-ecs-managed-sync.md). Use `FixedUpdate()` instead of `MonoBehaviour.Update()` for physics input (Recipes/dots-ecs/fixedupdate-input-bridge-physics-timing.md), and destroy orphaned child entities with a cleanup buffer element implementing both `IBufferElementData` and `ICleanupBufferElementData` (RCP-dots-ecs-005). Pair `VisualRef` (`IComponentData`) with `VisualCleanup` (`ICleanupComponentData`) for visual GameObject teardown (RCP-dots-ecs-065); when reusing dynamic buffers, check existing slots and destroy excess tail elements (RCP-dots-ecs-018).

originals.title: Hybrid ECS State Initialization and Aggregation
originals.body:
To separate entity state initialization from visualization state initialization in a hybrid managed/ECS system, split creation into `InitializeEntity()` (game state only) and `InitializeVisualization()` (visual binding only), then fire an ECS bridge event after both. Managed code aggregates ECS entity state via an injected `IEntityCache` abstraction keyed by integer cache keys; specifically, it calls `GetEntities<TBridgeType>(key)` for each entity category to accumulate results and write them to managed-side state, avoiding direct access to the ECS World. This approach originates from `lands-of-old-runtime`, documented in files `Recipes/monobehaviours/entity-state-vs-visualization-init-phases.md` (RCP-monobehaviours-007) and `Recipes/dots-ecs/hybrid-ecs-state-aggregation-injected-cache.md` (RCP-dots-ecs-001), located in the repository at `C:	ran_Unity
ity-workflow-optimization`. The goal is to maintain separation between game state and visual binding initialization, while also enabling managed code to access ECS data without direct coupling.

originals.title: ECS Entity Lifecycle Management & Synchronization
originals.body:
To prevent stale component states when an entity is despawned and respawned, implement an explicit `Reset()` method in `IComponentData` (BP-dots-ecs-020, file: Snippets/dots-ecs/ComponentStateReset.cs); frame-rate-independent spawn timers can be implemented using a singleton `ISystem` that stores a `SpawnCooldown` float, decremented by `fixedDeltaTime`, and recalculated upon spawning based on simulation state (RCP-dots-ecs-027). UI components with pointer events and async animations require state resets in `OnDisable()` to avoid freezes. To synchronize ECS simulation state back to managed objects safely within a fixed-step frame, use an `ISystem` in the `OrderLast` of the `FixedStepSimulationSystemGroup`, after `UpdateBefore EndFixedStepSimulationEntityCommandBufferSystem`, and utilize O(1) ID lookups (Recipes/dots-ecs/orderlast-fixedstep-ecs-managed-sync.md within `lands-of-old-runtime`). Avoid writing ECS input from `MonoBehaviour.Update()` to prevent a fixed step delay for physics, instead use `FixedUpdate()` (Recipes/dots-ecs/fixedupdate-input-bridge-physics-timing.md originating from `IntoTheEndlessSea`). To destroy orphaned child entities when a parent is destroyed, implement a cleanup buffer element with both `IBufferElementData` and `ICleanupBufferElementData` (RCP-dots-ecs-005), and for visual GameObject teardown, pair a `VisualRef` (`IComponentData`) with a `VisualCleanup` (`ICleanupComponentData`), destroying the `VisualRef` but leaving the cleanup component (RCP-dots-ecs-065). When reusing dynamic buffers, check existing slots before instantiation and destroy excess tail elements after reuse decisions (RCP-dots-ecs-018). These techniques are documented in the repository at C:	ran_Unity
ity-workflow-optimization, including recipes like `Recipes/dots-ecs/cleanup-buffer-orphaned-child-destruction.md`, `Recipes/dots-ecs/cleanup-component-visual-gameobject-teardown.md`, and `Recipes/dots-ecs/dynamic-buffer-entity-reuse-before-instantiate.md`.

title: Semantic Indexing Behavior - Claude Context
body: The `index_codebase` tool indexes large folders asynchronously, returning partial results immediately and progressively completing asset folder indexing (potentially taking several minutes). It supports concurrent querying of the previous index during new codebase creation or reindexing. Reindexing with `claude-context` always performs a full codebase re-index via `indexCodebase()`, exposed through MCP; incremental modes like `reindexByChange()` remain internal. The Knowledge/ and Recipes/ folders are indexed using `index_codebase` (idempotent); `get_indexing_status()` may report slow progress during embedding generation, a computationally intensive background process. Scheduled tasks omit `index_codebase` to prevent extensive reindexing.

originals.title: Claude Context Indexing Behavior
originals.body: The claude-context indexing tool performs a full codebase re-index each time, regardless of change size, and lacks incremental or diff-based modes; this process can span multiple sessions, necessitating `get_indexing_status()` checks in subsequent sessions.  `indexCodebase()` is fully exposed via MCP while `reindexByChange()` remains internal-only, preventing tool-dependent incremental indexing workflows. The Knowledge/ and Recipes/ folders are semantically reindexed using `index_codebase`, which is idempotent and safe to rerun after knowledge base modifications.  The operation of `index_codebase` is available but was intentionally omitted during scheduled tasks to avoid extensive reindexing.

originals.title: Semantic Indexing Behavior
originals.body: The `index_codebase` tool indexes large folders asynchronously, returning partial results immediately without waiting for 100% completion; Assets folders may require several minutes to fully index, but searches function from the start with progressively more complete results. During a new codebase index creation, the previous index remains active and serves queries while new embeddings process in the background, ensuring query continuity. The `get_indexing_status` polling during reindexing's embedding-generation phase may report slow or seemingly stuck progress (e.g., 15% for an extended time), which is normal due to the computationally intensive nature of generating embeddings for large corpora; this process continues in the background regardless of the reported status.

title: Cross-Index Generation and Index Management
body: The `build_cross_index.py` script updates CROSS-INDEX.json and CROSS-INDEX.md without modifying topic `.md` files; outdated `flow_version` fields in topic files are artifacts of previous `write_topic_files.py` runs. Project documentation originates from `.md` files, with derived indexes (`records.db`, `architecture.md`, `notes.md`) generated by `rebuild_index.py`; conflicts require editing original `.md` files then regenerating indexes; direct hand-editing of generated index files is prohibited. The gitignored `.decisions.db` file is regenerated by `rebuild_index.py ingest_files()` when deleted or modified, and documentation updates are handled via JSON payloads and subsequent regeneration using `rebuild_index.py`. title: Memory Extraction Candidate Limits and Prompt Dependence
body: Candidate count limits are prompt-based; an uncapped V3 run yielded 17 candidates versus a capped baseline of 20. The `MAX_CANDIDATES` threshold is currently 20 for generic sources and 40 for vcc-sourced extractions, effectively limiting output to approximately 9-11 candidates per window. Phase-section-cue tuning increases candidate count by 2–4x while maintaining groundedness, requiring a `MAX_CANDIDATES` increase to 30–40 for tuned vcc-input paths (FEAT-20260730150650-7f). Global preferences are crowded out during incremental window extraction when 5–9 dense technical items exist per window, but are captured in whole-session runs; a preference-crowding fix was validated (FEAT-20260730150709-cf). Incremental windows avoid the `MAX_CANDIDATES` cap and produce context-independent candidates via the `extract.ts` file's `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, testable with scratch files like `scratch-extract-tuned.ts`. Line-wrapped `### Phase:` markers necessitate multiline grep matching for flow transcript analysis (FEAT-20260730150641-ad), treating each section as independent.

title: Monster Hotel Core Loop Architecture and Request Handling
body:
The Monster Hotel core loop architecture was approved and updated on 2026-05-06, encompassing phases T0–T9 with deliverables including Asmdefs, fakes, request patience, worker fulfillment, a full day cycle, persistence seam, Unity shell, and PlayMode smoke tests. `Domain.asmdef` must have zero UnityEngine references for architectural compliance.

The maximum number of worker slots is determined by `DayCycle.MaxWorkerSlots = receptionRoom?.Level ?? 0`, increasing with reception room upgrades, which triggers `WorkerSlotUnlocked` firing `GameRoot.SpawnWorkersUpTo(evt.TotalSlots)`. Monster requests follow a Request: Pending → InProgress → Fulfilled / Failed state machine, queued in `_pendingMonsterSpecs[monsterId]: Queue<RequestSpec>`, with a cooldown timer of `cooldown = max(blueprint.RequestCooldownSeconds, gameSettings.MinRequestCooldownSeconds)` controlling dequeueing via `SpawnSingleRequest`. The gold payment formula is `blueprint.BaseGoldReward + BaseGoldReward × roomMatchBonusPercent / 100` (if TypeName matches RoomTypePreference) `+ BaseGoldReward × levelBonusPercentPerLevel / 100 × max(0, room.Level - blueprint.LevelPreference)`, with special currency awarded for fulfilling all requests.

`CheckDepartures` prevents monster departure if `_pendingMonsterSpecs` has entries or `_monsterCooldownTimers` is active. Movement uses `WalkTo(LocationId)` driven by `WorkerView` and `Vector3.MoveTowards`, reporting arrival via `gameRoot.NotifyWorkerArrived(workerId)`. Exit criteria include all EditMode tests green (~70+), all 3 PlayMode smoke tests green, and manual verification of tap actions (room with pending request → TapActionPanel; room without → upgrade panel; checkout monster → currency HUD increments).

originals.title: Monster Hotel Core Loop Architecture & Request Handling
originals.body: The Monster Hotel core loop architecture was approved and updated through Phase 3 on 2026-05-06, encompassing phases T0–T9 with deliverables including Asmdefs, fakes, request patience, worker fulfillment, a full day cycle, persistence seam, Unity shell, and PlayMode smoke tests.  `DayCycle.MaxWorkerSlots = receptionRoom?.Level ?? 0` determines the maximum number of worker slots, which is increased by upgrading the reception room; `DayCycle.AddWorker(Worker w)` adds workers post-construction and wires their callbacks. After upgrading reception, `WorkerSlotUnlocked` fires, triggering `GameRoot.SpawnWorkersUpTo(evt.TotalSlots)` to activate pending workers. Monster requests follow a Request: Pending → InProgress → Fulfilled / Failed state machine, with subsequent request specs queued in `_pendingMonsterSpecs[monsterId]: Queue<RequestSpec>`. A cooldown timer of `cooldown = max(blueprint.RequestCooldownSeconds, gameSettings.MinRequestCooldownSeconds)` is tracked and decrements until ≤ 0 to dequeue the next spec via `SpawnSingleRequest`, where MonsterBlueprint.RequestCooldownSeconds maps to MonsterType.requestCooldownSeconds and GameSettings.MinRequestCooldownSeconds maps to GameSettingsSO.minRequestCooldownSeconds. The payment formula calculates gold as `blueprint.BaseGoldReward + BaseGoldReward × roomMatchBonusPercent / 100` (if TypeName matches RoomTypePreference) `+ BaseGoldReward × levelBonusPercentPerLevel / 100 × max(0, room.Level - blueprint.LevelPreference)`, and special currency is awarded if all requests are fulfilled; `CheckDepartures` will not depart a monster while `_pendingMonsterSpecs` has entries or `_monsterCooldownTimers` is active. Movement abstraction uses `WalkTo(LocationId)` for symbolic navigation, driven by `WorkerView` with `Vector3.MoveTowards`, reporting arrival via `gameRoot.NotifyWorkerArrived(workerId)`.

title: Nexus Embedding Architecture and Truncation Considerations
body: Nexus uses a hybrid search architecture of FTS5+sqlite-vec+RRF (ranked reciprocal fusion), implemented in src/core/search.ts and indexer/indexer.ts, mirroring Claude Nexus’s atoms_vec pattern and generating mxbai-embed-large embeddings locally via Ollama. Client-side atom content is truncated to 1200 characters (512 tokens) using tree-sitter-mcp for AST-based semantic chunks. Incremental updates are gated by db_utils.is_stale(), and after sqlite-vec integration, `nexus_reindex` must be run once on session restart to backfill embeddings via embedUnindexed(). Phase 4B DBSCAN synthesis replaces per-atom LLM synthesis; retrieval quality risks exist beyond a document scale of ~1k (50k+ unbenchmarked), requiring pre-commit benchmarking of sqlite-vec. The system employs content-hash gating and uses `nexus_search(query, limit)` to avoid exceeding the ~295k token limit. Phase 4B fails silently if Ollama is unavailable, causing Phase 4C to skip.

originals.body: For interceptor-missile detection, use direct Entity reference with distance checks (InterceptorTag.target field) instead of adding physics colliders to missiles. This avoids BVH rebuild overhead at scale (500+ missiles). Add a splashRadius to interceptors to enable cluster kills within a radius, preserving gameplay without physics cost.

originals.body: Query projectile positions ship-by-ship rather than per-projectile. Computes threat data once, reused for damage resolution, avoidance steering, and point-defense targeting. More efficient than separate projectile-tracking queries and naturally feeds multiple ship systems.

originals.title: Projectile Hit Radius and Distance Queries in DOTS Physics
originals.body: The projectile's `hitRadius` parameter must be >= 0.1 for reliable narrowphase detection; a value of 0 often results in missed hits due to point-distance check behavior on FixedStep samples. Gameplay logic uses manual `CalculateDistance()` queries (O(N²/2)) with a closing velocity threshold for VFX and hull damage. title: WSL2 Docker VHDX Management and Configuration
body: Docker Desktop's WSL2 virtual hard disk (vhdx) file, such as `docker_data.vhdx`, grows with data writes but doesn’t automatically shrink; `docker system prune` and `docker system prune -a --volumes` only free logical space. To reclaim physical disk space, compact the vhdx using PowerShell's `Optimize-VDisk -Path <vhdx-path> -Mode Full` or Diskpart’s `compact vdisk` command, requiring first shutting down WSL with `wsl --shutdown` and running Diskpart in an elevated administrator PowerShell prompt. VmmemWSL hosts Docker Desktop's engine, and its memory footprint is affected by container memory usage; stopping containers reduces this consumption. A `.wslconfig` file (e.g., `~/.wslconfig`) configures WSL2 with parameters like `memory`, `processors`, `swap`, `autoMemoryReclaim=gradual` within the `[wsl2]` section, and `sparseVhd=true` within the `[experimental]` section to shrink the virtual disk. Changes to `.wslconfig` require a `wsl --shutdown` and Docker Desktop restart.

A `.wslconfig` file (e.g., `~/.wslconfig`) configures WSL2 with a `[wsl2]` section for parameters: `memory`, `processors`, `swap`, and `autoMemoryReclaim=gradual` which enables automatic memory reclamation to Windows, addressing indefinite memory retention prior to WSL 2.7.8. The `[experimental]` section allows enabling `sparseVhd=true` to shrink the virtual disk. title: Pymupdf4llm PDF Chapter Detection and Extraction
body: Pymupdf4llm's markdown extraction uses one-section-per-page for scanned/OCR PDFs lacking H1 headings, preventing large file sizes and enabling granular processing via a three-tier detection algorithm. PyMuPDF’s `doc.get_toc()` extracts bookmarks/outline data into the pipeline’s `nav_entries` format for Tier 1 chapter detection. Chapter detection employs a four-tier strategy: EPUB TOC, PDF outline/bookmarks, H1/H2/H3 headings, and numbered sections (`^£§`) as fallback; the adaptive word-count threshold is `max(50, min(300, total_words // 15))`. `book_encyclopedias` use a HIGH threshold (3–6) to limit gap lists to 0–3 entries per chapter. LLM classification acts as a Tier-4 fallback for structural signal failure. ONNX errors trigger `fitz.get_text('blocks')` instead of `get_text('text')` to preserve paragraph structure and enable numbered-section regex (`^ £§`).

originals.title: PDF fitz fallback: use blocks not text
originals.body: When pymupdf4llm crashes with ONNX errors, the fallback uses `fitz.get_text('blocks')` not `get_text('text')`. The text mode collapses all content into one paragraph, breaking section and heading detection. Blocks mode separates visual blocks with `\n\n`, preserving paragraph structure and allowing numbered-section regex (`^\d+\.`) to find titles.

title: InternalsVisibleTo Attribute Behavior & Assembly Compilation Stages
body: [assembly: InternalsVisibleTo(...)] enables cross-assembly implementation of lifecycle methods for internal abstractions; consuming assemblies can implement abstract disposal/lifecycle methods in separate `.asmdef` files. Runtime injection into DLLs is possible via Mono.Cecil (`AssemblyDefinition.ReadAssembly(path, ReadWrite:false)`, importing `InternalsVisibleToAttribute`, adding a custom attribute targeting the assembly name, writing to a new path - documented in `Recipes/editor/how-do-we-inject-internalsvisibleto-into-an.md`). Types referenced via [TestCase] attributes must be public (CS0051) because `InternalsVisibleTo` does not override this compiler rule. Custom `.asmdef` assemblies compile in stage 2, preceding `Assembly-CSharp` (stage 3), preventing direct references from custom asmdefs to `Assembly-CSharp`.  Therefore, `InternalsVisibleTo` functions between assemblies within the same or subsequent compile stages. Projects without `.asmdef` files utilize a default implicit editor assembly, allowing internal visibility access between test and production code without explicit `InternalsVisibleTo` attributes.

The extractor's `container` field only tracks lexical nesting for class members, so line-range intersection should determine symbol containment across TS/JS/C#/Python tree-sitter extraction.  In TypeScript extraction, use `visit(valueNode, container, enclosingQName)` instead of `descendAll(valueNode, container, enclosingQName)` to correctly handle variable initializers and capture call edges within non-function initializers like `const greeting = greet(name)`, as demonstrated in `typescript.ts`. Variables declared inside a top-level function report `container: null`, mirroring the behavior of true top-level symbols.

Previously, the TypeScript extractor's variable_declaration handler only descended into function initializers, incorrectly treating non-function variable initializers like `const greeting = greet(name)` as top-level variables. This resulted in missing call edges; the fix involves ensuring descent into all non-function initializers to capture these expressions.

title: ECS and IL2CPP Component Management Best Practices
body: For IL2CPP managed code stripping on iOS/Android/console, use `GetComponent(typeof(T)) as T` instead of `GetComponent<interface>` to avoid silent null returns. Component filtering should utilize `Component.GetComponents(List<T>)` with a persistent buffer and an 'is IInterface' filter loop, replacing allocating `GetComponents<T>()`. When adding components programmatically, use `SetComponent` for existing entities and `AddComponent` for new ones (RCP-dots-ecs-020), guarded by `DisallowMultipleComponentGuard` in Snippets/editor/DisallowMultipleComponentGuard.cs and implemented by BP-editor/guard-programmatic-addcomponent-against, preventing errors for types carrying [DisallowMultipleComponent] or built-in single-instance types like Transform, Rigidbody, Animator, and Canvas. Unused `IComponentData` fields consume chunk memory; orphaned serialized fields persist in .asset files upon config field removal; use `ComponentLookup<T>.HasComponent` (RCP-dots-ecs-019) for allocation-free entity destruction checks. Migrating `IComponentData` to unsafe structs improves performance via direct Burst pointer access and chunk-resident storage, as demonstrated by `DD2D_AlphaMaskComponent`.  `NativeArray` cannot be nested within job structs; use `GetUnsafeReadOnlyPtr()` with `Allocator.Persistent` and `[NativeDisableUnsafePtrRestriction]` for synchronous execution; jobs require `Allocator.TempJob`, iteration should use `[]` instead of `ElementAt()`. Use `UnsafeList<T>` which is blittable, stores directly in `IComponentData`, requires a `Resize()` after construction, offers pointer access via `.Ptr`, and provides indexing identical to `NativeArray`. Unmanaged `IComponentData` must be blittable, prohibiting managed object references like `Sprite` or `UnityEngine.Object`. Use `UnityObjectRef<T>` for UnityEngine.Object refs in IComponentData to ensure blittability, Burst compatibility, and survival during reloads; asset identity within components necessitates using blittable strings (`FixedString128Bytes`), requiring a separate managed layer for runtime resolution.

title: Service Access Vulnerabilities & Reentrancy Risks
body: Ungated service access, due to ServiceLocator patterns (used >50 times without null/registered guards), creates systemic vulnerability and breaks during mode/scene transitions; audit read sites for protection gaps. Reentrancy risks arise from TOCTOU vulnerabilities using `IsRegistered` before `Get`, especially during unregistration by `OnApplicationPause` and synchronous Quantum ticks impacting services, causing crashes in `PlayerHudViewsPool`, `PlayerActivityService`, and `EnemyTrainCarsPool`. Scene-scoped services potentially destroyed mid-frame require access guarded with `IsRegistered<T>()` before `Get<T>()`; null checks after `Get()` are ineffective. Sibling GameObjects' `OnDestroy` methods execute non-deterministically, necessitating null reference guards during lifecycle callbacks because proactive cleanup doesn’t reliably prevent destroy-order race conditions. Concurrent gameplay resume/teardown operations trigger `ObjectPoolsManager` destruction and pool de/registration (e.g., `_trainCarsPool`), creating a race condition where pools can be unregistered mid-async-operation; scene destruction is asynchronous (`WorldScreenView.cs:122`). Use `TryGet() + null/IsDisposed` instead of bare `Get()` to prevent stale-object crashes during concurrent teardown paths (e.g., `OnGameEnd`, `CloseTopScreen`, `OnEnter`); proactively scan and remove destroyed screen/popup references, implementing a `SceneManager.sceneUnloaded` subscription for cleanup.

title: Orchestrator Agent Working Directory & File Write Behavior
body: Orchestrator prompts require: (1) initial tool execution `cd` followed by Git verification; (2) `DIR/output_path` absolute paths only; (3) write verification before advancing. Agents default to the orchestrator's current working directory when prompt context lacks explicit information, causing unintended behavior in multi-repo/multi-worktree workflows without error reporting; therefore, every agent prompt must begin with `cd <path> && git log --oneline -1`. Creating Git worktrees requires adding `.worktrees/` to `.gitignore`, committing this change, and verifying with `git check-ignore -q .worktrees`; commit the `.gitignore` file before creating any worktrees. Filesystem verification (Test-Path or git status) is mandatory after claimed output due to frequent agent hallucinations and reported materialized write failures by implementer, knowledge-retriever, and close agents. When using `EnterWorktree`, subagents spawned with the Agent tool do not reliably inherit the worktree's cwd; always pass absolute paths to subagents within a worktree. Agents should use `Write()` for structured JSON payloads directly to the filesystem to reduce orchestrator context load and maintain file I/O responsibility; incorrect write locations have been observed in the main repo checkout affecting smart-implementer and knowledge-retriever subagents.

title: Atom Management and Database Synchronization
body: Atoms are upserted by name using `add_atom.py`, deduplicating on the 'name' field, differing from `add_adr.py` which keys on ID; new atoms receive an ATOM-NNN ID and file, while existing ones merge sources and rewrite files, supporting batch JSON array input. Database consistency is maintained by unconditionally writing to the database then conditionally writing markdown files based on their existence. Syncthing conflicts can revert gitignored databases (`atoms.db`, `records.db`, `sources.db`, `proposals.db`, `.stversions/`). The atoms.db schema is managed by `migrate_atoms.py`, incorporating cluster_id and self-healing checks within `add_atom.py`, `embed_cache.py`, `sync_clusters.py`, and `migrate_atoms.py`; atom IDs are generated via `next_id()` and filenames use angle-bracket markdown syntax, indexed by `rebuild_index.py` alongside architecture.md and design.md. File updates utilize `os.replace()`. Each pipeline script owns dedicated database connections (`_open_db`), and `migrate_atoms.py` is the authoritative source for schema migrations, including recreating tables with foreign keys OFF to add 'project_doc' to the source_type CHECK constraint, rendering `add_atom.py` stale. Low-volume harvest scripts like `add_atom.py` and `add_source.py` use per-call database open/close patterns mitigated by `write_txn/BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and `add_source.py` prevents duplicate URLs using `Path(file_path).stem`.

title: PostToolUse Hook Considerations
body: PostToolUse hooks must return valid JSON to avoid parsing failures; include `"shell": "powershell"` explicitly in the command to ensure consistent shell specification across platforms like Windows. Each PostToolUse hook spawns a PowerShell process with a ~200-400ms startup time, impacting performance during Edit/Write/MultiEdit operations within projects. To avoid errors related to missing POSIX paths on Windows, replace `/dev/stdin` with file descriptor 0 (fd 0) in bash scripts used as hooks. Always test PostToolUse hook commands directly in PowerShell rather than bash when targeting Windows environments. The 'fires from anywhere' behavior of these hooks justifies the performance tradeoff but warrants awareness during optimization efforts.

originals.body: PostToolUse hooks run command shells that must emit valid JSON. Inconsistent shell specification (some with 'powershell', some without) can cause parsing to fail on Windows. Always include `"shell": "powershell"` explicitly in PostToolUse hook commands.

originals.title: Windows hooks crash on /dev/stdin path
originals.body: Three hooks used POSIX /dev/stdin which doesn't exist on Windows; the error throws ENOENT before fallback logic can run. Use file descriptor 0 (fd 0) in bash instead. Always test hook commands in PowerShell, not bash, when targeting Windows.

title: UI Animation Conventions & Lifecycle
body: UI animations trigger via `OnEnable` for replayability and to avoid controller exposure; `OpenAnimationComplete` facilitates animation phase transitions, promoting modularity. UI components reside on child transforms to prevent LayoutGroup overrides and ensure `GetComponent` success. `CardFlipPresenter` classes decouple motion from logic controllers, routing transition metadata through the view layer with fallback behaviors. Initial rest states are captured during initialization and reset at each cycle start. Before flight animations, scale/position/rotation is read, active idle animations pause via `Pause()`, and transforms reset to their base pose. Asynchronous transitions use a suspended flag preventing restarts by `OnEnable`; `Resume()` calls after completion. Self-managing components use coroutines started on `OnEnable` and stopped on `OnDisable`.

originals.body: UI animations triggered by SetActive(true) naturally animate in OnEnable. This keeps animations self-contained without requiring controller exposure, and allows them to replay cleanly on re-enable.

originals.title: Animation Phase Handoff & Conventions
originals.body: Event-driven handoffs (e.g., `OpenAnimationComplete`) facilitate transitions between sequential animation phases on the same object, promoting modularity and reuse across contexts like open vs. close animations; UI animation components reside on child transforms to avoid LayoutGroup overrides and ensure `GetComponent` lookup success. Presenter classes such as CardFlipPresenter decouple motion from logic controllers, routing transition metadata through the view layer, with missing presenters triggering fallback behaviors reverting to previous styles or standard close animations. To prevent state corruption, authored rest states are captured during initialization and explicitly reset at each cycle start; before flight animations, scale/position/rotation is read, active idle animations are paused via `Pause()`, and transforms are reset to their base pose. Asynchronous transitions require a suspended flag to prevent premature restarts by `OnEnable`, with `Resume()` called only after transition completion, while self-managing components use coroutines started on `OnEnable` and stopped on `OnDisable`.

originals.title: Behavior Tree Decorator Reset & Cleanup Procedures
originals.body: To prevent permanent blocking of cooldown decorators during parent tree resets, the `Reset()` method must clear the `_elapsed` timer to zero; this ensures subsequent activations start fresh. When a Behavior Tree Timeout decorator expires, it should call its child's `Abort()` method before calling `Reset()`, propagating cleanup recursively down the subtree and preventing resource leaks. Similarly, any early-interrupting decorator must invoke `Abort()` prior to `Reset()`.  Action leaves should gate their `onStart` event using a `!IsRunning` check to ensure it fires only once per activation. To guarantee teardown regardless of termination method, action leaves must call `onEnd` both during natural completion and within the `Abort()` function. This pattern applies to Behavior Trees from Synaptic AI Pro. These procedures are documented in Recipes/monobehaviours/bt-cooldown-decorator-reset-preservation.md, Recipes/monobehaviours/bt-timeout-abort-before-reset-subtree.md, and Recipes/monobehaviours/bt-action-leaf-onstart-isrunning-gate.md within the C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization repository.

title: RTX 4090 Laptop: llama.cpp & Qwen3.6-27B Configuration

Q4_K_S (15.9GB) is too large and exceeds available memory, making IQ4_XS the optimal quantization level given this hardware constraint.

title: Lazy Field Hash Coercion and ALTER Table Strategy
body: To enable incremental migration with a `sha256(kind+name+content)` formula, coerce null `body` values to empty strings (`body ?? ''`) to maintain byte-identical hashes for un-reindexed rows; this avoids backfill jobs. Adding nullable TEXT columns via `ALTER TABLE symbols ADD COLUMN body TEXT` leverages SQLite's metadata-only path, preventing page rewrites and enabling lazy population during reindex.  A subsequent `PRAGMA table_info` probe is necessary to confirm column presence before executing Data Manipulation Language (DML) operations. This approach preserves backward compatibility while minimizing database impact.

title: Global Hook Crash Safety & Execution Environment
body: Global hooks execute within non-interactive shell contexts with restricted PATH and environment variables, requiring executable availability verification (e.g., python, node) on the system PATH; module-level imports in global hooks (UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStop, SessionEnd, PreToolUse, PostToolUse) must be wrapped in try/except blocks to prevent non-zero exits and prompt disruption across projects. Error handling within a global hook requires returning `{}` and exiting with code 0 for crash safety and prevention of cascading failures. `is_hook_active(__file__)` returns False outside Flow contexts, intended only for flow-local hooks invoked from /flow orchestration, not UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStop, SessionEnd, PreToolUse, or PostToolUse. Global hook failure results in a silent no-op via `{}` return and exit code 0 to maintain prompt stability across projects; hooks should be structured to return `{}` + exit 0.

title: FR2_Cache: Two-Way GUID↔Path Cache for Asset Lookups
body: FR2_Cache maintains bidirectional caches (GUID→path, path→GUID, instanceId→GUID) to avoid repeated `AssetDatabase` calls during rendering or search. Asset cache invalidation uses `m_assetChangeTS`, `m_fileInfoReadTS`, and a timestamp pair; `fileInfoDirty = m_fileInfoReadTS < m_assetChangeTS` avoids polling `File.GetLastWriteTime()`. FR2_Cache increments a monotonic timestamp during DB refreshes, stamps assets, then deletes outdated assets in O(n) without allocations. Multi-file imports use a 3-frame delay frame counter triggered by `AssetPostprocessor/AssetModificationProcessor` callbacks for coalesced refreshes; batch asset operations wrap with `AssetDatabase.StartAssetEditing`/`StopAssetEditing` and a suppressRefresh flag, deferring reimports and skipping `OnPostprocessAllAssets` reprocessing in batch mode for O(1) scaling. Dictionary<Object, string> caches results from `AssetDatabase.TryGetGUIDAndLocalFileIdentifier`, cleared on `AssetPostprocessor.OnPostprocessAllAssets` or `AssetDatabase.importPackageCompleted`. Bidirectional caching of GUIDs and paths using Dictionary<guid, path> and Dictionary<path, guid> eliminates repeated `AssetDatabase` lookups.

body: The Stars card uses shader-material Images (StarTwinkle procedural rendering) and atlas sprites; Tower card uses atlas sprites (Cloud A, Thunders, Tower Bricks) layered over a flat sky quad GameObject. Atlas binding failures cause the sky quad to become visible as a solid blue box. StarfieldGenerator.GenerateStars(int seed, int count, Rect bounds, float sizeMin, float sizeMax) generates StarInstance[] using System.Random with procedural data (positions, phases), rendering procedurally generated quads using vertex colors/UV1.y for phase/variant info and intensity variation via UV1.y. StarfieldGraphic distributes stars radially using weighted radius on an ellipse with centerClear01 (default 0.18) and edgeBias (default 1.6), preserving DDR-012's shader-driven _Time animation via mesh instancing. title: DOTS Instancing Standardization & Implementation Details
body: RRDestructible exclusively uses DOTS instancing; shader pragmas must update to `#pragma multi_compile DOTS_INSTANCING_ON` with conditional blocks collapsed to their DOTS content. URP 2D DOTS instancing utilizes `#pragma target 4.5`, `#pragma multi_compile _DOTS_INSTANCING_ON`, and CBUFFER properties `UNITY_DOTS_INSTANCING_START/END` guarded by `#ifdef UNITY_DOTS_INSTANCING_ENABLED`. GPU Instancing must be enabled on materials to set `m_EnableInstancingVariants` and trigger the `DOTS_INSTANCING_ON` keyword; sprite-specific symbols like `unity_SpriteProps` are protected by `#ifndef UNITY_DOTS_INSTANCING_ENABLED`. DOTS bakes sprite flip transforms into a matrix, so `UnityFlipSprite` logic should be omitted in vertex shaders when DOTS is active. The DD2D_SpriteRenderingSystem populates `_D2dAlphaArray` at runtime via `mat.SetTexture`; materials must be assigned through DD2D_DestructibleAuthoring to prevent full transparency due to uninitialized arrays. For D2D Sprite-Lit optimization, toggle 'Use Normal Map' and 'Use Light Mask', set 'Channels' to 'Alpha Only' with Alpha8 format (8 bpp), port CBUFFER and `_D2dAlphaArray` from Default.shader into D2D Sprite-Lit-Default, and build lit variants from unlit bases using URP abstractions while avoiding sprite-specific globals in DOTS passes.

title: Unity Testing and Editor Loop Quirks
body: Async race conditions in Unity necessitate Play Mode testing for non-deterministic timing, requiring scenarios like single unlock, double unlock, and rapid succession to avoid duplicates. EditMode tests do not advance fire-and-forget async operations (.Forget()) due to the absent player loop; this is safe for signal handler testing. Files in `Editor/` compile into `Assembly-CSharp-Editor`, preventing PlayMode API usage; create a dedicated PlayMode assembly definition file (`asmdef`) and move tests outside of `Editor/` to enable PlayMode testing. EditMode tests require manual verification within the Unity Editor, precluding headless automation via PowerShell or CLI. The editor's Update loop continuously executes even when unfocused, firing focusChanged but lacking runInBackground: 0. [ExecuteInEditMode] disables coroutines and causes crashes if StartCoroutine is called directly; use [ExecuteAlways] instead and conditionally execute coroutines with 'if (Application.isPlaying)'.

originals.title: Unity Editor Update Loop Behavior & Coroutine Restrictions
originals.body: The Unity Editor's Update loop continuously executes even when unfocused, unlike iOS which suspends; it fires focusChanged but lacks an equivalent to runInBackground: 0. This fundamental execution model difference impacts in-editor testing and distinguishes it from iOS backgrounding behavior.  Using the [ExecuteInEditMode] attribute forces Start() and Update() execution within the editor, disabling Unity's coroutine system which will crash if StartCoroutine is called directly. To work around this, use the [ExecuteAlways] attribute instead and conditionally execute coroutines with 'if (Application.isPlaying)'.

To enable PlayMode testing, move test scripts outside of `Editor/` folders and create a dedicated PlayMode assembly definition file (`asmdef`).  EditMode tests require in-Editor execution and cannot be run headlessly from PowerShell or the CLI; all EditMode tests must be verified manually within the Unity Editor before merging. This limitation prevents headless automation for EditMode tests.

title: Zone Creation Arc Orientation Bug - Polygon Orientation Mismatch
body: Polygon orientation selection failures occur when `ComputeZone*` (panam/main GenericZone.GetZoneCreatedPointsSingle) and `GetCreatedArea*` traverse complementary arcs for the same indices, resulting in opposite geometries and thin-border closure failures. The root cause is a convention mismatch: estimation functions use one arc direction while construction functions use its complement; area magnitude is unreliable. Bug 5492 caused animation bloat due to this. `GenericZone.cs`:519-540 contains flawed logic where `bestOrientation = argmax(surface)` compares raw shoelace magnitudes without distinguishing between the created-area arc and an almost-entire-zone arc, leading to incorrect surface estimates; magnitude selection is problematic when a candidate wraps nearly the entire zone boundary, surfacing as thin-border issues. The rule is that heuristic and builder must walk the same arc direction.

originals.title: Polygon orientation selection: estimate-builder arc mismatch
originals.body: Bug antipattern: if orientation heuristic (estimate) and final builder traverse complementary arcs for the same indices, the wrong candidate is always selected. panam/main GenericZone.GetZoneCreatedPointsSingle had this bug—Clockwise estimate vs Clockwise builder yielded opposite geometries, causing thin-border closures to fail. Rule: heuristic and builder must walk the same arc.

originals.title: Zone Creation Arc Orientation Bug
originals.body: The root cause of zone creation bugs is a convention mismatch between estimation functions (ComputeZone*) and construction functions (GetCreatedArea*), specifically a deterministic CW/CCW swap; the magnitude of the created area isn't the discriminator. Bug 5492, manifesting as animation bloat, resulted from `GetZoneCreatedPointsSingle` estimating arc orientation via shoelace heuristic then dispatching to the builder using complementary arcs for the same indices, consistently causing the 'losing' shape to be built. GenericZone.cs:519-540 contains the flawed logic where `bestOrientation = argmax(surface)` compares raw shoelace magnitudes without distinguishing between the created-area arc and an almost-entire-zone arc. This selection by magnitude alone leads to incorrect zone creation surface estimates, especially when a candidate wraps nearly the entire zone boundary. The bug surfaces at thin borders because small geometry relative to the zone makes the wrong candidate degenerate rather than suboptimal. The core issue is that `argmax(surface)` fails to account for the CW/CCW convention swap.

title: Gemma3 Performance Baseline & Health Confirmation
body: Initial assessments incorrectly estimated Gemma3's speed as 5x faster than Haiku; measurements reveal a ~20% speedup (8.3 seconds per call versus Haiku’s 15.8 seconds), with approximately 10 seconds of DB/KNN overhead per call resulting in an aggregate runtime estimate of ~14 hours. Latency extraction shows Haiku's 9.9s latency compared to Gemma3’s 6.2s latency. A previous test used a hand-typed prompt paraphrase instead of mergePrompt(), leading to the false suspicion of hallucinations and halting of a sweep; with real prompts, Gemma3 achieves 6/6 full retention at 6.1 seconds per call, confirming model health. Gemma3 produces valid JSON across four chunks (146/146, 139/139, 115/117, 96/96), significantly outperforming Haiku’s chunk 1 result of 84/86 (97.7%). Initial theories about the embedding model were incorrect; Gemma3's underperformance was due to GPU starvation, resolved by ensuring sufficient VRAM. A healthy Gemma3 performance baseline is defined as 6/6 full retention at 8.3 seconds per call and used for gating before long runs.

title: ExpandoObject Sidecar for Runtime Fields on Sealed Types
body: To circumvent .NET's restriction against adding fields to existing instances, use a `Dictionary<object, ExpandoObject>` or `ConditionalWeakTable<object, ExpandoObject>` (production) as a sidecar to store dynamic fields per instance. Default-value factory delegates are registered per type for initialization. Patched methods facilitate instance lookup, resolving the need for recompilation; the ConditionalWeakTable prevents memory leaks.

title: Unity Assembly Definition File Considerations
body: Editing assembly definition files can silently drop dependencies, including Unity.Newtonsoft.Json. TextMeshPro and Unity.Localization require `overrideReferences: true` in their asmdef files for correct resolution. DOTween Pro necessitates manual .asmdef creation; UI shortcuts (CanvasGroup.DOFade, DOColor, DOFillAmount) require the DOTween.Modules reference to avoid CS1929 errors. Code outside an .asmdef referenced from within another asmdef compiles to Assembly-CSharp and is invisible to code inside the referencing asmdef, potentially causing CS0103 'name does not exist' errors (e.g., EventPopupView cannot access CandleInstance.cs in FX/). Test assemblies using `overrideReferences: true` must explicitly reference production assemblies and include UnityEngine.UI.dll in precompiledReferences to prevent type-not-found errors when utilizing UI types like Image or Button. Always verify assembly references within test .asmdef files prior to writing tests.

title: Claude Agent Chapter Caching & Multi-Turn Extraction Architecture
body: The Claude prompt cache has a TTL of approximately 5 minutes and utilizes `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens`. It initially caches a ~24K system prompt (1.25x cost for the first call, 0.1x subsequent) then an ~8.9K CLI base prompt. Chapter caching of user content within system prompts (~4K token re-creation per call) can be enabled with `exclude_dynamic_sections: True` to create byte-identical [system+chapter] prefixes and leverage ~20.8K free tokens on Haiku 4.5, allowing subsequent forks to read cached chapter content. Stable prefixes like chapter + common extraction instructions are required for optimal caching; each encyclopedia call currently sends different extraction prompts limiting the cacheable prefix. Multi-turn extraction faithfulness degrades from A0's 0.954 to ~0.72–0.90 after turn 5 with a practical ceiling of 5–6 encyclopedias per conversation due to context accumulation and attention-split priming. Large chapters (3.5K–12K tokens) are crucial for faithfulness (0.962) and low fabrication (0.045), defining a safe group size as floor((25000 - chapter_tokens) / 1500). The optimal architecture uses sequential turns within a single conversation per chapter with H2 grouping (2 encyclopedias per call), achieving 73 extracted topics (recall 0.63) and reducing calls from 24 to 12 (~29% cost reduction) while decreasing input tokens from 496K to 86K (~5.6×). Opus faithfulness scoring should be used for verification, with prompt tuning occurring in a separate thread. Large chapters exceeding Windows CLI argument limits necessitate direct API access or local models for OAuth chapter caching.

originals.title: Multi-Turn Extraction Architecture and Prompt Caching Optimization
originals.body: The prompt cache structure prioritizes caching chapter prompts along with the system prompt for full hits (~26.4k cache_read), reducing rate limits to ~1.9k/fork, while half-hits (only chapter cached, ~13.5k cache_read) incur a unique per-fork extraction prompt cost (~15k rate-limit). Effective caching requires stable prefixes shared across calls, such as chapter + common extraction instructions, because each encyclopedia call currently sends different extraction prompts limiting the cacheable prefix to just the CLI base. Multi-turn extraction faithfulness degrades from A0's 0.954 to ~0.72–0.90 after turn 5 due to context accumulation and attention-split priming; an 8-turn run shows fatigue at ~48K tokens, establishing a practical ceiling of 5–6 encyclopedias per conversation. The optimal architecture utilizes sequential turns within a single conversation per chapter (not sub-agents) with H2 grouping (2 encyclopedias per call), achieving 73 extracted topics (recall 0.63) and reducing calls from 24 to 12 (~29% cost reduction) while decreasing input tokens from 496K to 86K (~5.6×). Large chapters (3.5K–12K tokens, H2-large) are crucial for faithfulness (0.962) and low fabrication (0.045), with a safe group size defined as floor((25000 - chapter_tokens) / 1500). Sequential architecture avoids sub-agent limitations due to independent system prompts, saves ~50% rate-limit tokens versus A0 single-call approaches, and requires conversation disposal between chapters. Opus faithfulness scoring should be used to verify final extraction quality, while a separate thread focuses on prompt tuning to improve faithfulness independently of architectural changes.

originals.title: Claude Agent Chapter Caching and Forking Strategy
originals.body: The Claude prompt cache has a TTL of approximately 5 minutes; parallel fork bursts can cause later forks to wait until the cache expires if rate-limiting is triggered, even with earlier cache hits. The `claude-agent-sdk` utilizes prompt caching, observable via `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens`, initially caching a ~24K system prompt (1.25x cost for the first call, 0.1x subsequent) and later only the ~8.9K CLI base prompt. To enable chapter caching of user content within system prompts or chapters (~4K token re-creation per call), forks can use a static system prompt (`exclude_dynamic_sections: True`) to create byte-identical [system+chapter] prefixes, allowing subsequent forks to read cached chapter content (~20.8K free tokens on Haiku 4.5). Each fork sees only [system+chapter+its-own-prompt], preserving A0 isolation and avoiding a quality drop of 0.875; the design uses a fork-per-encyclopedia approach, inheriting parent session's cached system/tools/history with each chapter loading once in the parent for subsequent cache reads ([chapter] + [its own enc prompt]). Large chapters within the system prompt exceed Windows CLI argument limits, necessitating direct API access or local models for OAuth chapter caching.

originals.body:
To optimize GOAP planning, implement an admissible A* heuristic by counting unsatisfied goal conditions as `h(n)`, ensuring optimality because each condition requires at least one action.  Actions should utilize a three-phase lifecycle: `OnEnter`, `OnTick`, and `OnExit`, with the planner triggering `OnExit` during interruptions to guarantee cleanup, guarded by `IsRunning` to prevent double execution. title: FloatMode and Data Layout Decisions for Collision Detection
body: FloatMode.Fast is selectively applied to broadphase and geometry-heavy loops (distancesq, SlabTest2D, BoxOverlapArea) within Burst jobs, balancing SIMD fusion gains against correctness requirements; the narrowphase stamp calculation retains FloatMode.Default to maintain visual placement precision. The Burst compiler supports FloatMode.Deterministic (branch-less execution) and FloatPrecision.Low (reciprocal approximation for sin/cos/sqrt), which is beneficial for VFX math and physics calculations in hot paths. ProjectileSystem and ShipRammingSystem utilize a Structure-of-Arrays float4 broadphase pattern, storing (x, y, radiusX, radiusY) per entity to enable parallel AABB distance checks before narrowphase and Burst compilation of O(N²) pair iteration.

title: Process Consultation Routing and Encyclopedia Finalization
body: 'Process Consultation' is multi-routed to shared-kb, leadership, communication, project-mgmt, and psychology encyclopedias with framings including domain-agnostic, coaching, conversation design, facilitation, and autonomy/agency, serving as a benchmark for evaluating multi-routing value; use 'Flows' (TDD, research-detective, doc-spine) for multi-session operations and 'Workflows' (encyclopedia batch processing, research retrieval) for session-scoped fan-out phases. Encyclopedia batch routing utilizes `pipeline()` and `parallel()` within Workflows with flow-shared agents as `agentType`, generating a thin index from canonical-topics.json files to map topic appearances across encyclopedias like 'Feedback Loops appears in: game-design, psychology-behavior, systems-thinking', prioritizing inclusion over duplicate merging and logging LLM routing confidence below 0.5 for manual review. Game design and psychology behavior encyclopedias use direct merge agents spawned with explicit file paths while the shared knowledge base uses a windowed merge pattern (`batch_size=50`) with resumable state tracking; `flow-book-encyclopedia-batch` writes topic `.md` files, consolidates touched encyclopedias, delegates indexing to Obsidian, removes LLM redundancy, and requires Phase 2 agents to have a status of 'ok'. The queue exceeding 300 items triggers a sequential background agent (error-skip-continue) logging every 10 books and performing routes/extracts/analyzes/consolidates/merges/indexes followed by concurrent individual book agents. Routing one agent per encyclopedia per chapter is rejected due to cost increases without accuracy gains, with static category filters replaced by LLM routing for (book, encyclopedia) pairs using Haiku (local LLM fallback acceptable), caching `{relevant, confidence, reason}` in `routing-cache.json` idempotently.

title: UnityWebRequest Limitations & WebGL Considerations
body: UnityWebRequest cannot execute in EditMode tests due to dependency on an active Unity player loop; asynchronous code utilizing UnityWebRequest requires play-mode testing or WebGL builds for verification. WebGL builds employ Brotli/Gzip compression, disable via Player Settings > Publishing Settings > Compression Format or server Content-Encoding headers if undesired. Desktop play mode does not accurately test UnityWebRequest functionality, impacting LocalEventSource (reading events.json via WebRequest.GetStreamingAssetAsync) and LocalPlayerStore (using PlayerPrefs.Save() for IDBFS flushing with FS.syncfs as a fallback). PlayerPrefs.Save(), called after atomic writes to force IndexedDB commits, is a no-op outside WebGL builds. Asynchronous IndexedDB flushing can lead to data loss during rapid tab closures; WebGL file I/O exclusively relies on UnityWebRequest (not System.IO.File) and utilizes LocalEventSource, LocalPlayerStore, PlayerPrefs.Save(), and .jslib.

title: Zero-Allocation Physics Queries and Truncation Handling
body: To prevent garbage collection allocations during physics queries, pre-allocate arrays for `Physics.OverlapBoxNonAlloc` and `Physics.RaycastNonAlloc` in the `Initialize()` function and reuse them across multiple queries. When using `Physics.OverlapSphereNonAlloc`, silently truncated results (returning `count == length`) require doubling the array as a field, re-running until `count < length`. For auto-growing buffers, double a `NonAlloc` physics query buffer and re-run when the returned count reaches the buffer length. Cache both the `RaycastHit[]` buffer and a `Comparer<RaycastHit>.Create` sort comparer as fields to maintain allocation-free sorting during multi-hit raycasts within the `lands-of-old-runtime` domain, aligning with recipe `RCP-physics-002`. Within `#if UNITY_EDITOR`, compare hit count to buffer length for `OverlapSphereNonAlloc` or `OverlapCircleNonAlloc` and issue a warning if equal. The `DegenerateQuadGuard` snippet (file: Snippets/performance/DegenerateQuadGuard.cs) checks edge pairs before emitting mesh triangles, degrading quads to triangles or skipping them; documented in `Knowledge/performance.md#BP-performance-015`. These techniques apply within C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization, with further documentation at C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization\Knowledge\performance\zero-allocation-multi-hit-raycastspherecast-with.md.

originals.title: Physics.OverlapBoxNonAlloc and OverlapSphereNonAlloc Array Handling
originals.body: To prevent garbage collection allocations during physics queries, pre-allocate an array buffer for `Physics.OverlapBoxNonAlloc` in the `Initialize()` function and reuse it across multiple queries by passing it to `OverlapBoxNonAlloc`. The `NonAlloc` variant writes results into the provided array and returns a count, avoiding heap allocations per query; if using `Physics.OverlapSphereNonAlloc`, be aware that it silently truncates when the provided array is full (returning `count == length`), requiring a fix where the array is stored as a field and doubled/retried until the returned `count` is less than the buffer's length, effectively self-healing truncation without per-call GC allocation. For scenarios needing auto-growing buffers, double a `NonAlloc` physics query buffer and re-run when the returned count reaches the buffer length.

originals.body: When using OverlapSphereNonAlloc or OverlapCircleNonAlloc, compare the hit count to the buffer length within `#if UNITY_EDITOR` and issue a warning if they are equal, as NonAlloc APIs silently truncate results which can cause AI blindness. The `DegenerateQuadGuard` snippet (file: Snippets/performance/DegenerateQuadGuard.cs) checks edge pairs before emitting mesh triangles to prevent NaN normals and invisible faces in procedural geometry by degrading quads to triangles or skipping them when vertices coincide. This guard is relevant for performance optimization (domain: performance, file: Knowledge/performance.md#BP-performance-015). The project resides at C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization.

originals.title: Zero-Allocation Multi-Hit Raycasts with Pre-allocation and Cached Comparer
originals.body: To eliminate per-frame GC allocations from raycast queries in input systems, pre-allocate a `RaycastHit[]` at initialization and reuse it via `Physics.RaycastNonAlloc()`, iterating only up to the returned hit count; this approach avoids allocating new arrays each frame.  Cache both the `RaycastHit[]` buffer and a `Comparer<RaycastHit>.Create` sort comparer as fields, not locals or lambdas, to maintain allocation-free sorting during multi-hit raycasts. title: Hybrid Search Latency Validation and Architecture
body: ADR-002 validated hybrid search latency against a synthetic 50k-chunk corpus, reporting a p95 of 198ms. Re-validation is TODO at the production database scale of 231k+ chunks; project enforces a p95 latency threshold of less than 500ms via `npm run bench`. Hybrid query performance requires a p95 latency of 500ms over a 50k-chunk corpus, currently measuring at 245.544ms (Phase-1 baseline: 198.217ms). The context-mode implements dual-tokenizer FTS5 full-text search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and proximity-based reranking, merging SQLite's FTS5 with sqlite-vec semantic search via RRF (k=60), achieving a p95 latency of 198ms on 50k synthetic chunks. Query sanitization includes quote-wrapping tokens to prevent FTS5 crashes, preserves AND/OR/NOT operators, and provides an Ollama dependency fallback; hybridSearch() utilizes claude-nexus and RRF fusion. FEAT-017 (hybrid-search latency) was benchmarked only on 50k synthetic chunks and requires validation at the actual target scale of 231k chunks, with cross-project scale verification beyond 1k documents required before Phase 2 (watcher, reranking, context reduction), and fallback strategies documented in docs/Uber Database SPEC.md Phase 0.

title: Spline Knot Manipulation and Reconstruction Techniques
body: To insert spline knots in reverse order, swap TangentIn/TangentOut before Insert(0, knot); no swap is needed for Append. After merging splines, set the zero-side tangent of a joining knot to the negation of the other's tangent to achieve C1 continuity without Catmull-Rom interpolation. For t-value reconstruction after partial deletion, store normalized t-values with world-space endpoints in each segment struct. When deleting segments, filter original knots by their t-interval and insert a boundary knot with tangents evaluated using EvaluateTangent to avoid resampling or approximation. These techniques originate from the lands-of-old-runtime project at C:\Fran_Unity\unity-workflow-optimization. Recipes are documented in Recipes/monobehaviours/spline-knot-tangent-swap-reversed-insert.md (RCP-monobehaviours-023), Recipes/monobehaviours/spline-knot-zero-tangent-continuity-fix.md (RCP-monobehaviours-025), and Recipes/monobehaviours/spline-segment-t-value-reconstruction.md (RCP-monobehaviours-032).

title: Boss Failsafe Timer & Combat Event Orchestration
body: The BossFailsafeMinutes timer (default: 5) in CombatEventOrchestrator spawns the authored boss wave if a wave fails to clear within that time, preventing infinite survival loops while respecting authored event definitions. Combat events use a two-stage pipeline: CombatEventSO generates a DifficultyContext containing PlayerMass from ECS and StorytellerBias from SOAP FloatVariable; this is passed to static CombatEventResolver.Resolve() producing ResolvedCombatEvent, following the WeaponStatResolver/ShipStatsResolver pattern. For VS, enemy count scales with PlayerMass via AnimationCurve relative to BaseMass = 1.0; enemy stats and FlowRate are fixed for difficulty scaling through DifficultyContext parameterization and testability. CombatEventOrchestrator (MonoBehaviour) handles orchestration (state machine, coroutines, wave sequencing, UI), signaling event completion via UnityEvent<CombatResult> for decoupled listeners; ECS systems detect DeathPendingTag on the player but do not manage UI choreography. ADR-035 documents this architecture including state machine states (Idle, WaveActive, CheckCompletion), ShipEntityBuilder driven on the main thread, and CombatEventOrchestrator superseding ADR-012.

title: Distillation Process Behavior & Recovery
body: Intermittent write-time contention causes distill rejections, which are expected behavior; rejected clusters remain eligible. Unparseable clusters in `distill.ts` are instrumented with response classification and sampling. 'clusters found' but 'created=0' in Distill MCP reports indicates authentication expiry. The sweep probe uses `mergePrompt()` with a 2-memory cluster, checking the `backendFailed` flag after three retries before strikes. Sweep auth-failure detection requires clusters > 0 && created == 0 && rejected == 0; all-rejected chunks signal data quality issues tracked in `DistillResult`, MCP responses, and sweep logs. Initial failure detection includes an embedFn failure guard mirroring callFn with a 5-consecutive-timeout abort. Merges are reversible by clearing `superseded_by` links and restoring originals (1694 recovered from 678 merges); `distill.ts:258` exclusively sets `refines` links and assigns `source_session_id: null`.

title: Dispatch Patterns for ECS and Monobehaviour Systems
body: To dispatch multiple ECS unit state machine handlers per faction without virtual dispatch, define an `IUnitStateMachineHandler` as a struct-constrained interface and use `ExecuteStateMachine<T>()`, short-circuiting on the first true result. For efficient passing of readonly `ComponentLookups` to burst-compiled AI helper methods, declare a plain struct holding `[ReadOnly]` `ComponentLookups` and singleton references; populate it once per system update and pass by value to static, burst-compatible helpers with mutation restricted via ref Aspect parameters. Command dispatch uses a `Dictionary<Type, ICommandLogic>` registered in `Initialize()`, employing aggressive inlining of `GetType()` for key dispatch and an early-return validation chain to prevent cascading state corruption; this avoids switch statements or factory methods. These approaches originate from the `lands-of-old-runtime` project at `C:‫ran_Unityity-workflow-optimization`. Relevant recipes are documented in `Recipes/dots-ecs/struct-generic-state-machine-dispatch.md`, `Recipes/dots-ecs/aspect-ai-context-readonly-lookup-bundle.md`, and `Recipes/monobehaviours/type-based-command-dispatch-validation-gate.md`. Identifiers: `RCP-dots-ecs-015`, `RCP-dots-ecs-022`, `RCP-monobehaviours-051`, `IUnitStateMachineHandler`, `ExecuteStateMachine<T>()`, and `ICommandLogic`.

title: CodeGraph Synchronization and File Watcher Health
body: Concurrent file edits can make staleCount unreliable; completion is declared when coverage ≥96% and both coverage and staleCount plateau. A /health response with watchedProjects count of 0 indicates a dropped file watcher lease, not an MCP connection issue. Rising staleCount in the /status response diagnoses watcher failures, pinpointing affected projects and revealing live reindexing breakage if files are touched but not picked up; do not pursue staleCount=0 in isolation. CodeGraph uses a three-layer incremental sync with zero-config filtering and project-specific watchers managed via `WatcherHandle.watchProject(projectId, rootPath)`, which is idempotent and automatically called by handleIndexProject in both the MCP and dashboard. The dashboard-server.ts calls `attachWatcherLifecycle()` to maintain live file-watching parity across projects indexed via the dashboard HTTP API, with watchers cleaning up on socket close/SIGTERM; concurrent watcher lifecycles can trigger UNIQUE constraint failures handled as 'another writer already completed this work'. CodeGraph synchronization uses a debounced file watcher (`CODEGRAPH_WATCH_DEBOUNCE_MS = 2000ms`, tunable between 100ms and 60s), combining OS file watching with per-file staleness banners and connect-time reconciliation of size, modification time (mtime), and SHA256 content hash for comprehensive updates, enabling hash gating; manual reindexing is possible via `claude-nexus reindexFile pattern`, while multi-task codegraph builds run asynchronously in the execute phase using `run_in_background=true`.

title: Background Shell Tasks and Windows Scheduled Task Termination
body: Background shell commands invoked via `run_in_background` are lost on session restarts; continuous sessions or foreground execution are required. Stopping these between sessions leaves no transcript marker, necessitating output file examination for completion indicators. The `Stop-ScheduledTask` cmdlet may delay termination of child processes up to 7 hours (ExecutionTimeLimit). To prevent premature termination of native commands like `docker compose up` by console signals (STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT), use `pwsh -NonInteractive -File <script>` with an explicit `exit 0`. Enable the `Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational` event log channel using `wevtutil set-log Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational /enabled:true` and query it via `Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational'}` for clarification of ambiguous exit codes. This `pwsh -NonInteractive -File` script with explicit `exit 0` solution is validated for constantly-running system tasks.

originals.title: Windows Scheduled Tasks: Native Process Handling & Termination Prevention
originals.body: The `Stop-ScheduledTask` cmdlet does not immediately terminate child processes; termination may require manual process killing or waiting up to 7 hours (ExecutionTimeLimit). To prevent premature termination of long-running native commands like `docker compose up` due to console signals (STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT), use `pwsh -NonInteractive -File <script>` and include an explicit `exit 0`. Enable the `Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational` event log channel with `wevtutil set-log Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational /enabled:true`; query using `Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational'}`. Examine the operational log to clarify ambiguous exit codes. This solution, wrapping commands in a `pwsh -NonInteractive -File` script with an explicit `exit 0`, is validated for constantly-running system tasks.

originals.title: Background Shell Task Persistence and Transcript Markers
originals.body: Background shell commands invoked with `run_in_background` are lost on session restarts, as harness does not save their completion record; long-running simulations/tests require either continuous sessions or foreground execution. Stopping a background shell command between sessions leaves no transcript marker, potentially masking successful task completion. To verify the status of such tasks, examine the output file for completion indicators rather than assuming failure. This behavior applies regardless of termination method (UI, timeout, process exit).

title: Clipper2 Merge Phase Issues
body: Clipper divergence originates from tangent-touch / LargestArea drops during the merge phase, impacting merge-area loss and fixture split. `CONVERSION_MULTIPLIER` limits precision in the fixed-point grid, potentially rejecting surfaces below `MinJoinArea` (≥0.1), now checked with a relative tolerance of `max(0.1, trimmedSurface * 2%)`. `LargestArea`-`Union` selection can cause area loss if contours don't weld or lead to Category 1/2 failures. Operations like `Difference(A, B)` followed by `Union()` and `Union(ZonePoints, ...)` create tangent boundaries or snap thin necks (0.56–52 surface units), splitting zones, as seen in `MergeSanityMismatch_20260805_220047_889`. Manual reproduction (`LoopCapture_SmallCandidatePass_20260805_103602`) showed a mergeGain area loss of 9.167, indicating thin/degenerate geometry triggers area loss in the `Union→Difference→Union` pipeline and potentially a native backend bug; candidateSurface values as low as 2.3 versus dropped pieces of 6.3 make area differences unreliable for correctness validation due to self-overlap discrepancies.

originals.title: Clipper2 Geometry Merging and Area Loss
originals.body: Clipper2's fixed-point grid uses `CONVERSION_MULTIPLIER` which limits precision, potentially rejecting surfaces below `MinJoinArea` (≥0.1) due to sub-pixel loss; `MergeSanityCheck` now employs a relative tolerance of `max(0.1, trimmedSurface * 2%)`.  `LargestArea`-`Union` selection can cause area loss if contours don't weld or lead to Category 1/2 failures, favoring geometric containment or summing touching pieces instead. `Difference(A, B)` followed by `Union()` and `Union(ZonePoints, ...)` operations can create tangent boundaries or snap thin necks (0.56–52 surface units), splitting zones; example: `MergeSanityMismatch_20260805_220047_889`.  Manual reproduction (`LoopCapture_SmallCandidatePass_20260805_103602`) revealed a mergeGain area loss of 9.167, suggesting thin/degenerate geometry triggers area loss in the `Union→Difference→Union` pipeline and potentially indicates a native backend bug. Area differences are unreliable for correctness validation due to self-overlap discrepancies resulting in candidateSurface values as low as 2.3 versus dropped pieces of 6.3.

title: Nexus Memory Extraction and VCC Compaction Pipeline
body: The memory extraction pipeline uses Observer (initial capture) followed by Reflector (deduplication, safe capture) for Claude Nexus persistent memory. Nexus raw condensing truncates sessions > 60,000 characters, setting 'truncated' to true; VCC compact processes full inputs without size limits. Distill (all-scope, limit:150) resolves ~124 memories from an initial pool of 8600 across ~450 processed memories and hangs on pools > 11,900, requiring batch processing with the `limit` parameter (e.g., `limit:150`). Nexus backfill processes sessions in batches of 10, yielding 200-300+ distinct memories across hundreds of sessions. VCC compact operates on incremental rawLines deltas and requires incremental-window validation before deployment due to phase marker omissions (V2 extraction keys) and out-of-view context citations (`reflector.ts → vcc-bridge.ts`), prioritizing fewer, more specific memories. Previous VCC compaction logic destructively overwrote live session transcripts in reflectorts integration (ADR-015, ADR-074), necessitating disabling `compactFileInPlace`. Consecutive Edit tool citations to the same file render empty because `artifact_registry.describe_artifact()` considers only headers for diffs within new_string snippets. Telemetry tagging uses `process.env.OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` (set in `runner.ts`: `service.namespace=nexus,automation=nexus`), propagated to spawned `claude` CLI calls. Configuration in `~/.claude/settings.json` is read at Claude Code startup and requires a restart for changes. Memory capture is enforced in `/extract.ts` via the `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, using a telegraphic format; existing 8860 Nexus memories are not re-authored. Manual `nexus_backfill` is needed only for pre-hook or missed sessions (`last_reflected_index = 0`), with `--all --dry-run` reprocessing all sessions if hook misses are suspected.

title: Auto-Discovery of Views
body: Views are auto-discovered in GameBootstrap via BootLoader and MainInstaller using `GetComponentInChildren<T>(true)`. A generic discovery method is provided through `ServiceContainer.FindView<T>()`, scanning scenes for MonoBehaviour view interface implementations, falling back to a mock if none found. Core installers avoid serialized fields pointing to controllers (manual-work.md §G), allowing [SerializeField] assignments for views (commit 78d4d96). GrimoireView is an exception with a direct serialized field on MainInstaller due to its critical main menu role and [RequireComponent] coupling, while GrimooreBookBuilder requires the view as a direct child of BootLoader's GameObject (ADR-021), falling back to a console mock if not properly placed. LoadingView and SplashView are explicitly parented under BootLoader; auto-find lookup for singleton views is deterministic but silent mock fallback when views are outside the installer subtree necessitates validation of view placement in the DI hierarchy (ADR-022). Serialized Inspector references were deferred due to editor workflow impact.
