title: Ship Ramming System Behavior and Configuration
body: Ramming system failures include inaccurate distance gap approximation (especially for elongated hulls) and lag from per-hit DD2D.ColliderRebuild on overlap; debug independently with separate fixes. ShipRammingSystem requires a `ShipRammingConfig` singleton; diagnostic probes should verify 'reached' and 'passed' counts in [RamDiag]. Large `minGap` values with overlapping visuals suggest collider-sprite scale mismatch. Phantom ramming can be caused by bounding-sphere overlap; disable ramming for testing using `MinClosingSpeed=9999`. Velocity impulses from ramming and knockback exceed `MaxSpeed` and decay via PhysicsDamping. Zero hits from projectile (460 entities) or ramming CalculateDistance queries indicate target collider invalidity, filter issues, or radius problems. The `ShipRammingConfig` includes a `ContactTolerance` parameter (defaulting to 0.1 world units, clamped to 0.1); baker handles stale values. Gap calculation approximates concave hulls by projecting (contactOnB - contactOnA) onto the hull normal using closest points; this is exact for convex shapes but inaccurate with concave notches. Replace gap detection with `ColliderDistanceInput`. `StampScale` and `CollisionRadius` must be proportional to visible hull size (approximately 0.2–0.4 units); excessively large `StampScale` values (e.g., 2–4 vs. 0.05–0.1) create holes, and overly large `CollisionRadius` values restrict ramming.

A `ColliderDistanceInput` query could provide a precise fix. `StampScale` and `CollisionRadius` must be proportional to visible hull size (approximately 0.2–0.4 units); excessively large `StampScale` values (e.g., 2–4 vs. 0.05–0.1) create holes, while overly large `CollisionRadius` values restrict ramming and impact broadphase efficiency. Current gap detection overestimates the gap for elongated hulls; replace this with `ColliderDistanceInput` for accurate hull separation.

title: Sprite Import Pipeline and Pre-Shrinking Decisions
body: Pre-process source art outside Unity if repo/CDN size is a blocker or higher-quality resampling (Lanczos) is needed; otherwise, Unity's box filter suffices. Use `sprite.rect` for extraction/transformation, where `textureRect` represents the trimmed mesh. SpriteExtractor extracts PSD at current resolution; pre-resizing or Affinity re-export can be used for other resolutions, with extracted PNGs inheriting destination folder settings via a postprocessor like Art/UI/crisp-UI. To prevent coordinate flips, blit a sub-region to a RenderTexture using UV scale/offset matching `sprite.rect`'s bottom-left origin and read the full RenderTexture; use `UiSpriteImportSettings.cs` `OnPreprocessTexture` with Single sprite and BottomCenter pivot for PNG extraction. PSD/PSB files bypass preprocessing, utilizing `AssetDatabase.SetImporterOverride<T>(path)` in `OnPostprocessAllAssets`, guarded by `GetImporterOverride`. Disable Automatic Reslice to prevent reimport conflicts; when resizing PSDs, disable Compression (or High Quality), turn OFF mipmaps, and set `Max Size` equal to the asset resolution; texture importer settings affect only new sprites unless `.meta` files are deleted or folders are reimported.

title: Adaptive UDP Retransmission Timeout and NTP Clock Offset
body: Adaptive UDP retransmission timeout is calculated as ResendDelay = 25.0 + avgRtt * 2.1 ms, designed to avoid HOL blocking on LAN and over-retransmit on WAN; this originates from LiveScriptReload/LiteNetLib in Recipes/async/how-do-we-set-a-retransmission-timeout-that.md. Accurate server clock offset is computed using the formula: offset=((t1-t0)+(t2-t3))/2, and rtt=(t3-t0)-(t2-t1), where t0/t3 are client UtcNow timestamps and t1/t2 are server-embedded big-endian timestamps; this originates from LiveScriptReload/LiteNetLib in Recipes/async/how-do-we-compute-accurate-server-clock-offset-from.md. The NTP clock offset calculation utilizes four timestamps to minimize error.

title: Baker Derived Value Precomputation, Static Projection, and DOTS Entity Instantiation
body: To maximize perception value in Baker, fold authoring perception fields into a single `MaxPerception` field during bake time, following the recipe documented in `Recipes/dots-ecs/baker-derived-value-precompute.md` within repository `C: ran_Unity ity-workflow-optimization`, originating from `lands-of-old-runtime`. Baker's projection logic should be extracted as a public static method on the `Baker` class, such as `Baker.Bake()`, enabling testing with `ScriptableObject.CreateInstance` fixtures (detailed in `Recipes/dots-ecs/baker-static-projection-unit-testable.md`), originating from `IntoTheEndlessSea`. SubScene prefabs require rebaking after physics baker logic changes; DOTS 1.0+ runtime `Instantiate()` does not trigger baking, requiring SubScenes for entity baking. To spawn entities at runtime, use `GetEntity(prefab, TransformUsageFlags)` to obtain the baked entity reference and store it in an IComponentData before using `em.Instantiate(prefabEntity),` because only SubScene GameObjects trigger baking.

originals.title: DOTS Entity Prefab Instantiation and SubScene Baking
originals.body: SubScene prefabs require explicit rebaking after physics baker logic changes in authoring scripts; stale baked data will be used if the prefab is not reprocessed by opening/closing the SubScene or restarting Play Mode. In Unity DOTS 1.0+, runtime `Instantiate()` does not trigger baking, necessitating a pattern of creating prefabs within SubScenes to bake them into entities. To spawn entities at runtime, obtain the baked entity reference using `GetEntity(prefab, TransformUsageFlags)` and store it in an IComponentData; then use `em.Instantiate(prefabEntity)`. This approach is standard because only SubScene GameObjects trigger baking, not those created at runtime.

title: ECS Sprite Rendering Scale and UV Handling
body: Non-uniform 2D sprite scale is stored in `PostTransformMatrix`, not `LocalTransform.Scale`. Copying `PostTransformMatrix` to fragments preserves scale; otherwise, the fragment appears 1x1. PhaseB previously divided UV scale by entity scale for scale invariance, but this compensation has been removed so that `transform.scale` directly controls mesh size in world space while the shader uses fixed [0,1] UV mapping to a 256x256 Texture2DArray slice. Sprites use 256x256 Texture2DArray slices with content centered via symmetric padding during Phase A registration and render using unit-quad meshes (object space ±0.5, texture UV [0,1]). Visual size is `content_size × transform.scale`. GPU offset/scale requires division by `entity.LocalToWorld.scale` for correct UV sampling. World positions are calculated using `entity.LocalToWorld` in `ExecutePaintCommand`. For sub-128 alpha textures (`architecture_ecs_rendering_option_a_uv_adjustment_for_sub_128_alpha_textures`), pixels are stored in the top-left corner, and UV correction uses `_D2dScale × ARRAY_TEXTURE_SIZE / textureSize`, computed each frame in `SpriteRenderingSystem.PhaseB`. When source texture width < `ARRAY_TEXTURE_SIZE` (128), a row-by-row copy in `TextureArrayManagerSystem.SetSlicePixels`: `for (int row = 0; row < clampedH; row++) System.Array.Copy(pixels, row * srcWidth, padded, row * ARRAY_TEXTURE_SIZE, clampedW);` prevents sheared output.

originals.title: PostTransformMatrix stores 2D sprite scale
originals.body: In DOTS, 2D sprites with non-uniform scale (e.g., X=Y=5 but Z=1) store the scale in PostTransformMatrix, not LocalTransform.Scale (uniform-only). When copying entity transforms to split fragments, must copy PostTransformMatrix or the fragment loses scale and appears 1×1 in world.

originals.title: Shader compensating for scale caused invariance
originals.body: PhaseB dividing UV scale by entity scale made sprites scale-invariant—transform.scale didn't affect visual size. Remove this compensation: let transform.scale drive mesh size in world while shader uses fixed [0,1] UV mapping to the 256×256 slice.

originals.title: ECS Sprite Rendering
originals.body: Sprites use 256x256 Texture2DArray slices (previously 128x128), content centered via symmetric padding in Phase A registration. Rendering uses unit-quad meshes (object space ±0.5, texture UV [0,1]). Visual size is `content_size × transform.scale`. GPU offset/scale requires division by `entity.LocalToWorld.scale` for correct UV sampling; entity position centers on the visual center to simplify movement, rotation, physics, and synchronization. World positions are calculated using `entity.LocalToWorld` in `ExecutePaintCommand`. Texture2DArray dimensions are fixed 128x128 due to a GPU constraint, necessitating UV correction (Option A) instead of dynamic per-entity sizes. For sub-128 alpha textures (`architecture_ecs_rendering_option_a_uv_adjustment_for_sub_128_alpha_textures`), pixels are stored in the top-left corner, and UV correction uses `_D2dScale × ARRAY_TEXTURE_SIZE / textureSize`, computed each frame in `SpriteRenderingSystem.PhaseB`. When source texture width < `ARRAY_TEXTURE_SIZE` (128), a row-by-row copy in `TextureArrayManagerSystem.SetSlicePixels`: `for (int row = 0; row < clampedH; row++) System.Array.Copy(pixels, row * srcWidth, padded, row * ARRAY_TEXTURE_SIZE, clampedW);` avoids sheared output.

title: DOTween Callbacks & PaperTask Gate Bypass
body: LevelEndScreenView:Close crashes occur through DOTween tween-callback paths (LoadingView.TransitionInCompleted), bypassing the PaperTask/UniTask gate; this structural limitation prevents fixes via the existing PaperTask gate, invalidating previous assumptions about PaperTask resolving all OnGameEnd* crashes. NextFrame, DelayFrame, and Delay overloads in PaperTask lack automated tests, requiring manual iOS verification (task-024) due to PlayMode asmdef limitations preventing task-004 referencing. VoodooSauceWrapper.CompleteInterstitial/Rv calls `PaperTask.WaitUntil(...)` breaking ad-callback guards; raw Action<bool> callbacks in `VoodooSauceWrapper.ShowRv()` bypass gate routing across multiple sites; rewarded video callbacks should be wrapped with `await` and may require dual-signal subscription for raced 'closed' events. Implement awaitable readiness gates (`WaitUntilRegistered<T>`) using `await WaitForGateOpen()` before `UniTask.WaitUntil(predicate, ...)` with guard flags like `_isWaitingForGameplayReady = true`. Ensure all gated PaperTask async methods begin with `if (s_state != GateState.Open) await WaitForGateOpen(token);`. Replace `PaperTask.Delay()` with `UniTask.Delay()` to address forty-five files bypassing protection via direct calls to `UniTask.Delay()`, `UniTask.WaitUntil()`, `UniTask.NextFrame()`, and `UniTask.DelayFrame()`; external event callbacks require `ServiceController.IsRegistered<T>()` checks or wrapping with `WaitUntilState`. A static PaperTask gate blocks methods until foregrounded plus approximately 200ms to resolve iOS background/resume races, necessitating phased migration to buffer continuation execution during pause transitions by mirroring the `GameAbandonmentController` pattern.

VoodooSauceWrapper.CompleteInterstitial/Rv calls PaperTask.WaitUntil(...) breaking the ad-callback guard due to missing PaperTask infrastructure; raw Action<bool> callbacks in VoodooSauceWrapper.ShowRv() bypass gate routing affecting multiple sites. Rewarded video callbacks can be wrapped with `await` using the existing state machine (Closed/Settling/Open) and may require dual-signal subscription for raced 'closed' events. Implement awaitable readiness gates (`WaitUntilRegistered<T>`) at action triggers using `await WaitForGateOpen()` before `UniTask.WaitUntil(predicate, ...)` with guard flags like `_isWaitingForGameplayReady = true`. Ensure all gated async methods in PaperTask begin with `if (s_state != GateState.Open) await WaitForGateOpen(token);`. title: Turret Projectile Distribution, BeamSlotState Alignment, and System Architecture
body: BeamSlotState buffer index-alignment to WeaponSlotBaked supports future N-weapon turrets; currently single-weapon turrets with a single buffer entry (index 0). When Volume > 1 and Spread is nonzero, turret projectiles distribute evenly across a [-Spread, +Spread] angle arc centered on AimAngle, computed branchlessly using `math.select`. The TurretTargetingSystem validates target distance per turret using `LocalTransform.Position` and utilizes `ProjectileSpawnRequest (Position, Direction, Speed, Damage, HitRadius, Lifetime, Owner, VisualPrefab)` stored in a Persistent `NativeList<ProjectileSpawnRequest>` of size 512 maintained by the TurretFiringSystem. Architecture flows Ship→TurretSlots→WeaponSlots→ProjectileSlots, populated by `WeaponDefinition`, `ProjectileDefinition`, and `WeaponModDefinition` Scriptable Objects into `WeaponSlotBaked` dynamic buffers. title: AutoCreateSO Exclusion & Binder Consolidation
body: During FEAT-009 Part 1, ShipScaleBinder and ShipStatsBinder were excluded from [AutoCreateSO] because ShipScaleBinder's SOAP FloatVariable reference is handled by ScriptableBasePropertyDrawer, and ShipStatsBinder lacks serialized SO fields; [AutoCreateSO] supports only types deriving from ScriptableBase, while the SOAP library uses ScriptableBasePropertyDrawer + SoapEditorUtils.CreateScriptableObject. An audit of 12 binder MonoBehaviours revealed four shapes: SOAP change-driven ECS singleton push (A), Start-time singleton push (B), static-accessor-only (C) with no ECS, and per-entity every-frame writer (D); consolidation proposals were rejected due to contradicting CLAUDE.md’s “minimal abstraction” rule. Shape C binders (EconomyRewardConfigBinder, RarityTierConfigBinder, AudioLodConfigBinder) are candidates for consolidation under a shared `abstract class StaticConfigBinder<TSO>` base class, deferred to `/tdd` pending resolution of an Awake vs Start execution order risk (AudioLodConfigBinder uses Awake while the others use Start; see BP-monobehaviours-022). The current binder count is 13, projected to reach 20+, creating tight coupling and dependency sprawl, as detailed in RCP-dots-ecs-061 regarding the SO+Binder singleton-push pattern.

When a workspace event triggers a rebuild of a CustomEditor (`RCP-editor/a-customeditor-needs-to-rebuild-its-entire`), it subscribes to an external event within `CreateInspectorGUI` and uses `EditorApplication.delayCall` with a null-panel guard before clearing and rebuilding the root VisualElement; this pattern is also used for UIToolkit PropertyDrawers, unsubscribing via `DetachFromPanelEvent`. The `OnEnable` method fires prior to editor state restoration.

title: Service Resolution Patterns and Atomic Retrieval
body: Implement service resolution changes in shared base classes (ServiceController, AbstractChildServiceController) for existing/future .Get<T>() callers. Generic methods returning null for reference types use `where T : class` plus `service = null;` to align with `[CanBeNull]` in `CachedService<T>`. Service resolution uses direct casts for Services, provider.Get() for ServiceProvider bindings (returning null if a UnityEngine.Object is destroyed without Unregister), and `TryGet<T>`/`CachedService<T>.IsValid` use `is UnityEngine.Object` for runtime type dispatch; AGENTS.md prohibits the null-conditional operator (`?.`) on `UnityEngine.Object` subtypes, requiring explicit checks like `if (x != null)`. Refactoring `ServiceController.Get<T>()` and `AbstractChildServiceController.IsRegistered<T>()` requires verifying concrete-typed null checks to prevent `MissingReferenceException`s from destroyed MonoBehaviours; generic/interface comparisons bypass Unity's fake-null check. `AbstractChildServiceController.TryGet<T>` centralizes the fake-null guard (`is UnityEngine.Object`) for non-null returns and `ServiceController.TryGet<T>(out T)` provides atomic single-dictionary lookup, replacing `IsRegistered<T>()` + `Get<T>()` to eliminate TOCTOU race conditions. Direct calls to `ServiceController.Get<T>()` unconditionally log exceptions on miss; use `IsRegistered<T>()` or `TryGet<T>()` as pre-checks. `ServiceController.cs` avoids `using System;` to prevent conflicts with Paper2.ServiceLocator.Interfaces.IServiceProvider.

title: ECS/DOTS Migration & Component Flag Strategy
body: During DOTS transition refactorings, retain component flags (e.g., ShipBuilt → ShipInitializedFlag) during the migration window for incremental test updates and to prevent system breakage; remove the old flag after validation. When migrating from Entities.ForEach to SystemAPI.Query, third-party plugins may require modification while maintaining dependency stability; cleanup involves removing unused CommandBuffer (ECB) fields and unnecessary imports like Unity.Mathematics, safely deleting dead ECS code by grepping the Assets tree for type names and compile-checking for dangling UpdateBefore/After system references. ApplyChanges() should only be called when structural changes occur to prevent redundant GPU flushes, except in AlphaInitializationSystem; collect affected entities into NativeList during SystemAPI.Query migrations, applying structural changes after the iterator closes to avoid races. Retain `Dependency.Complete()` in PaintCommandBufferSystem (line 200) until profiling confirms it's a bottleneck due to raw pointer access (`masks.Ptr`); defer unmanaged struct migration as a follow-up for P7 completion. Eliminate main-thread component access by moving them into scheduled IJobs using `ComponentLookup<T>` with write-access markers, exposing `JobHandle`s as public `OutgoingDependency` properties, combining them via `JobHandle.CombineDependencies(Dependency, systemA.OutgoingDependency)`, marking `ComponentLookup` as [ReadOnly] to enable reader concurrency and reduce serialization, and utilizing RequireForUpdate with dirtyCellQuery for zero-cost frames while profiling ApplyAllEntityStampsJob (line 307). Implement VisualGameObjectCleanup via ICleanupComponentData because Unity Physics ECS doesn't auto-destroy linked GameObjects; gate one-shot systems by calling SetComponentEnabled<T>(entity, false) at the end of OnUpdate and migrate managed class fields in components to blittable structs using `UnsafeList<T>`.

originals.title: Dual-write component flag migration strategy
originals.body: When refactoring component flags during DOTS transition (e.g., ShipBuilt → ShipInitializedFlag), retain both flags during the migration window. Allows downstream test updates to proceed incrementally without system breakage, then remove old flag after validation.
